## Summary
- Adds `shippedSince`, a sibling of the existing `mergedSince` (left untouched — no regression), that UNIONS ledger-merged runs with GitHub-derived merged `Remudero-Task`-trailered PRs. A run that ended some other terminal verdict (e.g. `blocked_review`) but whose task has a merged trailered PR on GitHub is now credited, annotated `gate-side merge; run ended <verdict>` — the gap `mergedSince` alone can't see.

- `buildGather` gains an optional `github` gateway; omitted, `shipped` degrades to the ledger-only list (no ownership check, no unverified annotation) so existing callers are unaffected. `renderGather` adds a SHIPPED section + a Discrepancies section, additive to the existing "Merged since marker" heading (kept byte-identical so `run-task.ts`'s `retroPrompt` reference to it stays valid).

body:
## Scoping decision

Issue #1942 left the actionable shape open with three options: a watchlist-style note, feeding into `interview-prep` for a future round, or a structured field on `interview-redflag`'s existing output. I went with **option 3** (structured field/section on `interview-redflag`'s output) after reading `modes/interview-redflag.md` (#1233) in full.

Reasoning:
- `interview-redflag` already ingests interview transcripts — the only place this signal (interviewer asking about something off-JD) is observable from.
- It's already the established pattern for "something surfaced during an interview that's worth flagging," matching #1854/PR #1856's precedent (blacklist suggestion added to this same mode's existing signal breakdown).
- A watchlist-style file or a hook into `interview-prep.md` would be a second output path for the same underlying observation this mode already owns, and would require touching or creating additional user-layer surface for a signal that's really a *variant* of "what did the interviewer's behavior reveal about this company" — which is squarely `interview-redflag`'s job.

## What changed

`modes/interview-redflag.md`:

- New input: the original JD text (user-provided — same "paste it or point at `local:jds/{file}`" pattern used by `jd-skill-gap.mjs`). Optional; only needed for the new step.
- New **Step 2b — Detect Scope/Compensation Mismatch**: checks, per session, whether (1) the interviewer asked about a skill/topic with zero textual grounding anywhere in the JD, and (2) the JD labels the role entry-level/junior with a correspondingly low pay band. Both conditions must hold in the same session to flag.
- Kept **out of the existing 4-signal red-flag score** (Step 3) on purpose — it's a different category of finding (JD-completeness / pay fairness, discovered only *after* the interview) from the four interviewer-conduct signals, which are about how the interviewer behaved and are discoverable pre-decision. Mixing it into the 0–8 scale would distort both.
- New output section in Step 5, and a summary line in Step 6, when the signal fires.
- Output language is descriptive/corroborating, matching the mode's existing non-alarmist tone — not accusatory.
- Explicitly notes a single instance is a data point, not a pattern, and points at the sibling coffee-chat cross-reference feature (**#1940 / PR #1941**, not yet merged) as the corroboration path when the user has an independent source for the same company.
- Added a line to the Scope/Non-Goals section clarifying this is descriptive/retrospective (can't protect the candidate in the round that produced it) and isn't auto-fed into any future prep file — same advisory-only posture as the rest of the mode.

No new script — this whole feature family (#1233, #1854/#1856) has been prompt-instruction-only, and a fifth transcript-classification dimension didn't need to break that pattern.

## Test plan

- [x] `node test-all.mjs --quick` — 1739 passed, 0 failed (1 pre-existing CRLF warning unrelated to this change)
- [x] Only `modes/interview-redflag.md` touched — no `data/`, `cv.md`, `config/profile.yml`, or other user-layer files modified

Closes #1942

author: karl5026ray
body:
## Why
Guards the mobile FloatingPlayer against the regression that landed in production earlier today (PR #103 / commit `cac0a04c`). If any of the three fixes there is reverted, these tests fail immediately.

## What
- New minimal Playwright setup: `playwright.config.ts` + one spec file at `e2e/floating-player.spec.ts`.
- Single mobile-chromium project pinned to iPhone 13 (390×844) — the exact viewport where the bug was reported.
- Three focused assertions:
  1. **Expanding near the right edge does NOT pop to the left.** Clears saved position, taps the bubble, asserts the expanded panel hugs an edge cleanly.
  2. **Expanded panel z-index sits above the mobile tab bar.** Walks up from the tab-bar Home link to its fixed ancestor and compares.
  3. **Tapping the X collapses back to a bubble.** Guards against the tab bar intercepting the close click.

## Key implementation notes
- `FloatingPlayer` uses React `onPointerDown/Move/Up` listeners. Playwright's `.tap()` fires touch events and `.click()` fires mouse events — neither produces PointerEvents. The tests synthesise real `PointerEvent`s via `el.dispatchEvent`, which is what a real finger produces on mobile Safari/Chrome.
- Forced `browserName: 'chromium'` on the iPhone descriptor to avoid pulling in the WebKit binary just for a viewport preset.
- Config accepts `BASE_URL` so the same suite can run against a Vercel preview:
  ```
  BASE_URL=https://<preview>.vercel.app npm run test:e2e
  ```
  Without it, `webServer` boots `next dev` locally.
- Retries: 2 local, 3 CI. The /music catalog is `force-dynamic` and can be slow on cold serverless starts; tests are deterministic once the page renders.

## Verified against production
Ran the full suite against `https://melorimusic.org` — all 3 tests pass. Latest run below:
```
✓ Mobile FloatingPlayer (390x844) › expanding near the right edge does NOT pop to the left
✓ Mobile FloatingPlayer (390x844) › expanded panel sits above the mobile tab bar
✓ Mobile FloatingPlayer (390x844) › tapping the X collapses the panel back to a bubble
3 passed
```

## How to run
```bash
npm install
npm run test:e2e:install      # one-time: downloads Chromium
npm run test:e2e              # runs against local dev server
BASE_URL=https://melorimusic.org npm run test:e2e   # runs against production/preview
```

## Files
- `.gitignore` (+6) — Playwright output dirs
- `e2e/floating-player.spec.ts` (new, 187 lines)
- `package.json` (+3 scripts, +1 devDep)
- `playwright.config.ts` (new, 54 lines)
- `package-lock.json` (+64) — Playwright deps

author: rbeezley
body:
Plans [MYK9-16](https://linear.app/myk9-platform/issue/MYK9-16/define-reusable-interaction-state-components). Planning only — no code changes. Implementation follows as 5 separate PRs.

## Why

`packages/ui` `Button` has no `loading` prop and `Card` has no `selected` state, so callers hand-roll around the gap: **175** `animate-spin` across **129** files, **279** focus rings across **127** files in **seven** spellings, **370** raw `red-NNN` across **135** files.

Not cosmetic: **~12 destructive dialogs render a confirm button with no `disabled` and no pending feedback — they are double-submittable deletes**, including `DeletePersonDialog`, `DeleteClassDialog`, `DeleteEntryDialog`.

## Two premises the audits overturned

Worth reviewers' attention, because both would have shipped as bugs:

1. **`enhanced-dialog.tsx` is not dead code.** Its "1 importer" is the barrel `components/ui/dialog/index.ts`, which aliases `EnhancedDialogContent as DialogContent` — **~88 files render it unknowingly**. It is a dark-mode theming shim, never a pending-state abstraction. Deleting it would repoint the barrel at `dialog.tsx`'s `bg-background` and turn every dialog **white → ivory** in light mode. Plan folds its classes down instead: zero pixel change.

2. **`BaseEntityDialog` declares `submitDisabled` and `maxWidth` and never destructures them.** They are accepted and silently dropped, and `DeleteConfirmationDialog` is a live caller — so a dialog passing `submitDisabled` today **is not disabled**. Plausibly a *cause* of the double-submit class, not an adjacent bug.

Also: `DialogFooterButtons` infers destructive styling by string-matching the label, so "Delete forever" works by luck while "Remove" and "Discard" silently render `default`.

## Scoped to consume, not redo

Three live specs own adjacent ground; this sits inside them:

| Spec | Owns | This change |
|---|---|---|
| `contrast-token-system` | WCAG AA, dark mode, `--destructive`/`--ring` | New state tokens extend its existing matrix test |
| `motion-language` | duration/easing, reduced-motion, CSS-only in shared pkgs | Adds the **missing loading category rule** (its Purpose names loading; no rule existed) |
| `shell-interaction-integrity` | 44×44px chrome minimum | Consumes, does not restate |

## Notable decisions

- **Fan-out over opt-in.** `FormDialog` and `enhanced-dialog` landed in the *same commit*: the opt-in one has **0 callers** to this day, the barrel-aliased one has **~88**. So `loading` ships *with* its 34 call sites converted — a prop with 2 converted sites is FormDialog with better intentions.
- **`loading` stays opt-in at the call site**, so INTENT's "no spinners between entries" and "sync is background and silent" hold *by construction* rather than by reviewer vigilance.
- **BREAKING (visual):** canonical focus ring `ring-2 ring-ring ring-offset-2` changes every button's ring. `Button`'s current `ring-primary/30 ring-offset-1` is the outlier and bypasses the contrast-verified token.

## Migration

5 sequential PRs, each independently revertable. PR 1 carries the correctness fix and ships first if anything slips. No DB, edge function, or deploy impact; no replication or offline path touched.

author: milesgray
body:
## Summary
Optimizes database queries on the remote TimescaleDB VM for both price and order book data loaders, resolving timeouts and network/parsing latency.

## Changes
- **Symbol Caching**: Cached SkipScan resolution in `postgres.py` to eliminate 9-second startup query delays.
- **Index Scan Optimization**: Refactored `book.py` and `price.py` to dynamically rewrite queries to use exact matching (`symbol = $1`) when single symbols are resolved. This allows Postgres to use Index Scan Backward/Forward and bypasses expensive Sort operations, yielding a 4x speedup.
- **Database downsampling**: Integrated database-side downsampling using TimescaleDB `time_bucket` and `last` aggregates, automatically skipped for intervals <= 1s to prevent unnecessary aggregation overhead.

## Testing
- [x] All 29 local tests pass (`uv run pytest`)
- [x] Verified query speedups and correctness via `test_db.py`
- [x] Verified complete pressure service examples (`example_data_loading.py`) execute successfully.

body:
A queued message stayed in the queue (chip visible) for the entire time its dispatched turn was running — `q.shift()` only ran after the turn completed. A message being actively answered isn't 'queued'. Now it's removed from the queue the moment dispatch starts; on a dispatch failure it's `unshift`ed back to the head so the pause/Resume retry path still works.

## Manual testing done
Isolated hub: enqueued 3 messages to an idle session — the queue immediately showed 2 pending (the running one removed on start), drained to 0 as each was picked up, and the session history confirmed all three still ran in order (ACK-1/2/3). No message dropped.

author: ganngann
body:
🚨 **Severity:** HIGH

💡 **Vulnerability:** The route performing a massive vector synchronization (`/vector-sync`) was accessible via a `GET` request.

🎯 **Impact:** This broke RESTful principles and introduced a Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) vulnerability. An attacker could trick an authenticated user into clicking a malicious link, inadvertently triggering a heavy server-side recalculation, potentially leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) or unexpected data states.

🔧 **Fix:** Replaced `Route::match(['get', 'post'])` with `Route::post()` to enforce Laravel's built-in CSRF validation middleware. Added an explanatory security comment.

✅ **Verification:** Verified that tests pass and the route correctly uses only `POST` via `php artisan route:list`.

author: danielleag30
body:
## Summary

Resumes DAN-118/119/120 eval-case authoring. Independently re-verifies the 57 previously-blocked temporal/adversarial/zoning eval cases against the **live** corpus now that EnCode Chapter 112.2 zoning ingestion (#92) and real Municode historical supplements (#91) are merged, using the same standard as #90: real `chunk_id`s, real quoted content, no fabrication.

**Net result: 89 → 116 of 185 total eval cases authored.** 27 new cases resolve with real data; 30 do not and are reported below rather than forced.

## What's newly authored (27 cases, all independently verified)

- **1 `temporal-correctness` case** (new `eval/cases/temporal-correctness.json`): Chapter 9.1 → 9.2 Cable Television repeal/replacement — confirmed genuinely different old vs. current text (not a duplicate), real dates (2019-09-11 repeal window, Jan 1 2020 effective).
- **4 `adversarial-near-miss` cases** (new `eval/cases/adversarial-near-miss.json`): Ch9.1 franchise-fee trap (real substantive change — current fee is now conditional on state law, not a flat mandatory 5%), Ch9 pre-2020 framing trap, and two repealed-chapter traps (Ch28 massage, Ch29 real estate salesmen).
- **12 numeric zoning cases** (appended to `citation-numeric.json`) from the live `encode_zoning` corpus (742 rows): R-1/R-2/R-3 lot area/width/setback/height, C-2 FAR, PDH open space, retail parking ratio, accessory living unit size/lot-size, sign height/area. Corrects two unverified guesses from the 2026-06-25 domain-knowledge doc (R-1 min lot area was assumed ~43,560 sq ft; real is 36,000) and its ADU/"home occupation" terminology (Fairfax's ordinance actually uses "Accessory Living Unit" and "Home-Based Business").
- **10 textual zoning cases** (appended to `citation-historical.json`): 5 of 6 requested definitions, all 3 procedural cases (BZA appeal, rezoning application, variance), both policy cases (home-based-business prohibitions, outdoor storage via the Portable Storage Container standard).

Every new `chunk_id` was re-verified to exist in `ordinance_provisions` as of this PR (23 unique IDs checked against the live table).

## What's still unresolvable — reported, not fabricated

**14 of 15 `temporal-correctness` cases and 11 of 15 `adversarial-near-miss` cases.** The headline finding: the "182 real `is_current=false` rows" from #91 are mostly **not** genuine amendment history once you look past the Cable TV chapter:
- 46 rows are byte-identical duplicates of current text — the same pipeline-artifact bug from before #91 (dated 2026-06-25→2026-07-06), confirmed via direct content/`content_hash` comparison across 5+ chapters (Ch84.1, Ch116, Ch30, Appendix Q, Appendix A).
- 18 rows (Chapter 4, Utility Tax) have **real** 2019 dates but **byte-identical content** to the current row — a genuine recodification event with zero substantive text change, so there's no real "before vs. after" to test.
- Chapters 8 and 109 are still entirely absent from the corpus.
- Zoning has **zero** historical (`is_current=false`) rows at all — only current EnCode text — so none of the 3 zoning-temporal or 4 zoning-adversarial cases have a real old-version chunk to cite.

**1 of 13 zoning numeric cases** (max impervious surface coverage %): no such metric exists anywhere in the ingested Zoning Ordinance. Fairfax regulates density via lot coverage / FAR / open space, not a residential impervious-surface cap — confirmed via exhaustive keyword search.

**1 of 11 zoning textual cases** ("special exception" definition): no standalone glossary definition exists in Article 9; the term is used throughout Article 8 procedural sections but never locally defined.

## Out of scope

61 remaining numeric/textual cases and all `retrieval` / `synthesis` / `out_of_corpus` cases (35 cases, never authored in the first place) are outside this task — this PR covers exactly the 57 cases that were previously blocked by missing zoning/historical data.

## Test plan

- [x] All 4 touched/new JSON files parse as valid JSON
- [x] No duplicate `id` values within or across files
- [x] Every new `chunk_id` re-verified present in live `ordinance_provisions` via direct SQL query
- [ ] Cross-vendor review (dispatched separately per usual lifecycle)

body:
## Root cause of the all-awaiting cards (ONE commit)

Score + verdicts are INTACT (lean has ipo_score L106, compute_verdicts L118 — the Ltd. card shows 85/WATCH). Three stacked breaks in the enrichment path; this PR fixes the two code ones:

### 1. route.ts L81 — the ipo_intelligence join normalizer kept "Ltd/Limited"
`sbifundsmanagementltd ≠ sbifundsmanagementlimited`, so verdict-bearing consolidated rows (Chittorgarh "Ltd." form) joined UNENRICHED intelligence rows after NSE discovery created "Limited"-form rows → anchors/OFS/band all null on the card. The RHP join two lines above ALREADY strips ltd|limited — the ii join didn't. Now both strip `ltd|limited|pvt|private`.

### 2. ipomatrix_ingest.py — same disease in `norm()`, worse consequence
Upcoming IPOs have no nse_symbol yet → matcher falls to name-norm → Ltd/Limited mismatch → `if not cid: continue` → **silently skipped**. That's why the 398 historical rows (symbols exist) enriched fine but every UPCOMING card is empty. Unit-tested: SBI/Alpine/Caliber Ltd↔Limited forms now match.

### 3. NOT in this PR — the 13 duplicate pairs
Run the pending `dedup_merge.sql` (backend chat's) — it's the durable identity fix; #155 prevents new pairs.

### After merge, in order
1. Merge → **Admin → Sync**
2. Run: `ipomatrix_ingest.py --only-null --apply` (Admin job or VM) — the skipped upcoming IPOs enrich now that the matcher works
3. `build_ipo_consolidated_v2.py` (or the nightly) → cards populate
4. `dedup_merge.sql` when ready → kills the ghost "Limited" cards

Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack/tree/0.15.0) (oldest at bottom):
* __->__ #190133
* #190138
* #190084

Collective, CUDA graph, point-to-point, and process-group contracts were split between the Gloo, NCCL, and NCCL2 test files, making equivalent backend coverage difficult to see and reuse. Add a shared multiprocess harness with capability-driven backend configuration and focused domain suites that instantiate the same contracts for every supported backend.

The collective suite covers zero and nonzero tensor sizes, all standard native dtypes, FP8 transport on capable hardware, supported complex operations, reduction operators, sync and async APIs, list and single-tensor variants, uneven splits, coalescing, and validation errors. The other suites cover blocking and nonblocking P2P, batched operations and Work lifetime, CUDA graph capture and replay, process-group lifecycle, sequence numbers, futures, and work registration. Keep backend-specific tests only for behavior that cannot share a contract, including NCCL's non-graphable barrier and NCCL2's lazy channels.

author: will-roscoe
body:
## What

`pull` now handles a file that changed on **both** sides since the last sync (edited locally AND changed on the remote), building on #24's direction-aware classification.

**Default (no `--resolve`) is a hard-stop:** pull brings down only files that are absent locally (remote-only / metadata-only), leaves every diverged file untouched, reports it as a conflict, and exits non-zero. A local edit is never silently overwritten — this preserves the previous safe behavior exactly.

**`--resolve` chooses a side** for diverged (both-modified) files, decided at the protonfs level (not proton-drive transfer strategies) so the outcome is identical and testable across backends:

| value | effect |
|-------|--------|
| `remote` | overwrite the local copy with the remote one |
| `local` | keep local untouched (it stays queued for the next push) |
| `both` | fetch the remote copy alongside local under a `.remote` suffix (untracked) for a manual merge |

Files that changed only on the remote (local still in sync) are brought down normally under any `--resolve`. A conflict with no remote copy to reconcile against is always reported, never auto-resolved.

## ⚠️ CLI change (relevant to M4 CLI-freeze)

`pull`'s `--resolve` choices are now **`remote|local|both`** (previously the proton-drive transfer-strategy vocabulary `merge|keep-both|replace|skip`, which was never meaningful for pull's three-way case). `push`'s `--resolve` is unchanged. This resolves the issue's open question: `both` is supported (non-destructive, suffixed fetch), and the default is the hard-stop rather than an implicit choice.

## How
- New protonfs-level resolution in `commands/pull.py`; a remote view (walk) is fetched only when `--resolve` is given, so the default path pays no extra cost.
- Tests cover remote/local/both outcomes and the no-resolve conflict report.
- Docs: a "Resolving a divergence on pull" section in `docs/getting-started/syncing.rst`.

Full suite: 247 passed, 4 skipped; ruff clean.

Closes #5

author: dj4oc
body:
## Summary

The oCIS collaboration service's `Collabora` struct (`services/collaboration/pkg/connector/fileinfo/collabora.go`) has historically lagged behind the `Microsoft` and `OnlyOffice` structs in WOPI `CheckFileInfo` coverage. This PR closes that gap across 9 areas:

- **Version** — cache invalidation / stale-document detection
- **LastModifiedTime** — plus a new `X-COOL-WOPI-Timestamp` / `COOLStatusCode` conflict-detection path in `PutFile` (Collabora's mechanism for detecting concurrent edits)
- **ReadOnly** — explicit read-only signal, derived from the WOPI session's view mode (applies to all three targets, since it was previously unset everywhere)
- **SupportsUpdate** — advertises `PutFile`/`PutRelativeFile` support
- **IsAnonymousUser** — correct UX for public-link/guest access
- **URL properties** — `CloseUrl`, `DownloadUrl`, plus wiring the already-computed `HostEditUrl`/`HostViewUrl`/`FileSharingUrl`/`FileVersionUrl` into the Collabora response (`SignoutUrl` field added for spec completeness but intentionally left unpopulated — no OIDC logout endpoint is configured in this service yet, matching Microsoft's/OnlyOffice's pre-existing gap for the same field)
- **Breadcrumb properties** — adds `BreadcrumbBrandName`/`BreadcrumbBrandUrl` (space name/root link, withheld for public-share access to avoid exposing internal resource ids) alongside the existing doc/folder breadcrumbs
- **PostMessage properties** — only `EditModePostMessage` is enabled (gated to the Collabora target), since the web frontend doesn't yet handle `UI_Close`/`UI_Sharing`/`UI_FileVersions`/`Edit_Notification`; the corresponding URL properties above serve as the fallback
- **IsUserLocked / IsAdminUser** — new Collabora-specific properties (feature-locking for secure-view sessions; audit-panel access restricted to the built-in system Admin role, explicitly excluding SpaceAdmin)

Every property flows through the shared `CheckFileInfo` properties map unconditionally unless otherwise noted above. Two of these are worth calling out explicitly, since they change behavior for Microsoft/OnlyOffice too, not just Collabora: `ReadOnly` and `CloseUrl` already have matching `case` handling in `microsoft.go`/`onlyoffice.go` (and `DownloadUrl` in `microsoft.go`), but the shared map never actually populated those keys before, so they silently defaulted to unset/false. Populating them unconditionally means Microsoft and OnlyOffice will now surface a real `ReadOnly: true` for read-only/view-only sessions, and a populated `CloseUrl`/`DownloadUrl` where they previously had none — a broader behavior change than the "Collabora gaps" framing above suggests (flagged in review, thanks @DeepDiver1975). `IsUserLocked`/`IsAdminUser` remain genuinely Collabora-only: no matching `case` exists for them on the other targets, so they're a true no-op there.

- [x] `go vet ./...` clean
- [x] `gofmt -l .` clean
- [x] `go test ./...` green for `services/collaboration` (unit + Ginkgo integration suites, new tests added per property)
- [x] Each change reviewed individually (spec compliance + code quality) before being folded into this PR, plus a final whole-branch pass over the complete diff

author: david-shortman
body:
Closes #561. Part of the Music Together epic #508.

## Problem
Installment families vault a card in MT's separate Square account so `chargeMusicTogetherInstallments` can auto-charge the Week-5 balance. There was **no way for a customer to update that card** if it changed or expired — the scheduled charge just failed (`music-together-installment-failed` email) and resolution was manual.

## What this adds
A customer-facing "update payment method" flow, mirroring the **Craft Club manage-link pattern** but scoped to a **registration** (the card lives on the registration), routed through **MT's** Square account (`MT_SQUARE_KEYS`).

Three Cloud Functions:
- **`requestMusicTogetherManageLink`** _(public, maple-core)_ — emails a single-use, 30-min magic link. Uniform response whether or not the email is enrolled (no enumeration). Picks the most recent confirmed installment registration with a card on file.
- **`startMusicTogetherManageSession`** _(public, maple-core)_ — consumes the token (single-use), issues a 1-hour session token, and returns a customer-safe view (section name + next installment amount/date).
- **`updateMusicTogetherPaymentMethod`** _(public, session-gated, maple-square)_ — vaults a new card on MT's Square account from a fresh Web Payments nonce, repoints `registration.squareCardId` at it, and disables the old card (best-effort).

### Overcharge-safety preserved
The Week-5 charge job reads `squareCardId` / `squareCustomerId` from the registration **at charge time**, so repointing the registration automatically retargets every still-pending scheduled charge to the new card. The Square customer id is unchanged, and no charge that is already `paid`/`charging` is touched.

### Also included
- `MusicTogetherTokenRepository` — hashed (sha256) access + session tokens, raw token only in the emailed URL / widget memory.
- `CardsService.disableCard` — detaches the old card via the Square Cards API.
- `MusicTogetherManageWidget` + `music-together-manage.webflow.tsx` — the manage page (reads `?token=`; without one, shows the email form). `SquareCardForm` rendered **without** `env` — the SDK environment follows the App ID prefix.
- `music-together-manage-link` email template (seeded).
- `MUSIC_TOGETHER_MANAGE_URL` param in `.env.dev` / `.env.prod`.

## UX
The manage page opens from a `?token=` magic link, shows which installment the new card will cover ("your $95.00 charge on September 15, 2026 will use the new card"), takes a new card via the Square Web Payments SDK, and confirms with the new card's last 4.

## Verification
- **Unit** (`vi.mock` Square/repos): 15 cases across the 3 functions + the widget, incl. failure paths — missing nonce, expired/unknown session, pay-in-full (nothing on file), cancelled registration, and best-effort old-card disable failure.
- **Integration** (`./tools/run-integration-tests.sh music-together`, emulator + Square mock): full chain — magic link → session → card replace → old card disabled → the charge job charges the **NEW** card (`source_id` asserted). **All 45 music-together integration tests pass.**
- **Interaction**: `MusicTogetherManageWidget.spec.tsx` drives request-link and token → save-card flows headlessly.
- Firestore index analyzer clean (`email + createdAt` already declared); typecheck + eslint clean; `validate-function-tsconfigs.sh` passes.

Note: `music-together.types.ts` and the api-types barrel are touched additively (parallel MT PRs also edit them).

author: ryan-evans-git
body:
## What

Σ.TW.2 — the measured mode memo. Every join query probes its three execution arms once (untimed): the **native twin** (Σ.TW.1), **forced-mesh** (broadcast off), and **forced-mesh + broadcast joins** (#216's opt-in). The 5 measured trials then run on the argmin. `plan_mode` reports the chosen arm; `EMAT_MODE_MEMO=0` restores Σ.TW.1 exactly.

## Why

Phase 1 (#220) fixed AUTO's execution penalty and made it the fastest mode (55.34s). The remaining ~3.5s gap to the oracle is the **decision bucket** — and the scan-byte threshold is data-proven non-monotonic with mesh benefit (Q02 3.86GB single-wins sits *between* mesh-wins at 1.28GB and 20.4GB). No static signal separates them; a distributed cost model would need reliable post-join cardinalities DataFusion doesn't have. So this PR stops predicting and measures: the 22-query workload repeats, probes are exact, and the broadcast arm's Q10-style regressions dodge automatically because they lose their probe.

## Safety

- **Row-parity guard**: probes compare row counts across arms; any disagreement logs loudly and falls back to the gate's own routing — a fast-but-wrong arm can never win.
- Arms are separate *sessions*, not plan rewrites (the #218/#219 lesson).
- Probes count against the untimed warmup budget (chosen arm: 1 probe + 1 warmup = the protocol's 2 untimed runs).

## Evidence

- 5 new `ModeMemo` unit tests; all local gates green (fmt, clippy `--workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, 81 lib tests).
- SF0.1 smoke (1 in-proc worker): 9 probes / 3 picks / 0 row mismatches; rows identical to the `EMAT_MODE_MEMO=0` control on every query; scan-aggs untouched.

## Expected at SF100 (validation pending — do not merge until it lands)

Phase-1 AUTO = 55.34s. The memo should recover the ~3.5s decision bucket *and* capture the broadcast wins on mesh-kept queries (mesh 61.9→51.0s measured in the #216 A/B) → target **~mid-40s**, ≈ the three-mode oracle (~44.4s). author: posthog-local-dev[bot]
body:
## Problem

One unresponsive-sandbox agent-server launch was spamming error tracking with three separate issues instead of one quiet, retryable timeout. All three fingerprints come from a single failure captured at three levels of one exception chain, from the same sandbox during one launch.

When the agent-server binds its port but never answers `/health`, the in-sandbox `curl` poll loop in `wait_for_health_check` outlasts the `execute` subprocess timeout, so `execute` raises `SandboxTimeoutError` instead of the health check returning `False`. That escaping timeout:

1. gets captured on construction (fingerprint #1), skipping the `capture=False` suppression the sibling health-check-fail branches already have,
2. bubbles up and is re-wrapped as a capturing `SandboxExecutionError` (fingerprint #2), and
3. on the way out, the log-tail helper's own `execute("tail … /tmp/agent-server.log")` times out against the still-dead daemon, minting a third fingerprint (#3).

The underlying launch failure is transient and already retried by Temporal, so the real cost is error-tracking noise and triage time for the team building PostHog Code / tasks.

## Changes

Treat a transient execution timeout on the launch path as non-capturing, mirroring the `capture=False` precedent already sitting a few lines away.

- Added a `capture_timeout` flag to the sandbox `execute()` implementations (Docker and Modal). When `False`, a timeout neither calls `capture_exception` nor constructs a capturing `SandboxTimeoutError`.
- `wait_for_health_check` now calls `execute` with `capture_timeout=False` and swallows a `SandboxTimeoutError` by returning `False`, just like its other failure branches. The caller then raises its existing quiet, non-capturing "failed to start" error, which Temporal retries.
- The health-check log-tail reads (`_emit_agentsh_log_tail`, `_emit_agent_server_log_tail`, and the in-sandbox `cat` log reads on the failure path) pass `capture_timeout=False` so a timeout against the dead daemon doesn't mint its own issue.

Net effect: one unresponsive-sandbox launch produces at most one quiet, retryable log line instead of three error-tracking issues.

## How did you test this code?

Added one unit test, `test_wait_for_health_check_swallows_execute_timeout_without_capturing`, at the cheapest rung (pure function). It catches the regression where a health-check `execute` timeout stops being suppressed: if the `except SandboxTimeoutError` swallow or the `capture_timeout=False` kwarg is removed, the timeout escapes and gets captured. No existing test exercised the timeout-during-health-check path — the sibling tests mock the health check to return `False` directly.

I (Claude) could not run the Python suite in this environment: the flox venv (Python 3.13) is unavailable here and only Python 3.12 is installed, so `hogli test` / pytest can't start. I did syntax-check all changed files with `py_compile` and ran `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` (all pass). A reviewer or CI should run `hogli test products/tasks/backend/logic/services/tests/test_docker_sandbox.py`.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Fully autonomous

Authored by Claude (via PostHog Code) from an inbox report about triplicated error-tracking issues on the tasks agent-server launch path. I traced the three fingerprints to one exception chain (`start_agent_server` → sandbox health-check `execute` timeout → log-tail `execute` timeout), found the existing `capture=False` precedent in the sibling failure branches, and extended the same treatment to the timeout path via a `capture_timeout` flag threaded through `execute()`.

Invoked the `/writing-tests` skill before adding the test and applied its value gate (named the specific regression the test catches; kept it at the pure-function rung rather than standing up a sandbox).

body: ## Summary Adds pattern-based formatting to `@ailuracode/alpine-timer` so consumers can choose display styles like `mm:ss`, `hh:mm`, `hh:mm:ss`, and sub-second patterns. ## Format API - **`format(pattern, ms)`** — format milliseconds directly (`format("mm:ss", 10_000)` → `"00:10"`) - **`format(pattern, options)`** — returns a `TimerFormatter` for timer options - **`formatPattern(pattern, ms)`** — low-level pattern renderer - **`createFormat(pattern, options)`** — explicit formatter factory - **`timer.format(pattern, options?)`** — format current timer state on demand ### Supported tokens | Token | Meaning | Example | |-------|---------|---------| | `hh` | Hours (padded) | `01` | | `h` | Hours | `1` | | `mm` | Minutes (padded) | `05` | | `m` | Minutes | `5` | | `ss` | Seconds (padded) | `09` | | `s` | Seconds | `9` | | `SSS` / `mmm` | Milliseconds (padded) | `432` | When a pattern includes `hh`, `mm` represents minutes within the hour. Without `hh`, `mm` is total minutes. ### Timer options ```ts $timer.countdown({ duration: 60_000, formatPattern: "mm:ss", }); $timer.stopwatch({ formatPattern: "mm:ss.SSS", lapFormatPattern: "mm:ss.SSS", }); ``` ## Demo Added `hh:mm` countdown example in `TimerDemo.astro`. ## Tests - 9 new unit tests in `packages/timer/test/format.test.ts` - All 29 timer package tests passing

author: farahbrunache
body:
## What and why

The GDP dashboard's "All Countries" panel counted only members who have a country recorded, so its rows summed to fewer than the dashboard hero's total-member count — with no explanation of the gap (for example, countries summing to 68 while the hero shows 74). This makes the panel and the hero look like they disagree.

This adds a single **"Location not set"** row so the panel reconciles exactly to the same member roster the hero shows.

## How

- `GET /api/gdp/countries` now also returns:
  - `totalMembers` — the full active-Directory roster (`countActiveDirectoryProfiles`, the same count the hero shows), and
  - `unspecified` — that roster minus the sum of the located per-country counts, i.e. active members with **no** country recorded (floored at 0; falls back to the located sum if the roster read fails, which simply omits the bucket).
- The web shell (`gdp-shell.tsx`) appends one synthetic **"Location not set"** row when `unspecified > 0`, and computes every share as a percentage of `totalMembers`. Country rows plus the bucket now sum exactly to the hero's member total.
- The bucket is styled apart in `gdp-dashboard.tsx` (muted, italic, caption "no country recorded") and is **excluded** from the hero's "N countries" line — it is not a country — via a new `unspecified` flag on `GdpCountry` (`gdp-shared.ts`).

Country is optional on the server (`validateProfileInput` does not require it), so seeded/legacy profiles can legitimately have none. This surfaces that gap honestly instead of hiding it.

## Scope

- **Web only.** The Android GDP surface already omits the country panel by design (unchanged).
- Query/UI-only: no schema, route-signature, or contract change (the route already reads `directory_profiles`).
- Updated the GDP feature inventory (route description + change log) and the GDP manual test script (GDP-3) to match.

## Checks

Local: web typecheck, web lint (`--max-warnings=0`), full-workspace typecheck (pre-commit), web `build:ci`, EOF format, inventory-drift, and test-script-drift all pass.

Parity Status: web + mobile-responsive + android complete

author: lazyants
body:
Fixes #198.

## Problem
W5 mass-translate dispatched codex translate/review via `agent(agentType:'codex:codex-rescue')` fire-and-forget, then polled `draft_ready.py`/`review_ready.py`. The forwarder backgrounds the codex `task`, returns a stub, and **sometimes never launches codex** — so no `segments/<seg>.draft.json` appears, every segment ends `translate-timeout`, and the review→fix loop is unreachable (forcing an ad-hoc direct-codex fallback).

## Fix
A shipped stdlib driver **`codex_job.py`** owns the codex launch deterministically:
- `codex-companion task --background --write --effort high` → poll `status` to a terminal state → validate the isolated attempt via the gate scripts' new **`--candidate-file`** mode → **atomic `os.replace`** to the canonical path (validate-before-promote).
- A plain-Claude drive agent launches the driver **detached** (`nohup`) and returns `DISPATCHED <seg> <DISP>`.
- The Workflow's on-disk content re-validation — `draft_ready.py` + `validate_draft.py` (translate) / `review_ready.py` (review) on the **current canonical** — remains the **sole acceptance authority** (never trusts a driver-written flag or an agent return).
- A template **SEGS uniqueness guard** enforces one dispatch per segment.
- The glossary-pass codex dispatch is **unchanged**.

`resolve_codex_companion.py` resolves the codex-companion path (plugin-anchored, never copied to durable_root). Version **1.4.6 → 1.4.7**.

## Review trail
- **Plan:** codex plan-review, **10 rounds** to explicitly clean (the design converged by deleting an impossible-guarantee snapshot and honestly scoping the disobedient-writer residual to the supported single-orchestrator model).
- **Build:** 5-lane disjoint team (driver / gate-scripts / template / durable+SKILL / docs+enumerations); canonical-path enumerations recomputed to **12 draft / 10 review**; `PLUGIN_BUNDLE_MEMBERS` → 10 scripts + 2 templates.
- **Suite:** `python3 -m pytest` → **1992 passed, 1 skipped, 1 xfailed**.
- **Reviewers:** code-simplifier (applied) · codex-rescue **CODE CLEAN** · security-review **no HIGH/MEDIUM** (heredoc not injectable — `language.code` = `^[a-z]{2}$`, verse-policy enum, validated seg; COMPANION single-quoted vs `path_is_safe`; all `subprocess.run` argv-list `shell=False`).

## Known low-severity residuals (documented, not blocking)
1. `codex_job.py` `_write_joblog` could leak an orphaned `.tmp` scratch file on an ENOSPC mid-write (self-limiting, unique `inv`, disk-hygiene only).
2. A completed codex attempt is **discarded** (not adopted) if the finalize budget is exhausted at the exact moment status flips — **fails safe** (never promotes unvalidated content), by design.
3. **Defense-in-depth:** the drive-command heredoc is safe today via schema enforcement, but has no explicit `/^LT_CODEX_TASK_EOF$/m` delimiter-guard at the sink — worth a future hardening throw if a free-form profile field is ever routed into a prompt builder.

author: coatless
body:
## What

Adds a standard integrity/completeness core to `manifest.json`, describing the published summary DB (`conda-forge-downloads-summary.db`), the asset the downstream `r-observatory/data` merge consumes. New TOP-LEVEL manifest fields:

- `db_filename` - basename of the summary DB
- `db_bytes` - byte size of the finalized file
- `db_sha256` - lowercase hex sha256 of the exact file bytes
- `tables` - object mapping every user table to its row count
- `complete` - `true`

All pre-existing fields (`tag`, `generated_at`, `last_checked`, `last_changed`, `source_kind`, `changed_shards`, `shards`, `summary`) are preserved.

## How

- `scripts/helpers.R`: adds `file_sha256()` (availability-ordered digest/openssl/sha256sum/shasum backend, no new declared dependency) and `summary_integrity_core()` (enumerates user tables + row counts from the finalized file); `write_manifest()` gains an optional `core = NULL` argument merged in as top-level keys via `obj <- c(obj, core)`.
- `scripts/update.R`: computes the core from `summary_path` after `export_summary_shard()` finalizes it, in both the cold bootstrap and incremental republish paths, and passes `core =` to `write_manifest()`. The frozen-source heartbeat path writes no fresh summary and carries the prior manifest's core forward unchanged.

## Why `complete = true`

The summary is a full per-run snapshot. Its widest window (365d) sits inside the always-loaded `RECENT_WINDOW` (400 days), and `merge_prior_summary()` carries the full package roster and first/last dates forward, so every run publishes a complete summary table (never a partial delta). The cold bootstrap loads full history from `HISTORY_START`, so it is complete as well.

## Verification

- Full test suite green (`Rscript tests/testthat.R`); adds `tests/testthat/test-manifest.R` with the three integrity assertions (fields present, sha256 matches an independent `digest`, `write_manifest` merges the core as top-level fields), each building its own tiny summary DB via the pipeline's own `export_summary_shard`.
- Local end-to-end check: built a real `conda-forge-downloads-summary.db`, ran the manifest path, parsed the JSON, and cross-checked every field: `db_bytes` == `stat`, `db_sha256` == both `shasum -a 256` and `digest`, `tables` == direct `count(*)`.

The workflow already uploads `manifest.json` unconditionally and the summary shard is written before the manifest, so no workflow change is required.

author: wcjord
body:
## Summary

A batch of clear, unit-tested logic/parsing fixes.

- **Orchestrator suggestion chip on the bot's opener — closes #7703.** `OrchestratorController.suggestionToShow`'s single-human branch only prompted when the current user sent the latest human message, so the bot's turn-0 opener produced no chip (`latestHumanMessageSenderId` is null before the human's first message). Under v2 the guards above already ensure a fresh own-role bucket exists and the sender's own role is omitted from outputs, so a surviving own-role bucket means it's the human's turn — prompt unconditionally in the single-human case. Multi-human is unchanged.

- **Ban-specific course-code join error — closes #7592.** `/knock_with_code` now returns `403 ORG.PANGEA.BANNED_FROM_ROOM` when a code is valid but the user is banned from every matched room. The client threw the raw response on any non-200 and dropped unknown keys, so a banned user saw the generic "code not found." Now `knockSpace` parses the body and throws a typed `BannedFromRoomException` (else keeps throwing the raw response so 429 handling is unchanged), the join flow maps it to a new `removedFromCourseError` message, and `KnockSpaceResponse` gains a `banned` field.

- **Onboarding CEFR selection reset on role switch — closes #7583.** The CEFR level is a single shared field, so picking one as a teacher and switching to learner left it set: the learner CEFR page showed nothing selected yet Next was enabled. `setUserType` now clears the level on an actual role change (same-role re-tap keeps it), and the view seeds its highlight from the persisted selection so display and the enable guard always agree.

- **Grammar-practice fill-in-the-blank alignment — #7360 (partial).** The cloze offsets index the IGC match's `fullText` (the base `SpanData.errorSpan` uses), but the generator paired them with a separately reconstructed `choreo.stepText(stepIndex-1)`; when the strings differed by a few chars the blank slid into the next word. It now displays and blanks off `igcMatch.fullText`/`igcMatch.errorSpan`. **This fixes the blank placement only** — the issue's secondary note (repeat sentences / 24h cooldown, `ConstructUses.shouldSkipForRecentPractice`) is a separate code path and is left as a follow-up, so #7360 stays open.

author: w1ne
body:
## Goal

Get as close as **fidelity-preserving** simulation allows to **native wall-clock** for C3 OLED labs (silicon = 160 MHz).

## Honest ceiling

| Mode | Host rate | Device-time vs wall (160 MHz silicon) |
|------|-----------|----------------------------------------|
| Busy firmware (no WFI) @ tick 512 | **~47 MIPS** | **~0.29× real-time** (was ~0.09× at 14.6 MIPS) |
| Delay-bound FreeRTOS / idle FF | **~227 device-MIPS** | **~1.4× faster than silicon wall-clock** |

We cannot claim busy-loop wall real-time without faking timers (forbidden). We **can** make delay-bound demos feel native+ via idle FF, and keep climbing busy MIPS honestly.

## Changes
1. **`RECOMMENDED_TICK_INTERVAL` 64 → 512** — OLED framebuffer **byte-identical** to interval 1 at 512 (`oled_lab_framebuffer_is_byte_identical_at_tick_512`).
2. **Deadline-clamped mid-batch arm** — clamp to earliest `pending_schedule` deadline instead of ending every arm (far timers no longer force ~60-insn batches).
3. Walk-deleted write-hook skips + `scheduler_driver_indices` (earlier on this PR).

## Cumulative vs pre-#555
Busy tick-64 era → tick-512: **~14.6 → ~47 MIPS (~3.2×)**.

## Test plan
- [x] FB identity 1≡64 and 1≡512
- [x] walk pinners → max_safe = 512
- [x] C3 bus tick matrix tests
- [ ] CI green

No firmware hacks, no fake millis.

author: leanandmean
body:
<!-- mach12-pr -->
## Summary
- Fixes the "This extension ctx is stale after session replacement or reload" error surfaced from `terminal-indicators`'s `agent_end` handler when a completed command chains to a fresh session (`fresh_session: true`).
- Root cause: `ExtensionRunner.emit()` reuses one ctx across all handlers; a mid-emit `setTimeout(0)` fresh-session dispatch invalidates the runner during an earlier handler's async yield, so later ctx-touching handlers throw.
- Adds a `skipStale(eventType)` guard to `ExtensionRunner`, wired into all ten `emit*` methods, so remaining handlers are skipped once the runner is invalidated mid-emit. A `session_shutdown` emit on an already-stale runner is routed to `emitError` as an ordering violation rather than silently skipped.
- Marked with `// SCRAMJET-DIVERGENCE:` and documented in `UPSTREAM_DIVERGENCE.md`.
- New test suite `extension-runner-stale.test.ts` covers the mid-emit invalidation window, the ordering-violation path, and that normal emits are unaffected.

## Test plan
- [x] `npx vitest run packages/coding-agent/tests/extension-runner-stale.test.ts` passes
- [x] Full `npm run typecheck && npm test` passes
- [x] Manual: run a command whose completion chains to a next step with `fresh_session: true` and confirm no `Extension <builtin> error` output appears; the chain proceeds normally

author: nexushero
body:
## Summary

Makes the Auto-Tracker's "app usage while tracking" split survive a reload / mid-session relaunch — by persisting the session buffer **only on this device**, never to a server. This is a deliberate **privacy / data-protection** choice: app-activity is behaviour-near data and, in a work-time context, sensitive to employee monitoring (Art. 5(1)(c) data minimisation, privacy-by-design, and the § 26 BDSG / § 87 BetrVG "Leistungs-/Verhaltenskontrolle" concern). So it stays where it was observed, and is cleared the moment the session ends.

This deliberately **replaces** an earlier server-backed cross-device design after a data-protection review — no `activity_spans` table, no ingest endpoint, nothing leaving the device.

Refs #41 (REQ-042 — Auto-Tracker; local-only slice)

## Type of change

- [x] `feat` — new feature

## What changed

- `apps/mobile/src/autotracker/activityStore.ts` (+ test) — the same cross-platform seam as `onboardingStore` (localStorage on web, in-memory fallback on native): `load` / `save` / `clear` the session buffer, plus a pure `mergeBySource` that bounds the buffer to one entry per source regardless of session length (`summarizeActivity` re-merges on read, so the breakdown is unchanged).
- `apps/mobile/src/autotracker/useAutoTracker.ts` — restores the buffer when (re)entering a session, persists each captured span, and clears it when the session ends (consent off / timer stopped). An unmount/reload leaves the buffer intact, so the split comes back.
- `apps/mobile/src/screens/TodayScreen.tsx` — states the guarantee where the data appears (“Stays on this device — never uploaded”) and fixes a typo in the off-state hint.
- `docs/testing/requirements-traceability.md` — REQ-042 row gains the store test + the local-persistence note.

No new ADR: this stays inside ADR-0057's local-only decision (no new technology, no new architectural pattern — a same-device buffer via the existing storage seam).

## How was this tested?

- `./test.sh` green (882 passed / 92 skipped; domain coverage 98.4 %; adherence + req-coverage + docs checks pass).
- `activityStore.test.ts` (jsdom): `mergeBySource` sums by source / drops non-positive / sorts by name; save→load round-trip persists merged samples under one namespaced key; `clear` forgets the buffer; a malformed blob loads as empty.

## Checklist

- [x] Full local gate passes
- [x] New behavior has a test written before the implementation (TDD)
- [x] Commit messages follow Conventional Commits
- [x] New tests use the `Subject_StateUnderTest_ExpectedBehaviour` naming convention
- [x] SOLID holds — pure `mergeBySource` + a narrow persistence seam; the hook composes, the view renders
- [x] No API keys, secrets, or PII committed
- [x] Consent-first preserved (capture still gated on the `autoTracker` opt-in and only while tracking)
- [x] Architecture Governance — traceability updated; no ADR needed (within ADR-0057)

## Notes

Privacy posture: the buffer never leaves the device and is cleared on session end. This is the intentionally conservative alternative to a server-backed cross-device breakdown, which was rejected on data-protection grounds. Real per-app OS capture (desktop companion / Android native module) remains a follow-up behind the unchanged capture port, and would keep the same local-only stance.

author: ddifa86
body:
## Problem

A compacted conversation can retain an assistant `tool_use` plus its matching result while injecting a `<system-reminder>` text block at the **front** of the following user message. The `tool_use`/`tool_result` IDs still match, but Anthropic requires every `tool_result` block to precede any `text`/`image` blocks in that user turn.

The result is a **non-retryable** HTTP 400:

```
messages.N: `tool_use` ids were found without `tool_result` blocks immediately after: call_XXX.
Each `tool_use` block must have a corresponding `tool_result` block in the next message.
```

Because the persisted session is unchanged, every retry re-sends the same malformed order and 400s again — the session appears dead.

Observed shape in the failing request:

- assistant: `tool_use(call_X)`
- next user content: `[text(<system-reminder>...), tool_result(call_X)]`  ← invalid order

## Fix

At the final Anthropic Messages SDK boundary (`sanitize_anthropic_kwargs`), stable-partition each user content list so all `tool_result` blocks come first, preserving relative order within both groups. This repairs payloads that later message decorators (compaction / system-reminder injection) may have reordered, so a single serialization defect can no longer wedge an otherwise valid session.

## Test

## 概要 / Summary

Google 認証が成功したあと、既存のメールアカウントをGoogleアカウントと初回連携するケースで、Passkey設定の案内を理由に `/login` へ戻っていました。ログイン済みセッションを確立した後は、`next` の遷移先またはホーム画面へ直接リダイレクトするように変更しました。

After successful Google authentication, users linking an existing email account for the first time were sent back to `/login` for a Passkey prompt. The flow now redirects directly to the requested `next` destination or the home page once the authenticated session is established.

## 変更内容 / Changes

- Google OAuth成功後のPasskey案内用 `/login` リダイレクトを削除

author: van-s-choruskube-agent[bot]
body:
## Summary

Self-iterating review nodes (Spec Review, Code Review) escalate to a human once they've iterated too many times without converging. After a human reviews the escalation and routes the workflow back, the intent is for the reviewing node to get a fresh iteration budget before it can escalate again. Previously, the AI agent escalated again almost immediately after such a reset, because it was only ever given the raw, ever-incrementing iteration counter and told to compare that directly against the cap — it had no way to know a reset had happened.

The backend's epoch-reset bookkeeping (the orchestrator's epoch-start tracking on human back-edges, and the API server's effective-iteration safety net) was already correct and already unit-tested. The actual bug was a data-visibility gap: the agent itself was never given the epoch-relative iteration number, so its own prompt-driven reasoning drifted out of sync with the safety net that was silently correcting it after the fact.

**This PR:**
- Computes an epoch-relative `iteration_in_epoch` value in the Go orchestrator (reusing epoch-start data it already tracks) and threads it into the agent's `config.json` (`orchestrator/internal/workflow/dag_executor.go`, `orchestrator/internal/activity/activities.go`).
- Rewrites the seeded Spec Review / Code Review prompts (`api-server/.../BaseFeatureDevSeeder.java`) to reason from `iteration_in_epoch` instead of the raw `iteration` field, and bumps the template `CURRENT_VERSION` per this repo's immutable-template versioning convention.
- Adds Go unit tests covering the epoch-reset and carry-forward cases for the new field, and a Java regression test asserting the seeded prompt text compares the epoch-relative field (not the raw one) against the cap — normalized against whitespace, since the existing prompt text wraps a comparison operator onto its own line in a way that would otherwise make a naive substring assertion pass vacuously.
- Relaxes the orchestrator's `go.mod` toolchain pin to unblock `go test` in this environment.
- Fixes `scripts/e2e-up.sh`'s image build to retry once without registry cache export (`--cache-to`) if the cache-exporting attempt fails, mirroring how a failed `--cache-from` import is already treated as non-fatal. In an environment that always pushes build cache, a registry HTTP/HTTPS mismatch was aborting the build before the image was even produced, even though cache export is purely a performance optimization.

No database migration is required — the epoch-start column and its bookkeeping already exist; this only changes what's computed from existing data and what prompt text ships in a new template version.

## Code Review Findings

Reviewed and **approved**. The core epoch-relative iteration-cap fix (prompt + orchestrator changes) was independently re-verified against live source — the orchestrator call site, the API server's existing safety net, test fixtures, and the seeded prompt text byte-for-byte — and confirmed correct and appropriately tested.

The `scripts/e2e-up.sh` build-retry fix was reproduced live: the cache-exporting build attempt was run against a real registry and failed with the expected HTTP/HTTPS mismatch error; the fallback path (retry without `--cache-to`) then fired and the build succeeded. `go build`/`go vet`/`go test` for the orchestrator were re-run clean, and the diff was confirmed minimal and correctly scoped.

One pre-existing, unrelated stale comment was noted in `scripts/e2e-up.sh` as a non-blocking future cleanup item.

## ⚠️ Manual Operations Required

| Action | Local (e2e) | Production |
|---|---|---|
| Env vars / secrets | None required — no new configuration surface | None required |
| Ingress / DNS / networking | Not applicable | Not applicable |
| External service configuration | Not applicable | Not applicable |
| Template version rollout | Auto via API server startup (`CURRENT_VERSION` bump creates the new template snapshot on next boot) | Same — new template snapshot is created automatically on the next API server deploy; no manual seeding step |
| Post-deploy smoke verification | `./scripts/e2e.sh` (unit suites + cap+human-gate E2E flow) | Confirm a fresh Feature Development run picks up the bumped template version, and that a reviewer node's `config.json` (visible via node-execution logs/artifacts) contains the new epoch-relative field |
| In-flight run handling | Not applicable (e2e runs are short-lived) | No action required — in-flight runs finish on their existing template version; no data migration or manual intervention needed |

**Notes for production rollout:** No database migration is required — the `iteration_cap_epoch_start` column and its bookkeeping already exist and are unchanged. The only rollout-visible change is a new template version becoming the default entrypoint for newly-started Feature Development runs after the API server restarts with the bumped `CURRENT_VERSION`; no traffic-draining or ordering constraint applies since template versions are independent, immutable snapshots and old versions keep running untouched.

## Caveats & Known Limitations

### No backend guard against an agent that self-escalates before its epoch-relative cap is reached
**Disposition:** Accepted
- **What's not handled:** if the agent ignores the corrected data and still submits `need_human_decision:iteration_cap` early, the API server accepts it as-is; the safety net only forces escalation, never reverses it.
- **Reasoning:** correcting a premature escalation would require guessing the decision the agent would otherwise have made, which the backend cannot do safely. This is a pre-existing, deliberate asymmetry in the safety net, not something this fix introduces.

### The prompt-reasoning fix has no automated end-to-end proof against a real model
**Disposition:** Accepted
- **What's not handled:** E2E tests use a scripted executor that always submits `revised` and relies entirely on the server-side safety net; they do not exercise an actual language model reading the rewritten prompt text and choosing a decision from it.
- **Reasoning:** this matches the existing project-wide constraint that E2E/CI runs never make real model calls. Confidence in the prompt wording comes from the text-content regression test plus manual review, consistent with how the rest of the seeded prompts are validated today.

### In-flight runs on the current template version keep the buggy prompt until they finish
**Disposition:** Accepted
- **What's not handled:** because graph templates are immutable seed data (bumping `CURRENT_VERSION` creates a new, separate template snapshot rather than mutating the existing one), any workflow run already in progress on the current version continues to use the old prompt text for the rest of its life.
- **Reasoning:** this is the established, intentional versioning model for templates in this repo; it is not something a single bug fix should override. Operators who want the fix applied to an in-flight run today would need to let it complete on the current version and restart it on the new one.

### The web UI's iteration badge still shows the raw, cross-epoch count
**Disposition:** Accepted
- **What's not handled:** the run graph's node badge (`iter N`) displays the same ever-incrementing raw iteration number that caused this bug for the agent; it is not changed to show the epoch-relative count.
- **Reasoning:** the raw count is a legitimate, human-meaningful audit value (total attempts a reviewer has made across its whole lifetime, including before any resets) and is not the source of the bug. Surfacing the epoch-relative count in the UI as well would be a reasonable follow-up but is not required to fix the reported behavior.

author: rbowen006
body:
## What

`DELETE /api/v1/concierge` (the Concierge **"Start over"** reset) returned **500** (`PG::ForeignKeyViolation` on `ai_requests.conversation_id`) whenever the conversation had logged any Claude call — i.e. always after the first turn.

## Why

`ai_requests.conversation_id` is intentionally **nullable** (ADR-0014) so the AI-spend audit log outlives its conversation. But `ConciergeConversation` had no association telling Rails to nullify those child rows on destroy, so `conversation.destroy` hit the FK constraint instead.

## Fix

One line on the model:

```ruby
has_many :ai_requests, foreign_key: :conversation_id, inverse_of: false, dependent: :nullify
```

Explicit `foreign_key:` because the column is `conversation_id` (not the inferred `concierge_conversation_id`), and `inverse_of: false` because `AiRequest` has no `belongs_to :conversation`. Destroy now nullifies the audit rows — the spend log survives, exactly what the nullable FK was designed for.

## Tests

- **Model spec** — destroy a conversation with an `ai_request` → no raise, row survives with `conversation_id: nil`.
- **Request spec** — `DELETE /api/v1/concierge` with a logged `ai_request` → `200`, conversation gone, audit row nullified.

Both RED before the fix (reproduced the exact FK violation), green after. Full suite for the touched specs: 14 examples, 0 failures.

## Verification

Drove the real endpoint (not just specs):
- Seeded conversation + `ai_request`, `DELETE` → `200`, row survived nullified.
- 🔍 Double "Start over" (no conversation) → clean `200` (idempotent).
- 🔍 Conversation with 3 ai_requests → all three survive nullified.

Closes #53

under-documented in the reference docs:

  without configured `auth` or `--unsafe-no-auth` — following the examples

body: The public demo banner read 'Seven studies passed and 29 identified systematic bias requiring investigation' — no real lab has 29 problem studies. Root cause: the covering studies seeded into the demo lab to credit the Coverage map carry reused template data that evaluates as fail, and the demo study-card feed counted them. Excludes `comment='COVERAGE_SEED v1'` from the demo study-list/count endpoints (/api/demo/data, /api/demo/overview, /api/demo/studies, PDF-fallback). The demo now shows only its 5 curated passing studies (Troponin, HbA1c, Glucose, Sodium, Creatinine); the Coverage block is unaffected (it reads the lab directly via computeCoverageForLab and still shows 16/18, 15/17). Server-only; Gate 3 step 8 N/A (no UI element in the diff). Verified by curling /api/demo/data + /api/demo/coverage post-deploy.

body:
## Decision
Publish ROUNDS as a standalone adjacent clinical lane for medical residents, not as a seventh Nurse AI OS post-setup lane.

## What ships
- separate /medical-residents/ route and medres_rounds.* namespace
- deterministic Complete Edition ZIP, manifest, internal and public checksums
- supplied one-file program and DOCX with exact provenance
- mechanically normalized Markdown rendering with upstream hashes retained
- 24 inactive optional SuperPowers, 10 disabled suggested agents, 160 declared checks
- dedicated fail-closed builder, 14 package/isolation tests, and CI workflow
- README and sitemap discovery without nursing Setup Helper or post-setup navigation insertion

## Safety and non-claims
- download/open/unzip does not install
- separate resident workspace required; nursing-population state is not shared
- no PHI or live patient-specific private use
- no autonomous clinical, supervision, evaluation, surveillance, credentialing, QI/research, or institutional decision authority
- institution-approved mode requires separate hospital provisioning and authorization
- 160 checks are declared installation/release scenarios, not independent clinical validation, compliance, accreditation, certification, institutional approval, or outcomes proof

## Verification
- ROUNDS suite: 14/14 passed
- existing six-lane regression plus ROUNDS: 107/107 passed
- deterministic ZIP rebuilt twice with stable SHA-256 e4a39cc6f9a1a87ceadb7721f1c7fe5c7e2de1f2a8fe8c0cf98309ea290f3a92
- ZIP CRC/inventory/checksums passed
- source archive: 22 members, CRC valid, no traversal/symlinks/special files
- DOCX: no macros, embedded objects, or external relationships; macOS Quick Look render clean
- desktop 1280px and mobile 390px visual/overflow QA passed
- public safety scan and internal links passed
- git diff whitespace check passed

## Summary

Closes #87.

- Server-render the research paper title, metadata, abstract, and document actions.
- Defer React PDF, PDF.js, its worker, styles, and viewer state until the viewer approaches the viewport or is explicitly opened.
- Preserve PDF download, print, pagination, zoom, rotation, annotation, and text-layer behavior.

author: catherineluse
body:
## Summary
Continues increasing coverage after #14/#15, targeting three self-contained, high-ROI modules. Adds **28 tests across 3 files**; overall line coverage roughly doubles (**~9% → ~17%**).

| Module | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `src/router/index.ts` | 4% | **100%** |
| `src/utils/clipboard.ts` | 0% | **100%** |
| `src/lib/openai.ts` | ~1% | **~70%** |

### `router.spec.ts`
Asserts route names/paths, nested book routes, mobile `meta` flags, and home resolution. Invokes each lazy `() => import(...)` loader so the dynamic-import lines execute.

### `clipboard.spec.ts` (jsdom)
Covers `copyToClipboard`/`copyToClipboardWithResult` across every path: native write with mobile read-back verification + truncation detection, native read-back failure, the `ClipboardItem` and `writeText` web fallbacks, and the `execCommand`/iOS fallback (including failure and throw cases).

### `openai.spec.ts`
Mocks the `openai` client and covers `createOpenAIClient` (key validation + browser flag), `getProfileByToneKey`, `BUILT_IN_PROFILES`, and prompt-shaping/response handling for `generateReview`, `generateChapterSummary`, and `generatePartSummary` — including context-section branches, JSON defaulting, and empty/no-content cases.

## Testing
`npm run lint`, `npm run type-check`, and `vitest run` all pass (Node 22). Full suite: **152 tests across 23 files**.

## Deferred to a follow-up
The wiki-orchestration functions in `openai.ts` (`updateWikiPagesFromChapter`, `generateWikiContent`) and the larger integration modules (`cloudSync.ts`, `useDatabase.ts`, the image composables) remain the next-biggest untested surfaces.

author: harshmhta
body:
## foundation: Xcode scaffold + PDFKit viewer + CI

The v0.1 alpha foundation — **"Better than Preview."** Every downstream Phase 2
worker builds on this scaffold. Verified: builds, all tests green, and the app
launches + opens a PDF (visually confirmed).

### What shipped

**Project & build**
- `Ream.xcodeproj` generated from [`project.yml`](../blob/ao/ream-3/foundation/project.yml) via **XcodeGen**. The `.xcodeproj` is **git-ignored** — run `./scripts/bootstrap.sh` after cloning (or after editing `project.yml`). This keeps parallel workers from fighting over project internals.
- macOS **14** min deployment, **Swift 5.9**, SwiftUI-first with AppKit interop, **universal** (arm64 + x86_64), Apple silicon first.
- **App Sandbox** on, **hardened runtime** on, notarization-ready entitlements.
- `com.adobe.pdf` registered as the primary document type.

**Viewer** (`Ream/`)
- Document-based app via `DocumentGroup` → tabs, multiple windows, Finder open, drag-onto-dock, Autosave/Versions.
- `PDFView` wrapped in `NSViewRepresentable`, continuous vertical scroll by default.
- Zoom: In `⌘+`, Out `⌘−`, Actual Size `⌘0`, Fit Page `⌘1`, Fit Width `⌘2` (menu items + shortcuts).
- Reopen last document on relaunch via a **security-scoped bookmark** (sandbox-safe).

**Command palette seam**
- `⌘K` opens the palette overlay.
- `CommandPaletteService.shared` singleton accepting `(id, title, category, keyboardShortcut, action)` registrations. Starts empty.

**Portable core** (`ReamCore/`)
- UI-free SwiftPM library (compiles, tested). The seam the CLI (`pdfx`) and the v1.0 editing engine plug into.

**Tests & CI**
- 10 unit tests (`ReamTests` + `ReamCore`) + 2 UI smoke tests; 2-page `sample.pdf` fixture.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` on `macos-14`: generates the project, builds, runs **unit tests** ad-hoc, uploads the `.xcresult`.

**Docs**: `README.md` (roadmap + build), `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (seam map).

### What's stubbed / deferred (by design)
- `ReamCore` is a near-empty stub (namespace + `PDFDescriptor` model seam). No content-stream editing — that's v1.0.
- No annotations, page management, compress, metadata, or security features — those are separate Phase 2 workers.
- No AI, no CLI binary.
- App icon asset is an empty placeholder set.

### ⚠️ Contract for Phase 2 workers — build against these

| Seam | Type | How to use |
|------|------|-----------|
| **Command palette** | `CommandPaletteService.shared` (`Ream/Services/CommandPaletteService.swift`) | `register(PaletteCommand(id:title:category:keyboardShortcut:action:))`. Re-registering the same `id` **replaces** (safe to call on appear). `unregister(id:)` on close. `PaletteCommand` fields: `id`, `title`, `category?`, `keyboardShortcut?` (display hint), `action`. |
| **Document model** | `PDFReferenceDocument` (`Ream/Documents/`) | Reference type holding a `PDFKit.PDFDocument` (`.pdfDocument`). Mutate in place for annotations/page ops. `snapshot(contentType:)` is the save seam — **keep the no-op round-trip byte-stable** (fidelity contract). |
| **View actions** | `PDFViewCoordinator` / `PDFViewAction` (`Ream/Services/`) | Extend `PDFViewAction` and route through the coordinator instead of touching `PDFView` directly. Reachable from menus via `@FocusedValue(\.pdfCoordinator)`. |
| **Menu commands** | `ReamCommands` (`Ream/App/`) | Add new `CommandGroup`s here; target the focused window's coordinator via `@FocusedValue`. |
| **Editing engine** | `ReamCore` | Land the v1.0 engine here as new UI-free types; the app consumes them via models like `PDFDescriptor`. |

**Adding files:** edit `project.yml` and re-run `xcodegen generate` — don't hand-edit the project in Xcode.

### Known limitations to pick up later
- The ⌘K palette **overlay** renders inside a document window, so it needs an open PDF to appear (the ⌘K menu command is always present). A follow-up should host the palette at scene/app level so it works from a bare launch. Documented in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`.
- **UI tests** need a real signing identity to inject their bundle, so they run **locally only** and are excluded from CI (which builds ad-hoc). Behavioral coverage lives in `ReamTests`.

### 🚩 Needs orchestrator decision: license mismatch
The brief said the README should reference **MIT**, but the committed `LICENSE` file is **GPL-3.0**. I made the README/docs match the actual committed file (GPL-3.0) rather than ship a contradiction. If MIT was intended, the `LICENSE` file needs replacing and the README/CONTRIBUTING/ARCHITECTURE license lines updated. Flagging rather than guessing.

### Verification
- `./scripts/test.sh` → build + all tests green.
- Fresh `bootstrap.sh` (clean-clone simulation) → builds.
- Ad-hoc build + `-only-testing:ReamTests` (exact CI path) → **TEST SUCCEEDED**.
- App launched, opened `sample.pdf`, rendered (visually confirmed).

author: hsliuustc0106
body:
## Summary

This PR implements the module-oriented design documentation layout proposed in #5137 against current `main`.

- reorganizes the Design navigation around 21 active module pages
- adds focused draft contracts for:
  - `engine_orchestration.md`
  - `stage_runtime.md`
  - `error_contracts.md`
  - `entrypoints.md`
  - `input_output_modality_contracts.md`
- records technical owners, independent required reviewers, primary and related code paths, validation paths, architecture status, ownership boundaries, invariant namespaces, and promotion gates
- moves the legacy AR, AsyncOmni, DiT, and entrypoint pages to `docs/design/module/archive/` and removes them from active navigation; no redirect stubs are added
- keeps `vllm_omni_config.md` explicitly deferred and draft pending configuration refactoring, without assigning a stable invariant namespace

All module contracts remain `draft`. Open refactors and RFCs are cited as in-flight context, not presented as current or normative behavior.

## Confirmed technical owners

| Contract | Technical owners |
| --- | --- |
| Engine orchestration | @tzhouam, @fake0fan |
| Stage runtime | @tzhouam, @fake0fan |
| Error contracts | @alex-jw-brooks, @NickCao |
| Entrypoints | @alex-jw-brooks, @linyueqian |
| Input/output and modality contracts | @Sy0307, @amy-why-3459 |

Technical owners are intentionally separate from each contract's independent required reviewers.

## Review guide

Please focus review on:

1. whether the five ownership boundaries match the current codebase
2. whether the primary and validation paths identify the correct implementation and enforcement points
3. whether the invariant namespaces and promotion gates are suitable for future normative use
4. whether the four archived pages have been fully replaced by the active module structure
5. whether configuration documentation should remain deferred until its refactoring settles

Boundary follow-ups remain tracked in #5227, #5441, #5453, and #5570.

## Impact and non-goals

Documentation only. This PR does not change runtime behavior, public APIs, deployment configuration, or error behavior. It does not make in-flight refactors normative and does not introduce compatibility redirects for archived pages.

## Validation

- synchronized with current `origin/main` through a normal merge; no history rewrite
- `mkdocs build --strict`
- applicable pre-commit checks for YAML, EOF, line endings, whitespace, and typos
- contract validation for required frontmatter and exact invariant namespaces
- owner/reviewer separation validation
- referenced source, test, exception, and related-path validation
- internal Markdown link and active-navigation validation
- archive exclusion from active navigation
- `git diff --check`

All checks passed. Runtime and device tests were not run because the change is documentation-only.

Related to #5137.

author: franciszver
body:
Closes #44

## What

The "trust but verify" payoff: the deterministic transformation that consumes the citation checker's per-claim verdicts and produces the user-facing answer — **verified claims kept, failed claims stripped and replaced with a "Not found in record." notice, never silently passed.** A hallucinated or miscited claim visibly does not reach the clinician as fact.

- `app/rendering.py`: `render_answer(list[ClaimCheckResult]) -> RenderedAnswer(segments: list[RenderedClaim | Notice])`. One segment per input result, **order preserved** (notices interleave with kept claims). `RenderedClaim` carries its text + passing `source_refs` (for P3.8's citation chips); a stripped claim becomes a bare `Notice`.
- Trusts P3.2's `ClaimCheckResult.passed` (AND-across-citations, zero-guarded) rather than re-deriving — no partial-credit path. Fails closed on a degenerate zero-citation claim.

## Design

New `RenderedAnswer` type rather than reusing P3.1's `VerifiedAnswer`: the latter's `claims` is `list[Claim]` requiring ≥1 `SourceRef` each, so it structurally cannot hold a notice or preserve interleaving. Frozen dataclasses, matching `ClaimCheckResult`'s in-process convention. Single constant notice (no `CitationStatus` differentiation) so the output never leaks *why* a claim failed. P3.7 verdict seam documented (computable from the same results / a `Notice` tally).

## Review (Opus) — PASS

The trust-critical property verified first-hand: a stripped claim's original `text` is read only inside the kept-claim branch, so it can never reach the output — proven by a planted-secret-string test asserting absence across all segments. Order preservation, fail-closed stripping, and the no-info-leak notice all confirmed. `/simplify` dropped a needless `field()` wrapper. `app/rendering.py` 100% coverage; hermetic suite 266 passed (P3.1/P3.2 included).

author: ichirio
body:
Closes #226 (regression in #223, caught in post-merge verification)

tfrmt hides gt''s default theme lines by overlaying `cell_borders(color =
"transparent")` on body, stub, column-label and spanner cells (verified:
a plain 3-tier `print_to_gt()` carries 21 such declarations). The #223
reader normalized "transparent" through `col2rgb()` to "#FFFFFF" and carried
those sides as solid borders -- rendered black (#224), i.e. spurious rules
all over a plain tfrmt table.

An invisible border carries no author intent for RTF. `.gt_border_side()`
now returns `NULL` for `"transparent"` and zero-alpha (`#RRGGBB00`) colours,
so the zone presets keep governing exactly as before #223; explicit visible
borders are unaffected.

Tests: synthetic transparent-border gt carries nothing (no promotion, no
cell_styles); a plain tfrmt render carries zero header/body borders. Full
suite green. NEWS folded into the #223 entry; 0.4.37 -> 0.4.38.
