author: gbyo
body:
## Summary

Uploading a CSV, wiring it to a menu (lunch) widget, and dropping that widget into a Layout showed **"No items available"** in the Layout preview instead of the menu.

### Root cause
The Layout preview resolved a widget's records with `getDataSource(id)` → `previewDataSource(config)`. For an **uploaded CSV**, `GetDataSource`/`GetDataSourceDetail` intentionally **strip `uploadedContent`** from API responses (they're bulky). Re-parsing that stripped config produced **zero records**, so the menu/list/ticker widgets rendered their empty state. The Player was never affected — it renders server-cached records delivered in the manifest.

This surfaced now because the recent live-widget preview (#67) actually renders widget data instead of a placeholder card.

### Fix
Resolve saved Data Sources **by id, server-side, using their full stored configuration** (including the uploaded CSV payload):

- Add `media.PreviewDataSourceByID`, which loads the raw stored config via `rawDataSource` and returns the same `StructuredPreview`/`CalendarPreview` shape.
- Expose it at `GET /api/v1/data-sources/{id}/preview` (read-only, dashboard auth, no CSRF).
- Add `api.previewSavedDataSource` and switch the Layout preview loader to it, so widgets **and** text bindings resolve the exact records/events the Player receives.

## Tests
- **Unit** (`TestUploadedCSVContentDrivesRecords`, runs everywhere): uploaded CSV content parses into records, and `stripUploadedContent` removes the payload from detail responses — capturing the bug's cause.
- **Integration** (`TestPreviewDataSourceByIDUsesUploadedCSV`, DB-gated): a saved uploaded-CSV Source returns records via the new endpoint even though its detail response is stripped.

## Validation

- [x] Formatting and lint checks pass (`gofmt`, `prettier`, `tsc -b`, `eslint`)
- [x] Tests pass (Go media/httpapi + 49 dashboard tests; new unit test green, integration test DB-gated)
- [x] Documentation is updated (N/A)
- [x] No future or mocked feature is presented as complete
- [x] Security and migration impact considered (new endpoint is read-only under existing dashboard auth; no schema/migration changes; no new data exposure — uploaded content stays server-side and is only used to compute the preview)

author: domalhambra
body:
Two opt-in, industry-standard cartographic refinements to the poster's labeling and track lines. Each is gated behind a spec flag so **existing posters reprint byte-identically** (the manifest forever-contract), while **new posters default to the enhanced look**.

## 1. Smart label placement (`spec.label_place`: `"anchor"` | `"smart"`)

`"anchor"` (default in the spec, unchanged) gives every point name a single centered box and drops it on any collision, treating the gold route as invisible. `"smart"`:

- **Ranked candidate ring** — a name tries the Imhof/Maplex offset order (centered, then the four adjacent diagonals, then pushed-out slots) instead of dropping on the first collision, so far more names survive on a busy sheet.
- **The route as a placement obstacle** — a warp-registered `_coverage` mask (the same one the ink drapes through) keeps a name off the journey it describes; only as a last resort does a name cross the line, and then with a widened halo.
- **Leader lines** — a name pushed out to escape a crowded cluster draws a hairline haloed leader back to its feature, with a small anchor dot (NatGeo/Swiss convention).

## 2. Chronological track weave (`spec.track_weave`: bool)

Off (default) sums every journey into one cased route. On (and ≥ 2 journeys), the journeys composite **oldest → newest as separate cased strands**, so each newer journey's paper casing knocks out the older gold where they cross — an honest **over/under weave, newest on top**, so lineage reads as depth. A no-op with a single journey.

## Design notes

- **One compositing primitive.** The casing→ink math is extracted into `_composite_ink_layer`; the summed path calls it once, the weave calls it once per journey in date order. The weave is a *loop over the primitive*, not a second copy that would drift as worn-width × track-color × oblique evolve.
- **The weave lives entirely inside `_ink_tracks`**, the single ink path shared by the still and every film frame, so the film's last frame stays pixel-equal to the still (guardrail extended to a `track_weave` spec in `test_timelapse.py`).
- **Chronology ordering** (`_group_day` / `_chrono_group_order`) moves down into the `render` layer; `timelapse._group_day` now delegates to it (reduces coupling rather than adding it).
- **Reprint-safe.** Both fields default to a render no-op and are omitted from the manifest at that default, so a pre-feature manifest re-stamps byte-identically; `spec_from_json` refills the default. New posters carry the enhanced value via the `/api/proof` Form defaults.

## Wiring

`/api/proof` Form params (enhanced defaults) → `style` dict → `_build_spec`; restored on the `/api/continue` prefill. Wizard gets a "Smart labels" switch by *Place names* and a "Weave crossings" switch in the Style panel, both on by default. `docs/MANIFEST.md` documents both keys as omitted-at-default.

## Tests

Full suite green (481 passed, 7 skipped — the real-DEM-only tests). New coverage in `tests/test_smart_labels_and_weave.py`:

- Weave: default is the summed path; single-journey is a strict no-op; the weave changes the crossing render; the newer journey breaks the older gold; oldest-on-top is the mirror break.
- Placement: centered when clear; relocates off a route corridor with a leader.
- Labels (rendered): anchor mode still drops a colliding name (unchanged contract); smart mode places it instead; smart labels stay DPI-stable (proof==final MAD < 3).
- Forever-contract: serialize omit-at-default + round-trip, validate rejects a bad `label_place`, and a frozen pre-feature manifest loads with the defaults.
- `test_timelapse.py` extends the film==still invariant to a `track_weave` spec.

author: wiseowl-casc-bot
body:
Makes `Diablo4Storage.GetAttributeName` season-robust and retires the fragile hardcoded `AttributeId → name` map. Delivers Optimizer FR-C27 (`casc-fr#39`) — with a corrected premise.

## The premise correction
FR-C27 assumed `DataAttributes` (sno 1907204) is the full AttributeId registry. It isn't — it's the **designer/season-extensible** subset (281 entries: skill consumes, socketables, `S14_Mythic_*` appended at the tail; all `gbid=0xFFFFFFFF`). The core attributes the name map covers aren't in it.

## The real problem
`AttributeId` is a **registry ordinal the engine renumbers each build**. Season 14 alone moved:

| attribute | old id | new id |
|---|---|---|
| Armor | 481 | 482 |
| DamageToElite | 950 | 953 |
| DamageToNear | 1102 | 1105 |
| DamageWhileHealthy | 1120 | 1123 |
| Barrier | 1124 | 1127 |

So a hardcoded id→name map silently rots every season. The durable key is the `Generic_<Rarity>_<Token>` node-name token.

## The fix
`GetAttributeName` now (1) scans the live `Generic_` nodes once (cached) for the current build's `id→token` map, (2) maps token → label via the season-stable `AttributeNames.LabelByToken`, (3) reuses the existing sno-4080 localization. The FR-C28 compound map is re-keyed onto `(baseLabel, ParamPlus12)`. `LabelByAttributeId` stays as a defensive fallback.

Also fixes a latent bug the new coverage test caught: `BlockChance`'s label is `Block_Chance`, not the absent `Block_Chance_Bonus`.

## Tests
- `GetAttributeName_resolves_every_live_generic_node_attribute` — season-robust, **no hardcoded ids**: walks live nodes, asserts each curated-token attribute resolves.
- Content-snapshot theory pinned to current ids (482→Armor, 1123→"Damage while Healthy", …) under `kind=content-snapshot`.
- **135/135** green on `3.1.1.72836`.

Spec §Appendix A **CL-88**, devlog 0083, API docs regenerated. SnoScan recon: `dataattrs`/`attrcover`/`attrname`.

## What

Moves the automated **KOI evaluation framework** out of my personal fork (`DarrenZal/koi-research`) and into this team-owned repo, per the 2026-07-14 Regen AI Builders Standup. The framework works and runs on a schedule today — the only thing it lacked was a team-visible home.

**Why it matters:** the weekly eval digest had a shell date-comparison bug that left it silently failing every Sunday for ~5 months, unnoticed because it lived in a personal fork no one else watched. Team eyes are the real safeguard — hence this move.

## Contents (14 files, purely additive — this repo had no workflows before)

| Area | Files |
|------|-------|
| Workflows | `.github/workflows/weekly-eval-digest.yml`, `.github/workflows/full-stack-tests.yml` |
| Aggregator | `scripts/aggregate_weekly_evals.py` |
| Eval suites | `evals/suite_b_gold_set.json`, `evals/suite_d_scenarios.json`, `evals/suite_d_delta_scenarios.json` |
| Docs | `docs/eval-framework-design.md`, `docs/runbooks/eval-triage.md` |
| Report history | `reports/weekly-digest/koi-weekly-eval-2026-07-{08,12,14}.{json,md}` |

The eval suites cover **retrieval quality** (Suite B), **agent scenarios** (Suite D), and a **hallucination/citation check**. Latest committed digest (2026-07-14) shows retrieval quality healthy.

## Safe-to-merge notes

- **Nothing runs on this PR.** Both workflows are `schedule` + `workflow_dispatch` only (no `push`/`pull_request` triggers), so no checks fire here.
- **After merge, secrets are what activate the scheduled runs:**

author: phildrumsdaniel
body:
You asked me to run the audit. I ran the 577-test engine suite plus a new 59-check cross-screen reconciliation audit across six deal types — it found **one real bug**, which this PR fixes.

## The bug the audit caught
`calcDealMetrics` (the deal-state engine behind the **Dashboard, Financial Modelling and Site Scorecard**) computed the residual land value **without** the Homes England affordable grant, while `computeSFHMetrics` (**SFH House Mix, Land Valuation, one-pager**) correctly added it.

Result: an affordable scheme with grant showed a **lower RLV on the Dashboard than on the one-pager** — the "two different RLV numbers" class of bug you've had me chase, but it only appeared once a grant figure was entered, which is why it slipped past earlier audits.

Example (200 homes, 30% affordable, £80k/home grant): Dashboard RLV **£16.91m** vs one-pager **£21.71m** — a £4.8m gap, exactly the grant.

## The fix
- `calcDealMetrics` now folds the SFH `grantIncome` into **both** `rlv` and `actualProfit`, so every screen shows the same residual and margin — and "at land = RLV, actual profit = target profit" stays internally consistent.
- Exposes `grantIncome` on the deal-state return.
- The **Financial Modelling** appraisal now shows the grant as a credit — *"less: Affordable grant (AHP)" → "Net cost after grant"* — so **Profit = GDV − net cost** still foots on that screen (verified: £89.08m − £65.78m = £23.30m).

## Verification
- **577 engine tests pass.**
- New **59-check cross-screen reconciliation audit** — fully green across six deal types (no-AH, AH+grant, itemised build, chosen exits, guide price). Checks: GDV engine==deal-state, RLV engine==deal-state, one-pager breakdown foots to RLV (£0), devCost==sum of lines, Fin fees/contingency decomposition, exit-range excludes negatives, chosenRlv matches basis, timeline total==planning+build, profit==target% of GDV.
- Post-fix: Dashboard RLV **£21.71m** == one-pager **£21.71m**.

author: asoftby
body:
## Summary

Second blocker found during the golden-write attempt — this one on the very first real targeted commit (Place 5389, `--profile FULL_IMPORT`), after PR #49 (resumable media retry) was already merged. Zero DB writes occurred; the crash happens before `persistPlan()` is ever called.

- **Root cause**: `createMamagoMediaImporter` (used whenever media policy is FULL) transitively imports `@/server/media/media-storage`, which starts with `import "server-only"`. That package throws unconditionally outside Next.js's bundler — under plain `tsx`/Node, loading the module always throws, regardless of how lazily it's imported. Not Place-specific: the same importer is shared by `EventMediaSyncer`/`RouteStopMediaSyncer`. This appears to be the first time any FULL-media commit has ever run end-to-end through this CLI — every prior media-policy PR was validated only against fakes in unit tests.
- **First fix attempt, tested and rejected**: a global `--conditions=react-server` flag on the npm script, matching `server-only`'s own conditional package.json export. This is process-global, so it also changed how `react` itself resolved for the rest of this CLI's much larger import graph — several UI dependencies (`@radix-ui/react-*`) crashed with `React.createContext is not a function`, since the `react-server` build of React has no hooks.
- **Final fix**: `installServerOnlyStub()` patches Node's CJS loader to special-case only the exact bare specifier `"server-only"`, leaving every other module's resolution untouched. Verified directly: `react` and `@radix-ui/*` still resolve to their normal builds, and `createMamagoMediaImporter` imports successfully.

## Test plan

- [x] `testInstallServerOnlyStubNeutralizesServerOnly` — real dynamic import of `../src/lib/migration/media`, matching the CLI's actual trigger exactly (not a top-level `import("server-only")`, which resolves via a different path through Node's native ESM resolver and doesn't reproduce the real bug)
- [x] `testInstallServerOnlyStubDoesNotAffectOtherModules` — `React.createContext` remains a function after the patch is installed
- [x] Full `src/lib/migration/**` + `scripts/migration-*.test.ts` sweep — all green
- [x] `tsc --noEmit`, eslint, `git diff --check`, `pnpm build` — all green
- [x] Zero DB writes in this PR — code change + real-but-read-only dynamic-import tests only

author: brunorodolpho
body:
## Summary

This PR should be **the first fully-green `check` since `fea8d590`**. dev's `check` has been red since commit `37d928d6` (2026-07-15) — root cause was NOT the vi.mock gaps fixed by #248, but `pnpm audit --audit-level=high` hitting `ERR_PNPM_AUDIT_BAD_RESPONSE`: npm's registry retired the legacy `/v1/security/audits{,/quick}` endpoints (HTTP 410) that pnpm 10's audit client targets. #248 fixed the test-step regression; this PR fixes the audit-step regression and remediates the real findings the restored audit surfaces. Rebased onto `dev` post-#248-merge so this PR's own CI includes both fixes.

## Root cause 1 — the audit gate itself (FE-D08)

pnpm 10's audit client is permanently broken against the current npm registry — no 10.x patch exists; the fix (bulk `/v1/security/advisories/bulk` endpoint) landed only in pnpm 11. A full workspace migration to pnpm 11 is real, separate work (pnpm 11 stops reading `package.json`'s `"pnpm"` field entirely — `overrides`/`onlyBuiltDependencies`/`auditConfig` all move to `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, and a `--frozen-lockfile` install fails on an `overrides` config mismatch until that migration lands). Tracked as **FE-D08**, deferred.

Instead, `ci.yml`'s "Security audit" step now invokes a pinned pnpm 11 via `npx` **without** touching the workspace's pnpm 10 pin used by every other step:

```yaml
- name: Security audit
  run: npx -y pnpm@11.13.1 audit --audit-level=high
  env:
    pnpm_config_pm_on_fail: ignore
```

`pnpm_config_pm_on_fail: ignore` is **not optional** — verified empirically that pnpm 11 otherwise self-re-execs the `packageManager`-pinned pnpm 10 on startup and silently re-hits the dead endpoint, even when `npx` explicitly fetches v11. Without this env var the "fix" would silently do nothing.

`auditConfig.ignoreGhsas` moved to `pnpm-workspace.yaml` (pnpm 11's read location for this config). `package.json`'s original `pnpm.auditConfig` block stays in place too — it still holds the prose "why" for each entry in `ignoreCveNotes`, and pnpm 10 ignores the unfamiliar keys harmlessly. Verified: a clean `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` under pnpm 10 with the new `pnpm-workspace.yaml` key → *"Lockfile is up to date, resolution step is skipped"* — zero behaviour change.

## Root cause 2 — 5 real findings from the restored audit

Before this PR: **41 vulnerabilities** (6 low | 30 moderate | 3 high | 2 critical), `--audit-level=high` → exit 1.

- **vitest (GHSA-5xrq-8626-4rwp, CRITICAL) — genuinely FIXED, not ignored.** The advisory has two independently-patched ranges (verified against the advisory itself, which contradicted this repo's own pre-existing ignore-note claiming *"the only patch is vitest 4.x, a breaking major"*): `3.2.6` within v3, or `4.1.0`. Bumped `vitest` + `@vitest/coverage-v8` from `^3.2.0` → `^3.2.6` in all 19 files that pin them (root + 18 packages/apps); lockfile now resolves `3.2.7`. Removed the now-obsolete ignore entry (`CVE-2026-47429`) and its stale note.
- **@mikro-orm/core + @mikro-orm/knex (GHSA-gwhv-j974-6fxm, GHSA-qpfv-44f3-qqx6, GHSA-cfw5-68c4-ffqp — 1 critical + 2 high) — attempted the patched `6.6.14` override, REVERTED.** `pnpm install`, apps/commerce's vitest suite (16/16), and `medusa build` (compile) all passed clean — but none of those exercise the live DI-container service-bootstrap path where this repo's pre-existing documentation records a real crash (MikroORM's 6.4→6.6 `EventManager` subscribers `Array`→`Set` change breaking `registerInternalServiceEventSubscriber`). Reaching that verification needs `medusa start`/`develop` against a live Postgres, which this repo's `CLAUDE.md` explicitly forbids ("do not start dev servers to verify changes"). Reverted rather than ship an unverified bootstrap-crash risk; kept the existing `ignoreGhsas` entries (added `GHSA-cfw5-68c4-ffqp`, previously only tracked as `CVE-2026-44680`).
- **vite (GHSA-fx2h-pf6j-xcff, high) — confirmed NOT viable as a patch bump, not attempted.** Inspected `@medusajs/admin-bundler`'s own `package.json` directly: it declares `"vite": "^5.4.21"` as a hard direct dependency. The advisory's patched floor is `6.4.3` — a different major line entirely, unreachable within admin-bundler's declared range without overriding across Medusa's own semver contract. This repo's existing note already correctly identified this exact blocker; reconfirmed it directly rather than trusting the note blindly.

After this PR: **40 vulnerabilities** (6 low | 30 moderate (1 ignored) | 3 high (3 ignored) | 1 critical (1 ignored)), `--audit-level=high` → **exit 0**. The critical count dropped 2→1 because vitest's is now genuinely gone (41→40 confirms it), not ignored. The remaining 1 critical + 3 high are exactly the mikro-orm ×3 + vite ×1 GHSAs above, correctly suppressed with documented justification — nothing silently swallowed.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm_config_pm_on_fail=ignore npx -y pnpm@11.13.1 audit --audit-level=high` — verbatim output above, exit 0.
- [x] Clean `rm -rf node_modules && pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` (pnpm 10, CI simulation) — passes clean, no lockfile changes needed.
- [x] `pnpm exec turbo test --continue` (full repo, post-rebase onto #248): **37/37 packages successful, 0 failures.**
- [x] `pnpm build` (full repo): **22/22 successful.**
- [x] apps/commerce specifically: vitest suite 16/16 pass (both with and without the reverted mikro-orm override); `medusa build` (compile) passes clean in both states.
- [x] Rebased onto `dev` post-#248-merge (`6b0ba1e6`) — no file overlap (#248 touched only 2 test files), clean rebase.

author: avrabe
body:
## What

Backstop tier of the #351 fix: meld now **hard-fails** with `MisalignedReloc`
when a `reloc.CODE` memory-address site does not land on a rebasable operator
immediate, instead of silently emitting a miscompiled module.

## Why (grounded)

avrabe reported (#351) that `meld fuse --memory shared --address-rebase` left a
`ptr = &data[0]` `i32.const` un-rebased — reproduced on v0.41.1 with their exact
bytes: `wasmtime --invoke ptr-b` returned **65536** (aliasing component-a)
instead of the rebased **196608**.

**Root cause** (byte-level): the producer (clang 22.1.4 + wit-component 0.245.1)
relaxed address immediates from 5-byte-padded to minimal LEB128 but did **not**
rewrite `reloc.CODE` offsets, so each site drifts **+2 bytes per preceding
memory-address reloc**. The memargs survive (drift stays inside their wide
immediate window); the trailing `SLEB@42` drifts past `ptr-b`'s `i32.const`
range `[37,41)` → `addr_reloc` never set → silently not rebased. Upstream
producer defect filed as pulseengine/wasm-tools#3.

## The fix (layered — this is tier 1)

meld verifies every `R_WASM_MEMORY_ADDR_*` site lands on a rebasable immediate;
if any is misaligned (stale), it hard-fails rather than corrupt the shared
address space — upholding the "never silently corrupt" invariant #326 rests on.
**Drift-tolerant *correct* rebasing** (so these inputs fuse rather than fail) is
the tier-2 follow-up.

## Falsification / tests

- `test_351_stale_reloc_offsets_hard_error` — fuses avrabe's exact components
  (`tests/reloc351/{a,b}.wasm`, b sha256 `481c36…d3a3`); asserts
  `MisalignedReloc { offset: 42 }`. Pre-fix this silently returned 65536.
- `reloc::first_misaligned_code_reloc_detects_drift` — unit oracle: aligned site
  → ok; drifted onto `end` / past the section → caught.
- Negative: `test_326_reloc_const_rebasing_end_to_end` (consistent relocs) still
  rebases correctly; a real clang-22.1.8 consistent-reloc build still fuses
  (`ptr_b = 196608`) — the backstop does not over-reject valid modules.

Local: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy`, full `meld-core` test suite green.
Traceability: SR-53 (mitigates LS-D-1).

Refs #351, pulseengine/wasm-tools#3

author: brcornelius
body:
## What was done

Implements the Phase 2 component kit for the Design v1 milestone (#16), plus the planning docs that produced it (`.agents/issue-planner/16/`).

New primitives in `site/src/components/`, each built on the Phase 1 design tokens and Motion presets, each with component tests:

- **`GlassCard`** — polymorphic (`as`) elevated glass surface: translucent layer, hairline border, panel radius/shadow, hover lift, optional PS-blue `glow` variant. Renders as any element so it nests inside a `<li>`.
- **`AnimatedNumber`** — Motion count-up that renders the **final value immediately** under reduced motion and in jsdom (no timers), and counts up from 0 only in a motion-capable browser.
- **`TrophyBadge`** — trophy-metal tier marker with an accessible label naming the tier and count (e.g. "3 platinum trophies"); glyph is decorative.
- **`SectionHeader`** — heading with a decorative, `aria-hidden` PS-shape glyph rotating through △ ○ ✕ □.
- **`StatTile`** — big animated-number + label card composing `GlassCard`, entering via the shared `fadeRise` preset.
- **`GameSection`** redesigned into staggered glass card rows (rounded icon tile over a surface fallback, name, metric, hover lift + glow) while preserving its exact DOM/a11y contract; the `GameEntry` interface is unchanged so `PlayerPage` keeps compiling.

## Why it was done

#16 is the sole gate between the Phase 1 foundation (#15) and the page redesigns (#17/#18/#19), which all compose these primitives. No component is wired into a page here — that is deferred to the page phases — keeping this PR self-contained. Two decisions were locked up front: `AnimatedNumber` must be jsdom/reduced-motion safe, and `GameSection` must keep the semantics its existing tests assert.

Refs #16.

## How to manually test / verify

From the repo root:

1. `pnpm install`
2. Run the `site` gate — all must pass:
   - `pnpm --filter site lint`
   - `pnpm --filter site typecheck`
   - `pnpm --filter site test` (37 tests; 17 new across the six components)
   - `pnpm --filter site build`
3. Root package is unaffected but still green: `pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test && pnpm build`.
4. Confirm behavior spot-checks in the new test files, e.g.:
   - `AnimatedNumber.test.tsx` asserts the final value renders with no fake timers.
   - `TrophyBadge.test.tsx` asserts the accessible name "3 platinum trophies".
   - `GameSection.test.tsx` (unchanged) still passes — heading role, one `listitem` per game, empty-alt decorative icon, empty-state fallback.

body:
## Summary

Two UI/UX fixes for the deployed site:

- **Language switch only translated part of the UI.** `loadLocaleStrings` short-circuited on the small inline string table (a boot-time subset) and never fetched the server's full table from `/api/i18n/strings`. It now always fetches once per locale and merges in place over the inline table — in place so `t()`'s `I18N_EN` fallback also gains the full key set. The full English table is fetched on boot as well, so keys outside the inline subset no longer render as raw key names.
- **No pointer feedback on clickable elements.** Added global cursor-affordance CSS: interactive elements (`a`, `button`, `select`, `[onclick]`, `[role=button]`, …) show `cursor:pointer`, disabled controls `not-allowed`, text fields the I-beam.
- Service-worker `CACHE_VERSION` bumped to `v2.97.3` so cached clients pick up the new page.

## Verification

- Headless Chromium: role-switch buttons, language trigger, and `[onclick]` elements all report `pointer`; disabled language entries report `not-allowed`.
- Switching to Hindi now renders 430 Devanagari characters across the nav/landing/topbar (previously only the small inline subset translated).
- Full test suite on Node 20.20.2 and 22.22.2: 4,108 assertions, 0 failures.

body:
## What

AEAD 層を 0.10 世代(aes 0.8 / polyval 0.6 / generic-array)から **0.11 世代**(aes 0.9.1 / polyval 0.7.2 / ghash 0.6 / hybrid-array)へ移行。**cfg なしの AES-NI 経路のまま**での改善なので、配布フロア(x86-64-v2/v3)含む全ターゲットに効く。

## 実測(4 GiB / tmpfs / 無負荷直列 / 3反復×3モード)

| | 移行前 | 移行後 | |
|---|---|---|---|
| 暗号化 | 1.2 | **~1.8 GiB/s** | +50% |
| 復号 | 0.67 | **~1.07 GiB/s** | +60% |

生 AEAD マイクロベンチ(1 MiB チャンク): 1.59 → 2.95 GiB/s。さらに aes 0.9 の **VAES-512 opt-in**(`--cfg aes_backend="avx512"`)では 6.0 GiB/s を確認 — ただしコンパイル時固定で非 AVX-512 CPU では SIGILL のため、**config.toml には入れず**ローカルビルド専用オプションとして README に記載。

## コード変更(機械的)

- `generic_array` 撤去 → 各クレートの `Nonce` エイリアス+`TryFrom`/`From`(スライス由来は長さ検査つき)
- `AeadInPlace` → `AeadInOut`(in-place open)
- `aead::OsRng`(upstream 削除)→ `rand_core::OsRng` で XNonce を fill
- 対象: strategy/streaming_aead.rs、group/{at_rest,redb_storage,crypto_adapter/rc_aead}.rs

## 互換性

- **ワイヤ形式不変**(AES-256-GCM/ChaCha20-Poly1305 そのもの)。interop フィクスチャ含め **177(default)/326(mls) 全テスト green**
- baseline 対象ファイル変更なし / clippy 新規警告なし

## Docs

- README 性能表を 1.8 / 1.1 に更新、バックエンド比較注(OpenSSL 優位は約 1.8×/2.3× に縮小)、移行注記+VAES opt-in の記載、0.10 時代の検証注記は「当時」スコープに変更

author: tinkpa
body:
Backend slice of the cross-repo fix for **TINKPA/receipt-assistant-frontend#137** (HTML receipt documents can't be displayed). This is the contract-owning repo, so it merges first; the frontend slice codegens against the regenerated `openapi.json`.

## What was broken
HTML receipts (portal invoices saved as `.html`, first seen with a Tekmetric invoice, doc `019f62d7…`) ingest and post correctly, but `GET /v1/documents/:id/rendered` returned **422 `document-not-email`** — it only served `receipt_email` `.eml` docs — so the detail page's "Original receipt" fold was blank.

## Changes
- **`/rendered`** (`renderEmailDocument` → `renderDocumentHtml`): also serves raw `text/html` (and `application/xhtml+xml`) documents, sanitized through the existing `EMAIL_SANITIZE` allowlist; the `.eml` decode path is unchanged.
- **Transaction-detail** now exposes each embedded document's `mime_type` (additive `TransactionDocumentRef` field; list view leaves it null) so the viewer gates the render path on mime, not `kind`.
- **`guessDocumentKind`**: `text/html` / `.html` → `receipt_pdf` (drives only the list glyph; display is gated on mime_type).

## Security hardening (from an adversarial review of this change)
`GET /content` served raw stored bytes inline with the stored mime and **no `nosniff`/CSP** — a same-origin active-content sink. Because `.html` now classifies as `receipt_pdf`, a near-miss mime (a `.html` uploaded as `application/xhtml+xml`, which survives multer's normalization) could route to the **non-sandboxed PDF iframe** and execute script. Now: any HTML/XML/SVG doc (matched by mime **or** extension) is served as an opaque `application/octet-stream` **attachment** with `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, so it can never render inline. The mime gate also strips charset params; an empty render now 404s instead of a blank 200. HTML receipts render only through `/rendered` (sanitize-html + strict CSP + sandboxed iframe = three containment layers).

## Verification
- `tsc` clean; `openapi:generate` regenerated (106 schemas).
- Against the mini before this change: `/rendered` for the Tekmetric doc → 422; `/content` → 200 text/html. Post-deploy verification (200 rendered + sandboxed browser render + no script execution) tracked on the frontend issue.

author: kdroidfilter
body:
## Summary

- Adds a new `CompressionLevel.Ultra`. The DMG LZMA (ULMO) and DEB `xz -9e` post-processing steps — which are slower than electron-builder's own packaging — now run **only** on `Ultra` instead of `Maximum`.
- `Ultra`'s `id` maps to `"maximum"`, so electron-builder and config generation treat it exactly like `Maximum` for every natively-handled format (NSIS, AppImage, etc.). It just additionally enables the plugin's post-processing.
- `Maximum` now yields a faster build with no extra recompression; the post-processing is opt-in.
- The AppImage slow-startup warning fires for both `Maximum` and `Ultra` (both send `"maximum"` to electron-builder).
- `cmp-demo` moves to `Ultra` to keep benefiting from the smaller deb.

### Resulting behavior

| Level | electron-builder | Plugin DMG/deb post-processing |
|---|---|---|
| `Store` / `Normal` / `Maximum` | unchanged | ❌ (faster build) |
| `Ultra` | same as `Maximum` | ✅ LZMA DMG + `xz -9e` deb |

Other examples intentionally stay on `Maximum` (faster builds, no recompression).

## Test plan

- [x] Plugin compiles (`:plugin:compileKotlin`) and passes `ktlintMainSourceSetCheck`
- [x] E2E `Ultra`: `:examples:cmp-demo:packageGraalvmDeb` → `xz recompression: … −28.3%` (48 MB → 35 MB)
- [x] E2E `Maximum`: same task → 0 recompression log lines, deb stays 48 MB
- [x] `id` collision safe — no reverse `id → enum` lookup exists in the codebase

author: yzw1128
body:
## PR Category
Operator

## Type of Change
Performance Optimization

## Description

This PR adds an Iluvatar-specific `nonzero_numpy` implementation using a hybrid strategy:
- **< 8M elements**: single-pass `@libentry` kernel with per-block cumsum scatter.
- **>= 8M elements**: two-pass count+fill Triton kernels that eliminate the large intermediate prefix-sum allocation and use coalesced Structure-of-Arrays writes.

### Limitation

Small input performance (sub-million elements) is limited by flag_gems dispatch overhead (~0.5 ms per call), which is a fixed cost from the `aten::nonzero_numpy` -> Python function dispatch path. This overhead dominates kernel time for small inputs and cannot be eliminated at the operator level. Future work should register `nonzero_numpy` as a native aten dispatch target.

## Correctness Verification

Verified against `torch.nonzero(inp, as_tuple=True)` on Iluvatar BI-V150 (float32, bins=100):

| Shape | Elements | Result |
|-------|----------|--------|
| (64, 64) | 4,096 | PASS |
| (256, 256) | 65,536 | PASS |
| (1024, 1024) | 1,048,576 | PASS |
| (4096, 4096) | 16,777,216 | PASS |
| (1024, 65536) | 67,108,864 | PASS |
| (10000, 1) | 10,000 | PASS |
| (10000, 256) | 2,560,000 | PASS |
| (10000, 65536) | 655,360,000 | PASS |

All 6 dtypes tested: float16, float32, bfloat16, int16, int32, bool.

## Performance

Benchmarked on Iluvatar BI-V150 (48 samples, 6 dtypes x 8 shapes):

| Shape | Original | Optimized | Improvement |
|-------|:--------:|:---------:|:-----------:|
| 64x64 | 0.27x | 0.23x | - |
| 256x256 | 0.25x | 0.28x | +12% |
| 1024x1024 | 0.36x | 0.46x | +28% |
| 4096x4096 | 0.99x | 1.81x | +83% |
| 1024x65536 | 1.25x | 2.92x | +134% |
| 10000x1 | 0.30x | 0.27x | - |
| 10000x256 | 0.50x | 0.66x | +32% |
| 10000x65536 | 1.35x | 3.81x | +182% |
| **GeoMean** | **0.529x** | **0.753x** | **+42%** |

## Files Changed

- `src/flag_gems/runtime/backend/_iluvatar/ops/nonzero_numpy.py` (new)
- `src/flag_gems/runtime/backend/_iluvatar/ops/__init__.py` (modified)

- **Wear-requirements backfill (A1.1)** — coverage stopped ~Feb 2022; **452 wiki-cited rows** added (fang → Varlamore/Yama era) + stale fixes (bowfa 80 Ranged + 70 Agility, saeldor 80 Attack). A 40-Attack account no longer gets told to wield a fang, and a 500m budget buys bracket-appropriate gear. Citations committed.
- **Wilderness toggle (A3.1)** — the +50% wildy-weapon buff fired by monster *name*; Catacombs hellhounds got Ursine picks. Now an `inWilderness` request flag (exclusive monsters default on; shared-name monsters get an "In the Wilderness" checkbox), threaded panel → service (cache-keyed) → engine, `--wilderness` in headless.
- **Dragonfire honesty (A3.2)** — unsatisfiable shield constraint no longer half-applies (2h banned + empty shield). Falls back to the unconstrained set flagged `antifireAssumed`; the card chip says "you own no anti-dragon or dragonfire shield". Vorkath magic: Sang 2.71 → Shadow 7.10 dps.

## Engine math
- **Salve(ei) tiers (A2.1/A2.2)** — string-match bug demoted (ei) to 16.7% melee; magic *damage* had no salve branch at all. Ankou melee 7.63→8.03, magic 6.34→7.56.
- **Leaf-bladed battleaxe (A2.4)** — +17.5% vs turoths/kurasks, with pool boost + optimizer-level pick test. Kurask melee ceiling 7.29→8.18.

## Picks & defaults
- **Uncharged-weapon gate (A3.4)** — never suggest *acquiring* a weapon that can't attack (budget bought Webweaver (Uncharged)); owned uncharged twins still stand in.
- **Default monster versions (A3.3)** — bare names now mean the everyday fight: "vorkath" = Post-quest, "zulrah" = Serpentine, DT2 ≠ Awakened, zuk ≠ Enraged.
- **F2P assumptions (A3.5/A2.12)** — F2P prayer book (caps at Mystic Might), attack+strength potion pair, standard-spellbook-only; sub-31 prayer tiers now named (with corrected tier levels).

## Docs (A5)
Audit report + repro profiles + backfill citations committed; ENGINE-GAPS stale claims corrected; README calculator claim tempered.

**Tests:** 6 new suites (Salve, UnchargedWeaponPool, MonsterVersionDefault, LeafBladed, WildernessToggle, DragonfireHonesty, RequirementsBackfill, F2pAssumptions); full `preSubmit` green.

## Problema

Quando o dispositivo do visitante está em modo escuro, o texto do site aparecia em branco sobre os fundos claros das seções, ficando ilegível.

## Causa

O bloco `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` em `app/globals.css` trocava a cor do texto do `body` para chalk (`#FAFAF7`, quase branco), mas todas as seções do site usam fundos claros fixos (`chalk`/`paper`) definidos inline. Títulos e textos que herdam a cor do `body` (ex.: o `h1` da página Sobre) ficavam brancos sobre fundo claro.

## Correção

Removido o bloco de modo escuro. O site agora renderiza sempre no tema claro projetado: texto na cor escura ink (`#1A1A2E`) sobre fundo de papel. As seções escuras (hero, CTAs) não são afetadas, pois já definem suas próprias cores inline.

## Verificação

- `npm run build` passa sem erros.

body:
## 관련 Issue

- Closes #11

## PR 상태

- [x] Draft PR로 생성했다. `Codex 확인`

## 위험도와 리뷰 수준

- 위험도: `HIGH`
- 판단 근거: 동일 사용자 포인트 원본 잔액의 동시 갱신과 주문·충전 경로에 영향을 준다.
- 필요한 리뷰:
  - [x] Codex 자체 Diff 리뷰
  - [ ] 작성자 Human 리뷰
  - [ ] ChatGPT 문맥 리뷰
  - [ ] 비담당 팀원 리뷰
  - [x] 독립 AI 리뷰
  - [ ] 강화된 Human 리뷰
- 독립 리뷰 생략 사유 또는 수행 결과: 독립 AI가 최신 Diff를 검토했고 차단·수정 필요 문제를 발견하지 못했다. 실제 MySQL 실행은 별도 검증 명령으로 완료했다.

### 위험도별 기준

- LOW: 자체 Diff 리뷰 + 작성자 Human 리뷰 + CI + 실제 Diff 기반 질문 3개
- MEDIUM: 자체 Diff 리뷰 + 작성자 Human 리뷰 + 비담당 리뷰어 1명 + Human/ChatGPT 리뷰 + CI + 실제 Diff 기반 질문 5개
- HIGH: 구현 전 설계 확인 + 작성자 Human 리뷰 + 비담당 리뷰어 2명 이상 + 독립 AI 리뷰 + 강화된 Human 리뷰 + 위험 테스트 + CI + 실제 Diff 기반 질문 5~8개

## 작업 목적

#10에서 재현된 동일 사용자 동시 주문의 갱신 분실을 MySQL `point_wallet` 행 비관적 쓰기 락으로 직렬화하고, 성공 주문·USE 이력·잔액이 함께 일치하도록 보장한다.

## Human 최종 결정 요약

- 핵심 도메인 규칙: 10,000P로 3,000P 메뉴를 동일 사용자에게 10건 동시 주문하면 성공 3건, `INSUFFICIENT_POINT` 실패 7건, 주문·USE 이력 각 3건, 잔액 1,000P여야 한다.
- 선택한 설계: 주문과 충전에서 동일한 잠금 전용 지갑 조회(`PESSIMISTIC_WRITE`)를 사용한다.
- 선택 이유: 잔액 검증과 변경을 같은 DB 원본 행 기준으로 직렬화한다.
- 감수하는 한계: 별도 락 타임아웃·재시도 정책, 낙관적 락, Redis 분산락, 조건부 UPDATE와 주문–충전 혼합 경합 실험은 이번 범위에서 제외한다.
- 관련 ADR: 없음

## 구현 내용

- `PointWalletRepository#findByUserForUpdate`에 `PESSIMISTIC_WRITE` 잠금 전용 조회를 추가했다.
- 주문·충전 서비스가 잔액 변경 전 해당 조회를 사용하도록 전환했다.
- MySQL 동시성 테스트를 관찰형 로그에서 결과 강제 회귀 테스트로 전환했고 concurrency 프로필에서 Outbox 스케줄러를 제외했다.

## 주요 변경 파일

| 파일 | 변경 이유 |
|---|---|
| `src/main/java/com/example/coffeeordersystem/repository/PointWalletRepository.java` | 지갑 행 잠금 전용 조회 추가 |
| `src/main/java/com/example/coffeeordersystem/service/OrderService.java` | 주문 잔액 차감 전 잠금 조회 적용 |
| `src/main/java/com/example/coffeeordersystem/service/PointChargeService.java` | 충전 잔액 변경 전 동일 잠금 조회 적용 |
| `src/main/java/com/example/coffeeordersystem/config/OutboxSchedulingConfig.java` | concurrency 프로필의 백그라운드 Outbox 발행 격리 |
| `src/test/java/com/example/coffeeordersystem/service/ConcurrentOrderMySqlIntegrationTest.java` | Service 10회·API 보조 시나리오의 정합성 결과 강제 검증 |

## Contract Traceability

> Issue의 최종 합의, 구현 계약, 완료 조건, 테스트·직접 검증, 포함·제외 범위를 원자 항목으로 나눕니다. 결과 요구사항뿐 아니라 Human이 확정한 구현 제약도 포함합니다.

| ID | 최종 계약 | 실제 코드 증거 | 테스트·직접 검증 증거 | 상태 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C-01 | 사용자 지갑 `PESSIMISTIC_WRITE` 잠금 전용 조회 | `PointWalletRepository#findByUserForUpdate` | 실제 MySQL `concurrencyTest` 성공 | `PASS` |
| C-02 | 주문·충전은 동일 잠금 조회 후 잔액 변경 | `OrderService#order`, `PointChargeService#charge` | `OrderServiceTest`, `PointChargeServiceTest` 성공 | `PASS` |
| C-03 | 기존 주문 트랜잭션·USE/주문/Outbox 및 CHARGE 이력 유지 | `OrderService#order`, `PointChargeService#charge` | 관련 단위 테스트 및 전체 `test` 성공 | `PASS` |
| C-04 | Service 10회: 성공 3·실패 7·주문/USE 3·잔액 1,000P | `ConcurrentOrderMySqlIntegrationTest#assertExpectedResult` | 실제 MySQL `동일_사용자_동시_주문_Service는_10회_모두_정합성을_보장한다` 성공 | `PASS` |
| C-05 | API 10건도 동일 정합성 및 실패 유형 검증 | `ConcurrentOrderMySqlIntegrationTest#postOrder`, `#assertExpectedResult` | 실제 MySQL API 보조 시나리오 성공 | `PASS` |
| C-06 | concurrency 프로필에서 Outbox 스케줄러 격리, 저장은 유지 | `OutboxSchedulingConfig` | `concurrencyTest` 성공 및 기존 Outbox 통합 테스트를 포함한 `test` 성공 | `PASS` |
| C-07 | API·DTO·DB 스키마·기존 오류 계약 불변, 제외 기술 미도입 | 운영 API·DTO·스키마 파일 미변경 | 실제 Diff 및 `git diff --check` 확인 | `PASS` |

### Contract Traceability 판정

- [x] 모든 최종 계약을 행으로 분리했다. `Codex 확인`
- [x] 모든 행에 실제 코드 또는 명확한 비코드 근거가 있다. `Codex 확인`
- [x] 테스트가 필요한 행에 테스트·직접 검증 증거가 있다. `Codex 확인`
- [x] 구현 방식 제약을 결과 요구사항과 별도로 확인했다. `Codex 확인`
- [x] `N/A`에는 사유가 있다. `Codex 확인`
- [x] `HOLD` 행이 없다. `Codex 확인`

## 테스트·검증 증거

> `docs/12_EVIDENCE_GUIDE.md` 기준으로 실제 실행한 사실만 기록합니다.

### 실행한 명령과 결과

```text
./gradlew test --tests 'com.example.coffeeordersystem.service.OrderServiceTest' --tests 'com.example.coffeeordersystem.service.PointChargeServiceTest' : 성공
DB_USERNAME="$MYSQL_USER" DB_PASSWORD="$MYSQL_PASSWORD" ./gradlew --no-daemon concurrencyTest (로컬 .env 로드 후) : 성공
./gradlew test        : 성공
./gradlew build       : 성공
git diff --check      : 성공
직접 API 검증         : MySQL concurrencyTest 내 동일 사용자 주문 API 10건 동시 요청으로 성공
DB·로그 확인          : MySQL concurrencyTest가 orders·point_history·point_wallet을 직접 조회해 성공
```

### 테스트가 보장하는 것

- 실제 MySQL에서 Service 10회와 API 보조 시나리오가 각각 성공 3·잔액 부족 7·주문 3·USE 이력 3·잔액 1,000P를 만족한다.
- 주문과 충전이 잠금 전용 지갑 조회를 호출한다.
- concurrency 프로필에서 Outbox 스케줄러가 동시성 fixture를 간섭하지 않는다.

### 테스트가 보장하지 않는 것

- 주문과 충전이 동시에 같은 지갑을 변경하는 혼합 경합 결과
- 락 대기·타임아웃·데드락의 운영 예외 정책과 재시도
- 다중 서버에서의 처리량·지연 시간 성능
- GitHub Actions의 최신 Commit CI 결과

### 직접 검증 결과

- API 검증: 실제 MySQL 기반 랜덤 포트 서버로 주문 API 10건 동시 요청, 계약 결과 확인.
- DB 상태 검증: `orders`, `point_history(USE)`, `point_wallet.balance`를 JdbcTemplate/JPA로 확인.
- 로그 검증: `CONCURRENCY_OBSERVATION` 로그에 회차별 결과와 위반 목록을 기록하고, 빈 위반 목록을 강제 확인.
- 상태 전이·Rollback 검증: 기존 전체 `test`에 포함된 주문 Rollback·Outbox 테스트가 성공.
- 캐시·성능 검증: 이번 범위 제외.
- 기타: MySQL 연결에는 로컬 Docker Compose 컨테이너를 사용했다.

### GitHub Actions

- 최신 검증 대상 Commit: `088ba5f6f3cb3cfcb19c20ece95701a3b930b3f1`
- Actions 상태: `진행 중` (Harness Check #94)
- 실패 시 원인과 조치: 미확인

## 트러블슈팅

### 실제 발생한 문제

- `findByUserForUpdate` 메서드가 파생 쿼리로 해석되어 애플리케이션 컨텍스트 생성에 실패했다.
- 초기 MySQL 실행에서 애플리케이션용 DB 환경 변수가 없어 JDBC 연결에 실패했다.

### 확인된 사실

- 메서드명 끝의 `ForUpdate`는 엔티티 속성이 아니므로 명시적 JPQL이 필요했다.
- 로컬 `.env`에는 Docker용 `MYSQL_USER`·`MYSQL_PASSWORD`가 있고 애플리케이션용 `DB_USERNAME`·`DB_PASSWORD` 키는 없었다.

### 추정 원인

- Spring Data의 파생 쿼리 이름 규칙과 잠금 의도용 메서드 이름이 충돌했다.
- Gradle 실행 프로세스에 애플리케이션용 환경 변수가 주입되지 않았다.

### 시도한 방법과 결과

- `@Query`와 `@Param`을 추가해 잠금 조회를 명시했고 관련 단위 테스트와 MySQL concurrencyTest가 성공했다.
- 코드나 설정 파일을 바꾸지 않고, 검증 프로세스에서만 Docker MySQL 계정을 DB 환경 변수로 매핑해 concurrencyTest가 성공했다.

### 최종 해결 또는 BLOCKED

- 잠금 조회와 실제 MySQL 정합성 검증은 해결됐다. 로컬 환경 변수 키 정리는 이번 Issue 범위 밖이므로 변경하지 않았다.

### 재발 방지

- 잠금 전용 Repository 메서드는 잠금 애너테이션과 명시적 JPQL을 함께 두고, 실제 MySQL concurrencyTest로 검증한다.

## 미검증 항목과 알려진 제한

- 별도 락 타임아웃과 타임아웃 예외 API 정책이 없다.
- 데드락 재시도 정책, 낙관적 락, Redis 분산락, 조건부 UPDATE는 도입하지 않았다.
- 주문–충전 혼합 동시성 및 다른 사용자 간 병렬 처리량은 검증하지 않았다.
- #10의 적용 전 결과는 Issue 기록(잔액 7,000P 또는 4,000P, 주문·USE 이력 10건)과 이번 적용 후 결과를 비교했다. 적용 전 실험을 이번 PR에서 재실행하지는 않았다.

## Issue 범위 확인

- [x] READY Issue 기준으로 구현했다. `Codex 확인`
- [x] 권위 있는 최종 계약 영역을 기준으로 구현했다. `Codex 확인`

## Codex 자체 Diff 리뷰

- [x] Issue 최종 계약과 실제 Diff를 대조했다.
- [x] Contract Traceability의 코드·테스트 증거를 확인했다.
- [x] 범위 이탈과 불필요한 리팩터링을 확인했다.

- [x] 수정 후 필요한 테스트를 재실행했다.

### 자체 리뷰에서 발견하고 수정한 내용

- 잠금 조회 메서드의 이름만으로는 JPQL이 생성되지 않아 `@Query`를 추가한 뒤 관련 단위·실제 MySQL 테스트를 재실행했다.

author: kbukum
body:
## Description

Adds `cli`, a light, stdlib-only terminal-UX toolkit that mirrors the *shape* of rskit's
`rskit-cli`. It is a presentation kit, not a flag parser: it owns theming, structured output,
progress, interactive prompts with a non-interactive fallback, and cooperative shutdown. Every
renderer writes to an injected `io.Writer`, and this is the one package where `fmt.Print*`/stdout
writes are expected — nothing leaks into other modules.

The kit is intentionally *light*: raw-mode rich TUI widgets stay rskit-only, where the Rust
runtime is the stronger fit. It lives in the root module because its only third-party dependency
(`go.yaml.in/yaml/v3`, used by `render` for YAML error output) is already a direct root dependency,
so no new heavy dep is introduced.

## Motivation

gokit had no `cli` module while rskit ships `rskit-cli`. Services and tools built on gokit had no
canonical, testable way to render tables/status, drive progress, prompt interactively, or wind down
gracefully on Ctrl+C — each reinvented ad-hoc `fmt.Println` output. This fills that gap at parity
with the reference kit.

## Type of Change

- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

## Module(s) Affected

- `cli` (new package: `theme`, `render`, `progress`, `prompt`, `signal`, `live`)

## Changes Made

- **theme** — semantic `Palette` colors and `Glyphs`, resolving `NO_COLOR`, TTY, and UTF-8 locale
  capability with byte-clean ASCII fallbacks.
- **render** — `OutputTable`, `OutputKV`, `StatusReporter`, `OutputFormat`, and an
  `ErrorRenderer`/`ExitCode` that maps RFC 9457 `AppError` codes onto a CLI exit-code convention.
- **progress** — caller-driven determinate `Bar` and indeterminate `Spinner` (no background timer),
  so they render deterministically without a clock.
- **prompt** — a `Prompter` over a `Terminal` seam: cooked-stdio `LineTerminal`, a deterministic
  `ScriptedTerminal` test double, validators, and a non-interactive fallback (default/typed-error).
- **signal** — graceful-shutdown helper mapping SIGINT/SIGTERM onto `context.Context` cancelation
  via `signal.NotifyContext`.
- **live** — a bounded multi-region console (documented `MaxRegions` backpressure) for concurrent
  streaming output.
- Wiring: `domains.toml` infra `modules` now lists `cli`; `docs/MODULE-INDEX.md` and the CHANGELOG
  are updated.

## Testing

- [x] `make test` (or `make test M=<module>` / `make test-affected`) passes locally
- [x] `make lint` is clean (includes `vet` + `depguard` layering)
- [x] `make fmt` reports no diffs (`gofmt -s`; `gofumpt` also clean, enforced by lint)
- [x] `govulncheck ./...` passes for the affected module(s)
- [ ] `make check-<domain>` passes for the affected domain
- [x] Manual testing performed (describe below if applicable)

Deterministic tests use injected writers and the scripted terminal — no real TTY, no `time.Sleep`.
Per-package coverage: theme 100%, progress 100%, signal 100%, prompt 98.0%, render 97.0%,
live 95.8%.

### Test Evidence

```
$ go test -race -shuffle=on -count=1 ./cli/...
ok  github.com/kbukum/gokit/cli/live
ok  github.com/kbukum/gokit/cli/progress
ok  github.com/kbukum/gokit/cli/prompt
ok  github.com/kbukum/gokit/cli/render
ok  github.com/kbukum/gokit/cli/signal
ok  github.com/kbukum/gokit/cli/theme

$ make lint M=.
0 issues.

$ govulncheck ./cli/...
No vulnerabilities found.
```

## Breaking Changes

None — this is a purely additive new package.

## Sibling Parity

- [x] Sibling-parity tracked: rskit https://github.com/kbukum/rskit/tree/main/core/rskit-cli

Mirrors the `rskit-cli` surface as a light kit (theme/render/progress/prompt/signal + a bounded
live console; line + scripted prompt terminals with a non-interactive fallback). Raw-mode rich
widgets remain rskit-only. `docs/parity-matrix.md` already records the `cli` row as aligned (light).

## Checklist

- [x] Code follows the coding standards in CONTRIBUTING.md
- [x] Behavior was developed test-first; new/changed behavior has tests (failure paths included)
- [ ] Bug fixes include a regression test that fails without the fix
- [x] Suite is green under `-race -shuffle=on`; coverage meets the per-package floors (≥80% pkg)
- [x] No public `interface{}`/`any` (generics/typed); documented exceptions only
- [x] No `panic`/`log.Fatal`/ignored errors/unchecked type assertions on runtime paths
- [x] Dependencies (writer/glyphs/palette) injected — no globals or `init()` side effects
- [x] Code split by concern into focused files — not piled into one file
- [x] Exported items have godoc; each package has a `doc.go`; docs updated
- [x] `make tidy` run so go.mod/go.sum are clean for affected modules (no dep manifest change)
- [x] CHANGELOG entry added under `[Unreleased]`
- [ ] New dependencies (if any) are justified, minimal, and pass `govulncheck` (no new deps)

## Additional Notes

`live` is the highest-risk area: `Console` spawns no goroutines (the caller owns render cadence),
holds a one-directional lock order (`console.mu` → `region.mu`), enforces `MaxRegions` as
documented backpressure, and has a race test for concurrent region appends.

author: blas1n
body:
## B0 — stop the sandbox reaching internal services + close the unauthenticated DinD escape

The acute pre-launch risk is **internal SSRF + an unauthenticated Docker-in-Docker escape**, not internet exfil. A nested `bsvibe-sbx-*` container runs untrusted work-agent shell code and, by default, could:
- reach the DinD daemon's **plaintext, unauthenticated `:2375`** control socket on the nested bridge gateway → full Docker control → a privileged container mounting `appdata` (`/app/var` = **ALL tenants' data**). Total compromise, no exfil needed.
- reach `postgres:5432` / `redis:6379` / `backend:8000` via NAT masquerade (SSRF).

Founder decision (2026-07-16): fix before launch with **private-range egress block + `:2375` hardening + Redis auth**. Public internet egress stays OPEN (so `uv sync`/PyPI, npm, and founder external-API tasks keep working). No full egress allowlist proxy (post-launch).

### Enforcement mechanism + exactly where applied

**Part 1 — nested-sandbox egress isolation (the primary control).** `deploy/sandbox-dind-firewall.sh`, baked into the new `deploy/Dockerfile.sandbox-dind`, runs inside the privileged `sandbox-dind` daemon:
- **FORWARD (`DOCKER-USER`):** DROP traffic **originating on the nested bridge `docker0`** to RFC1918 (`10/8`, `172.16/12`, `192.168/16`) + link-local (`169.254/16`). Public destinations fall through → masqueraded out. Private ranges are STATIC.
- **INPUT:** DROP `-i docker0 -p tcp --dport 2375` (nested → gateway:2375 is INPUT, not FORWARD).
- Applied at DinD startup: dockerd creates `docker0` + `DOCKER-USER` only after it starts, so a background waiter blocks until they exist, applies the rules, then the wrapper `exec`s the **stock** `dockerd-entrypoint.sh` (wrap, never replace).
- **Nested-vs-backend separation (load-bearing):** every rule is scoped `-i docker0`. The backend→daemon management path (`BSVIBE_DOCKER_HOST=tcp://sandbox-dind:2375`) arrives on `eth0`, so it is **untouched**. The firewall never installs a rule on `eth0`.

**Part 2 — `:2375` hardening decision + residual.** Full mutual-TLS + client-cert on the daemon is a large lift (CA + server/client certs mounted into backend + worker + the `docker exec` image-load path) — **deferred post-launch**. Instead, network segmentation in `deploy/compose.yaml`: `sandbox-dind` joins a dedicated `sandboxnet` shared **only with `backend` + `worker`**; `postgres`/`redis`/`pwa` are not on it, so the plaintext socket's reachability drops from all six services to the two that legitimately manage sandboxes. This also directly addresses the brief's "compose defines NO `networks:`" root cause. **Residual (documented in the runbook):** `:2375` is still plaintext-unauth on `sandboxnet`; a compromise of `backend`/`worker` itself still reaches it — a strictly smaller surface than a nested-sandbox escape (untrusted code runs in the nested sandbox by design, not in backend/worker). Part 1 is the primary control for the nested escape.

**Part 3 — Redis `requirepass` (defense-in-depth, CI-testable).** Prod `redis` runs `--requirepass` from `BSVIBE_REDIS_PASSWORD` — the single source of truth; the healthcheck (now `redis-cli -a`) and the app's `BSVIBE_REDIS_URL` default (`redis://:${BSVIBE_REDIS_PASSWORD}@redis:6379/0`) both derive from it, so there is no drift. Adding a password to the URL means it must never hit logs: added `redact_url_password()` and applied it at the **four** log sites that echoed `redis_url` (`api/main.py`, `workflow/.../lifecycle.py`, `executors/worker/main.py`, `workflow/.../product_bootstrap_runtime.py`).

### Verification

**CI-tested:**
- `tests/shared/core/test_http.py::TestRedactUrlPassword` — password masking across URL shapes (Redis/Postgres/no-password/garbage).
- `tests/deploy/test_sandbox_network_isolation.py` — static guards: every private range dropped on `docker0`, `:2375` INPUT drop, `DOCKER-USER` used, wraps (not replaces) the dind entrypoint, **no rule on `eth0`**, sandbox-dind builds the hardened image + is on `sandboxnet`, Redis requirepass + single-source URL.
- Full gate green: `pytest --cov=backend --cov=plugin` → **5082 passed, 89.26% cov** (≥80); SDK tests 24 passed; `mypy --strict backend/`; `lint-imports` (5 kept, 0 broken); `ruff check` + `ruff format --check`.

**Runbook-verified, NOT CI (CI has no privileged Docker):** the nftables-in-DinD enforcement is proven by `docs/e2e/sandbox-network-isolation-checklist.md` — copy-pasteable commands against the real Mac-Mini DinD proving (a) a throwaway nested container CANNOT TCP-connect to postgres:5432 / redis:6379 / backend:8000 / gateway:2375, (b) it CAN reach PyPI, (c) backend still creates/manages sandboxes + a real run's verify works, (d) rollback (in-place rule removal + full revert).

### Reversibility / guardrails
- Fully reversible: in-place `iptables -D` rollback + PR revert (only `deploy/` + a logging helper touched). Rules reapply on next dind restart.
- Does NOT break: backend managing sandboxes (eth0 path untouched), `uv sync`/npm to public registries, founder tasks to public APIs.
- Scope held: sandbox network isolation + `:2375` + Redis auth only. No app logic, two-role DB, or verification logic touched.

body:
## Favicon cache-bust + hero/provider logos → z.ai

Three requested changes, isolated cleanly off `main`.

### 1. Favicon "won't change" (both apps)
The favicon files are already the correct designed art (blue disc + white orbit, generated from `ainfera-favicon-256`). The reason the tab icon didn't update is the **browser's URL-keyed favicon cache** — the stickiest cache in a browser, separate from HTTP caching *and* the service worker. Without a URL change, the browser keeps painting its previously-cached `/favicon.ico`. Added `?v=2` to every favicon URL in both apps' layout metadata so browsers refetch. (PR #264 fixed the dashboard service-worker layer; this handles the browser's own favicon cache — the last layer.)

### 2 & 3. Marketing logo swaps
- **Hero constellation:** groq → **z.ai**
- **Provider wall:** meta → **z.ai**

z.ai (Zhipu) is a real brand already surfaced on `/models`; reuses the existing `zhipu.svg` asset. The homepage brand logos are a curated showcase (not the live `/v1/catalog/brands` marquee), so no claim or CI gate is affected.

### Verified
`tsc` + build (both apps) + `check-claims` (35) + `lint:literals` + `check-links` — all green on these exact changes.

  those commands have a new option ``--keep-combined`` to retain the data files
  after combining them instead of the default, which is to delete them.
  Finishes `issue 2198`_.

- Fix: the LCOV report would incorrectly count excluded functions as uncovered,
  as described in `issue 2205`_. This is now fixed thanks to `Martin Kuntz
  Jacobsen <pull 2206_>`_.

- When running your program, coverage now correctly sets
  ``yourmodule.__spec__.loader`` as `strongly recommended <--loader--_>`_,
  avoiding the deprecation warning described in `issue 2208`_. Thanks, `A5rocks
  <pull 2209_>`_.

- Fix: with Python 3.10, running with the ``-I`` (isolated mode) option didn't
  correctly omit the current directory from the module search path, as
  described in `issue 2103`_. That is now fixed thanks to `Ilia Sorokin <pull
  2211_>`_.

.. _--loader--: https://docs.python.org/3/reference/datamodel.html#module.__loader__
.. _issue 2103:  https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2103
.. _issue 2198:  https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2198
.. _issue 2205:  https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2205
.. _pull 2206: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2206

.. _pull 2209: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2209
.. _pull 2211: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2211


.. _changes_7-14-3:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.14.3
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: the default ``...`` exclusion rule now also matches function bodies
  whose closing return-type bracket is on its own line (for example, after a
  long ``-> dict[ ... ]`` annotation that a formatter has split over multiple
  lines). Closes `issue 2185`_, thanks `Mengjia Shang <pull 2196_>`_.

- Fix: On 3.13t, we incorrectly issued ``Couldn't import C tracer`` errors.
  We can't import the C tracer because in 7.14.2 we stopped shipping compiled
  wheels for 3.13t. Thanks, `Hugo van Kemenade <pull 2203_>`_.

.. _issue 2185: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2185
.. _pull 2196: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2196
.. _pull 2203: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2203


.. _changes_7-14-2:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.14.2
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: some messages were being written to stdout, making ``coverage json -o
  -`` useless for capturing JSON output. Now messages are written to stderr,
  fixing `issue 2197`_.

- Fix: ``CoverageData`` kept one SQLite connection per thread that recorded
  coverage, but never closed them when those threads terminated. On long runs
  with many short-lived threads this leaked one file descriptor per dead
  thread, eventually failing with ``OSError: [Errno 24] Too many open files``.
  Connections belonging to terminated threads are now closed and dropped.
  Fixes `issue 2192`_.  Thanks, `Matthew Lloyd <pull 2193_>`_.

- Fix: when using sys.monitoring, we were assuming we could use the
  ``COVERAGE_ID`` tool id.  But other tools might also assume they could use
  that id.  Pre-allocated ids don't really make sense, so now we search for a
  usable one instead. Fixes `issue 2187`_.

- Following `the advice of cibuildwheel <no-13t_>`_, we no longer distribute
  wheels for Python 3.13 free-threaded.

.. _issue 2187: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2187

.. _issue 2197: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2197

.. _changes_7-14-1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.14.1
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: the HTML report used typographic niceties to make file paths more
  readable by adding a small amount of space around slashes. Those spaces
  interfered with searching the page for file paths of interest. Now the report
  uses CSS to accomplish the same visual tweak so that searches with slashes
  work correctly. Closes `issue 2170`_.

- `Add a 3.16 PyPI classifier <hugo-316_>`_ since we test on the 3.16 main
  branch.

.. _issue 2170: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2170
.. _hugo-316: https://mastodon.social/hugovk/116588523571204490


.. _changes_7-14-0:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.14.0
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Feature: now when running one of the reporting commands, if there are
  parallel data files that need combining, they will be implicitly combined
  before creating the report. There is no option to avoid the combination; let
  us know if you have a use case that requires it.  Thanks, `Tim Hatch
  <pull 2162_>`_. Closes `issue 1781`_.

- Fix: the output from ``combine`` was too verbose, listing each file
  considered. Now it shows a single line with the counts of files combined,
  files skipped, and files with errors. The ``-q`` flag suppresses this line.
  The old detailed lines are available with the new ``--debug=combine`` option.

- Fix: running a Python file through a symlink now sets the sys.path correctly,
  matching regular Python behavior. Fixes `issue 2157`_.

- Fix: ``Collector.flush_data`` could fail with "RuntimeError: Set changed
  size during iteration" when a tracer in another thread added a line to the
  per-file set that ``add_lines`` (or ``add_arcs``) was iterating. The values
  passed to ``CoverageData`` are now snapshotted via ``dict.copy()`` and
  ``set.copy()``, which are atomic under the GIL. Thanks, `Alex Vandiver <pull
  2165_>`_.

- Fix: the soft keyword ``lazy`` is now bolded in HTML reports.

- We are no longer testing eventlet support. Eventlet started issuing stern
  deprecation warnings that break our tests. Our support code is still there.

author: tyreseluo
body:
## Summary

Adds a **Matrix app-card emitter** to the gateway: agent runtime events are auto-projected into structured `org.octos.app` cards over the Matrix channel, so a Matrix client (e.g. Robrix) can render native tool/plan/summary/artifact/diff cards instead of plain text.

All of this rides existing infra — no new config. The emitter only fires when the `send_app_card` tool is registered **and** we're on the `matrix` channel (`suppress_matrix_transient_status`), so nothing changes for non-Matrix channels.

## How it works

`ChannelStreamReporter` (`crates/octos-cli/src/stream_reporter.rs`) implements `ProgressReporter::report(ProgressEvent)`. It maps runtime events → a new `StreamProgressEvent::AppCard { card_type, body, initial_state }` on the existing unbounded channel; `run_stream_forwarder` consumes them and does the actual `Channel::send(&OutboundMessage)` with the card in `metadata["org.octos.app"]`.

## Cards emitted

| Card | Trigger | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `plan` | `PlanUpdated` | checklist; reads `step/title/content/text/description` for the item label |
| `tool_activity` | `ToolCompleted` (accumulated) | **one coalesced card per turn** — a list of all tool calls with status/duration, instead of one card per tool call |
| `run_summary` | `CostUpdate` (accumulated) → `TaskCompleted` | per-turn token/cost footer; costs sent as decimal **strings** (Matrix canonical JSON forbids floats) |
| `artifact` | `FileModified` (accumulated) → `TaskCompleted` | coalesced per-turn file list |
| `diff_view` | `FileWritten` paths → end of turn | green/red unified diff, reconstructed via `git diff` (`api::diff_view_for_paths`) |

`update_plan` / `send_app_card` are treated as **self-carding** and excluded from `tool_activity` so they don't double-report.

## Design notes

- **Coalescing**: the AppCard path always sends a *new* message (no edit), so tool/summary/artifact/diff cards are accumulated during the turn and flushed once on `TaskCompleted` — one card each per turn, not a flood.
- **No floats on the wire**: all costs are `format!("{:.4}", …)` strings.
- **diff_view** is gated behind the `api` feature (the diff reconstruction helpers live there); `run_stream_forwarder` gained a `workspace_root: Option<PathBuf>` param, threaded from `session_actor.rs` call sites.

## Tests

- `projects_tool_activity_and_plan_app_cards`
- `projects_run_summary_on_turn_end`
- `projects_artifact_card_coalesced_on_turn_end`

body:
### Motivation
- Users reported recommendations skewing toward lower-rated Animation/Family movies instead of their stronger-rated genres, indicating taste signals and top-genre/tag stats were being overwhelmed by popularity/quality signals.
- The change aims to ensure top tags/genres and creator signals more accurately reflect the user's rated history so recommendations match explicit tastes.

### Description
- Increased the impact of negative genre, tag, and creator signals by raising their multipliers so disliked categories suppress candidates more strongly (`src/lib/recommendations.ts`).
- Require shared tags or genres to be a positive taste signal before granting the "shares creative DNA" bonus by adding `hasPositiveSharedSignal` and `MIN_RELATED_SIGNAL` checks (`src/lib/recommendations.ts`).
- Reduced the short-runtime bonus for candidates that conflict with learned genre/tag tastes so "easy runtime" no longer rescues disliked categories (`src/lib/recommendations.ts`).
- Added a regression unit test that verifies lower-rated family/animation signals do not appear in `topGenres`/`topTags` and do not outrank stronger thriller/mystery candidates (`src/lib/recommendations.test.ts`).

### Testing
- Ran `bun run test -- src/lib/recommendations.test.ts` and the recommendations tests passed (all tests in that file succeeded).

author: nikhilsaggi
body:
## Summary

Replaces the heuristic edge-snapping matcher with a hidden Markov model (Viterbi) matcher using [leuvenmapmatching](https://github.com/wannesm/LeuvenMapMatching). Each GPS observation gets candidate street edges scored by proximity and route plausibility; the most likely path through the network is decoded jointly rather than per-point.

### Changes
- New `bike_routes/hmm.py`: HMM matcher with beam-width retry, skip-past-dead-end resume, spur trimming
- `bike_routes/config.py`: HMM parameters (`HMM_MAX_DIST`, `HMM_OBS_NOISE`, `HMM_LATTICE_WIDTH`, etc.)
- `bike_routes/cache.py`: matcher-aware config hash (switching matchers triggers full reprocess)
- `bike_routes/cli.py`, `matching.py`: dispatch through `_build_matcher_context`/`_match_one`
- `pyproject.toml`: added `leuvenmapmatching>=1.1`, `rtree>=1.0`
- `tests/test_hmm.py`: 5 tests on synthetic grid
- Full-corpus reprocessed GeoJSON (1,198 rides)

### Full-corpus comparison (1,198 NYC rides)

| Metric | Heuristic | HMM | Change |
|--------|-----------|-----|--------|
| Merged features | 22,412 | 18,363 | **-18%** |
| Street km | 1,441 | 1,225 | **-15%** |
| Jog vertices (global) | 3,545 | 2,607 | **-26%** |
| 9th Ave jogs | 17 | 17 | 0% |
| Greenway jogs | 27 | 24 | -11% |

Fewer features and street-km reflect elimination of parallel-way oscillation and block-sized routing detours. 26% fewer jog vertices means smoother rendered corridors.

## Test plan
- [x] `pytest` passes (77 tests including 5 new HMM tests)
- [x] Full reprocess of all 1,198 rides completes without error
- [x] Comparison metrics show improvement across all measured dimensions
- [ ] Visual inspection of live map with HMM GeoJSON

Closes #11

author: nikitapav19
body:
### Отчёт по заданию: Задание 14: Знакомство с потоками

**Цель**  
Познакомиться с возможностями класса `Thread` платформы .NET. Научиться запускать длительные операции в отдельных потоках, синхронизировать их выполнение с помощью примитивов (`Barrier`) и безопасно агрегировать результаты с помощью атомарных операций (`Interlocked`).

**Что сделано**  
Реализован метод `DefiniteIntegral.Solve`, вычисляющий определенный интеграл методом трапеций с распараллеливанием вычислений. Отрезок интегрирования разбивается на части по количеству потоков, каждый поток вычисляет свою локальную сумму, после чего результаты атомарно объединяются в общий результат.

**Логика работы компонентов:**
- **Разбиение задачи:** Исходный отрезок `[a, b]` делится на `threadsnumber` равных частей (чанков). Для последнего потока верхняя граница явно устанавливается в `b`, чтобы избежать ошибок округления `double`.
- **Многопоточное вычисление:** Для каждого чанка создается и запускается экземпляр `Thread`. Внутри потока выполняется цикл вычисления площади трапеций на локальном отрезке.
- **Атомарная агрегация:** Поскольку в .NET нет метода `Interlocked.Add` для типа `double`, используется паттерн `CompareExchange` в цикле `while`. Это гарантирует, что обновление общей суммы `_totalSum` произойдет только если значение не было изменено другим потоком с момента его чтения, предотвращая гонки данных (race conditions).
- **Синхронизация:** Используется примитив `Barrier`, инициализированный количеством рабочих потоков + 1 (для основного потока). Метод `SignalAndWait()` блокирует основной поток до тех пор, пока все рабочие потоки не завершат свои вычисления и не вызовут `SignalAndWait()` со своей стороны.

**Тестирование (xUnit)**  
Для проверки корректности создан проект `task14tests`. Написаны тесты, проверяющие точность вычислений на разных функциях и конфигурациях потоков:
- `Test1` — интегрирование функции $f(x) = x$ на отрезке $[-1, 1]$ (ожидаемый результат 0) в 2 потока.
- `Test2` — интегрирование функции $f(x) = \sin(x)$ на отрезке $[-1, 1]$ (ожидаемый результат 0) в 8 потоков.
- `Test3` — интегрирование функции $f(x) = x$ на отрезке $[0, 5]$ (ожидаемый результат 12.5) в 8 потоков с высоким шагом точности.

**Примеры работы:**
- Вызов `DefiniteIntegral.Solve(0, 5, x => x, 1e-6, 8)` -> создается 8 потоков, каждый вычисляет свою часть интеграла, результаты атомарно суммируются, `Barrier` дожидается завершения всех 8 потоков, возвращается значение `12.5`.

body: dracut is not installed in the image (only initramfs-tools), so kernel-install's `initrd_generator=dracut` was a no-op: it left the staging area empty and the loaderentry plugin fell back to initramfs-tools' /boot/initrd.img-<ver>. author: almaslennikov
body:
## Summary
- mount a dedicated emptyDir at /var/lib/mft in the sriov-network-config-daemon container
- keep readOnlyRootFilesystem enabled while allowing the NVIDIA/DOCA reset tooling to persist its runtime state

## Why
The NVIDIA config-daemon image replaces the mstfwreset compatibility command with the mlxfwreset implementation. That path can write under /var/lib/mft. With the config daemon root filesystem mounted read-only, firmware reset can fail before node reboot with:

```
-E- [Errno 30] Read-only file system: '/var/lib/mft'
```

The upstream CentOS/mstflint image does not reproduce this because its mstfwreset implementation does not use /var/lib/mft. This change is needed for the NVIDIA/DOCA image used by this branch while keeping the container root filesystem read-only.

## Validation
- go test ./pkg/render
- Built and pushed linux/amd64 operator image from this branch: harbor.mellanox.com/cloud-orchestration-dev/sriov-network-operator:network-operator-26.7.x-mft-state-amd64
- Built and checked the upstream-Dockerfile config-daemon image separately; it uses mstflint mstfwreset and does not reproduce the /var/lib/mft failure

author: lmdc45
body:
## Problem

Full-screen TUIs (vim, less, Claude Code, Grok, …) enable DEC mouse tracking
(`?1000` / `?1002` / `?1006`, …).

Two failure modes after **Reload Window** / unclean exit:

1. **Dead process** — modes stay on → next shell gets mouse as text (`[M…]`, `[MC…]`).
2. **Live process** — modes stripped or incomplete on restore → clicks stop working
   even though the app (and often the PTY) is still running.

## Split ownership (two PRs, one fix)

| Situation | Owner | Responsibility |
|-----------|--------|----------------|
| Dead process / sticky modes in a shell | **VS Code (host)** | Clear modes on root exit; strip mouse-enable CSI on PTY replay when there is no live owner |
| Soft Reload, process may still be alive | **App (e.g. Grok)** | Do not RESTORE on CTRL_CLOSE; drain-coalesced mouse-only reassert on FocusGained/Resize |

Neither side alone is enough: the host cannot repaint every app’s UI; the app cannot clear modes after it is already dead.

## This PR (host)

1. **Root process exit** — full sticky reset (mouse + paste/focus + leave alt + show cursor) when the **root** PTY process exits.
2. **Conditional strip on replay** — strip mouse-tracking *enable* CSI (incl. X10 `?9`) only when:
   - root is already dead, or
   - Windows + shell-like root + **no** console children (nested TUI died under a live shell).  
   Live full-screen TUI / shell with children → **verbatim** replay (no live-app regression).
3. **SGR on live replay** — SerializeAddon re-emits tracking (`?1002h`) but not SGR (`?1006h`). When tracking is present without SGR, append `?1006h` so modern apps still get `\x1b[<…M` clicks after Reload.
4. **Fail-open child detection** — if the process tree cannot be read, assume children exist so we never false-strip a live nested TUI.
5. **Replay complete** — full exit reset only if the root already exited.

**Intentionally not done:** host-synthesized focus-in (`CSI I`). Stale `?1004` after a dead child can inject protocol input into a shell. Live reassert is the app’s job (companion PR).

## Companion (app)

Soft CTRL_CLOSE (no full RESTORE) + drain-coalesced FocusGained **mouse-only** reassert (no EnterAlternateScreen; no soft-reattach latch; no wall-clock cooldown) for keep-process Reload:

https://github.com/xai-org/grok-build/compare/main...lmdc45:fix/sticky-mouse-tracking-after-unclean-exit?expand=1

Fork PR: https://github.com/lmdc45/grok-build/pull/1

## Tests

| Layer | What |
|-------|------|
| Unit | `src/vs/platform/terminal/test/common/terminalMouseModeReset.test.ts` — strip, conditional policy, ensure SGR |
| Headed smoke | Filter **Terminal Mouse Modes** — fake TUI + Playwright clicks; oracle = SGR growth in a log file |

| Case | Expect |
|------|--------|
| Live TUI + Reload | Process **alive**; SGR mouse log **grows** after Reload clicks |
| Unclean kill of TUI | Shell usable; **no** sticky `[MC…` |
| Nested-dead + Reload | Same after restore (Windows childless shell path) |

```text
npm run smoketest-no-compile -- -f "Terminal Mouse Modes"
```

## Risks / non-goals

| Item | Notes |
|------|--------|
| POSIX nested-dead + Reload | Residual hole (no reliable child signal) — same as upstream for that combo; root exit still cleans |
| False strip | Mitigated by fail-open children + shell-like gate |
| Host CSI I | Non-goal (unsafe into shells) |
| App-side soft Reload | Companion PR, not this change |

## Why this shape

- Host owns terminal state that **outlives** the process.
- Live apps keep mouse without requiring every TUI to reassert on FocusGained.
- Dead / nested-dead paths get a clean shell.
- Composes with keep-process Reload (inference can stay alive).

author: neverhook
body:
## Summary

- switch Ubuntu Ports entries from HTTP to HTTPS before the ARM64 CUDA install
- install job-wide apt IPv4, retry, and timeout policy for all ARM64 package operations
- make the NVIDIA keyring download use IPv4 with bounded retries
- free hosted-runner disk before the source Docker build and report disk usage before/after
- enable plain Docker build progress logs

## Motivation

### ARM64 package access

The ARM64 matrix failed before Mooncake was configured or built. In PR #2934 run 29479306961, Python 3.10 failed in `Install CUDA Toolkit 13.0 (arm64 SBSA)` and Python 3.12 was cancelled by matrix fail-fast. PR #2935 reproduced the same failure in run 29479320966. The completed logs show IPv6 is unreachable and all IPv4 connections to `ports.ubuntu.com:80` time out while fetching Ubuntu packages.

### Docker build capacity

PR #2934 run 29479306961 also failed while linking inside `docker/mooncake.Dockerfile` with `/tmp ... No space left on device`; pip then reported `[Errno 28]`. The same Docker job passed on the larger stacked #2935 SHA, so this is hosted-runner capacity pressure rather than a source error. The cleanup removes large unused hosted-toolcache and Android SDK directories before Buildx starts and leaves disk diagnostics in every run.

This PR is intentionally separate from #2934 and #2935 because both failures are runner/CI reliability issues, not their feature code.

## Validation

Local checks:

- parsed `.github/workflows/ci.yml` with PyYAML
- extracted the modified ARM64 and Docker `run` blocks and passed them through `bash -n`
- `git diff --check`
- `typos-cli 1.30.2 .github/workflows/ci.yml`

Remote validation:

- [full run 29482832654](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/actions/runs/29482832654) on the original base: all jobs passed, including ARM64 3.10/3.12, Docker, MUSA, wheel tests, Ascend, integration, and CI Gate
- [build-arm64 (3.10)](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/actions/runs/29482832654/job/87575069685): success
- [build-arm64 (3.12)](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/actions/runs/29482832654/job/87575069364): success
- [Build Docker Image](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/actions/runs/29482832654/job/87575069433): success

After `main` advanced to `90cdf179`, the original commits were rebased without conflict. A blind review then found that step-local apt options did not cover later `dependencies.sh` package operations; head `9392972f` persists the policy through `/etc/apt/apt.conf.d`, adds the established Android SDK cleanup target, and removes a redundant Docker build argument. [Final run 29497850441](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/actions/runs/29497850441) is pending on head `9392972f`.

author: gertvandenberg
body:
`vercel link` appends a blanket `.env*` rule to `.gitignore`. Half of that is genuinely useful, half is a trap.

**Useful:** it closes a real gap. The old rules (`.env`, `.env*.local`) never covered a plain `.env.production` — which would have been committable to a public AGPL repo.

**Trap:** it also swallows `.env.example`, which this repo tracks as the documentation for every supported variable. Already-tracked files are unaffected so nothing is broken today, but anyone who removes and re-adds it — or a contributor adding it fresh — would find git silently refusing.

Keep the broad rule, add `!.env.example`, and fold both into the existing env block with a note on why it's shaped this way.

| `.env` | ignored |
| `.env.local` | ignored |
| `.env.production` | ignored (newly covered) |
| `.env.production.local` | ignored |
| `.env.development` | ignored |

Fixes #1307.

## Problem

When a `DO_WHILE` task is nested inside another `DO_WHILE`, the inner loop's
`loopCondition` evaluation throws:

```
TypeError: Cannot read property 'iteration' of undefined
```

`DoWhile.java::evaluateCondition()` builds the condition-input map by calling:

```java
conditionInput.put(task.getReferenceTaskName(), task.getOutputData());
```

At runtime, a nested DO_WHILE task has its outer iteration suffix appended to its
reference name (e.g. `inner__1` instead of `inner`). The `loopCondition` expression
references the bare name (`$.inner['iteration']`), so the lookup returns `undefined`
and the expression throws.

## Fix

Apply `TaskUtils.removeIterationFromTaskRefName()` — the same helper already used
for loop body tasks in lines 534-536 of the same method — to the self-entry:

```java
// Before
conditionInput.put(task.getReferenceTaskName(), task.getOutputData());

// After
conditionInput.put(
    TaskUtils.removeIterationFromTaskRefName(task.getReferenceTaskName()),
    task.getOutputData());
```

One-line change, no new imports (TaskUtils is already imported).

## User impact

First-time and experienced users writing nested DO_WHILE workflows would hit an
opaque TypeError and have no path to fix it (the `loopCondition` syntax was
correct; the engine was at fault). After this fix, nested DO_WHILE loops with
correct `loopCondition` expressions evaluate cleanly.

## Test

Reproducible with the `ks_combo_do_while_do_while` workflow in
[conductor-oss/conductor-test-harness](https://github.com/nthmost-orkes/conductor-test-harness)
kitchen-sink battery. With this fix deployed, the nested DO_WHILE runs to
COMPLETED correctly (outer=1 iteration).

Note: A companion bug (#1308) exists where outer>1 iterations cause body-task
naming collisions. That is a separate, deeper issue.
