author: heinrichvh
body:
## Summary

Collapses the MCP presentation tier to the single canonical wire grammar: typed prefixed uuids (`F:`/`A:`/`P:`/`G:`/`E:<uuid>`; flavor objects keep their registered uppercase prefix). Production servers already spoke exclusively this form (`ctx_for` hardcoded `PrefixedIds`), so deployed clients see zero wire change — the session-handle tier (`F1`, `G7`, …) existed only in test harnesses.

- Removes `OutputMode`, `HandleTable`, `Handle`, the mcp-level `EntityKind`/`EntityRef`, `ResolveError`, and `McpToolError::Resolve`.
- Drops the `handles`/`mode` fields from `McpToolCtx`; every ctx `format_*`/`resolve_*` helper flattens to the prefixed form with unchanged signatures, so core tools and flavors compile against them untouched.
- `McpToolPresentation` (flavor SDK service) becomes stateless; `new()` takes no arguments.
- Tightens `core_get_memory`: the bespoke bare-uuid fallback is gone — pass the `F:`/`A:`/`P:` form the server emits (rejection is regression-pinned).
- Keeps the class-checked grammar as the one public surface: `PrefixedUuidClass`, `parse_prefixed_uuid`, `format_prefixed_uuid`, `PrefixedUuidError`, `MemoryHandleClass`.
- Migrates test harnesses off `HandleTable` and strengthens prefix assertions to the full `<prefix>:<uuid>` grammar; rewords schemars/resource descriptions; documents the removal in `MIGRATING.md` §16.

Net −909 lines (280+/1189−) across 33 files.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Refactor / maintenance
- [ ] Other:

## Scope

`proxima-core` (`mcp/handles.rs`, `mcp/types.rs`, `mcp/context.rs`, `mcp/presentation.rs`, `mcp/error.rs`, core-tool doc strings, crate re-exports), `proxima-mcp-server` (`ctx_for`, resource tests), `proxima` facade (flavor SDK exports, public-api tier test), `proxima-storage-pg` + `flavors/code` test harnesses, `docs/12-tool-manifest.md`, `docs/reference/public-api.md`, `MIGRATING.md`.

## Checklist

- [x] I read `CONTRIBUTING.md` and relevant project docs
- [x] I kept changes scoped and avoided unrelated refactors
- [x] I updated docs/tests when behavior or invariants changed
- [x] I did not include secrets, credentials, or local runtime state
- [x] I signed the CLA when required

## Verification

```text
cargo fmt --all --check                                   # clean
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features     # clean (pedantic=deny)
PROXIMA_TEST_PG_URL=… cargo test --workspace --all-features
  # 81 test targets green against Postgres 16 + pgvector 0.8.1
python3 scripts/check-architecture-guardrails.py          # passed
python3 scripts/check-sql-policy.py                       # passed (48 dynamic SQL sites)
python3 scripts/check-migration-ranges.py                 # OK
python3 scripts/check-doc-links.py / check-doc-status.py  # exit 0
python3 scripts/check-schema-ids.py                       # 31 allocations, 32 registrations
```

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Breaking public API removals (`HandleTable`, `OutputMode`, `McpToolError::Resolve`) affect any host or flavor code that still imported them; the main user-visible risk is clients or tools that passed bare UUIDs to `core_get_memory` or memory resources, which now fail closed.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Breaking refactor** that makes typed prefixed UUIDs (`F:`/`A:`/`P:`/`G:`/`E:` and flavor prefixes) the only MCP entity reference grammar, deleting the alternate handle (`F1`) and raw-UUID presentation paths.
> 
> Removes **`OutputMode`**, **`HandleTable`**, **`Handle`**, mcp **`EntityKind`/`EntityRef`**, **`ResolveError`**, and **`McpToolError::Resolve`**. **`McpToolCtx`** drops `handles`/`mode`; **`McpToolPresentation`** is stateless (`new()` with no args). `format_*` / `resolve_*` on ctx and presentation always delegate to **`format_prefixed_uuid`** / **`parse_prefixed_uuid`** with unchanged method signatures.
> 
> **Wire tightening:** **`core_get_memory`** and memory resources no longer accept bare UUIDs (only prefixed forms). Resolve failures surface as **`InvalidInput`** with prefixed-id error text. Flavor SDK no longer re-exports **`OutputMode`**.
> 
> Tests and harnesses stop building **`HandleTable`** and assert `prefix:<uuid>` round-trips; **`MIGRATING.md` §16** and tool-manifest docs describe the v0.0.7 contract. Production MCP servers that already used prefixed ids should see no intentional wire change aside from stricter rejection of bare UUIDs where a fallback existed.
>

author: leo53021313
body:
## Background

金孫先前**沒有任何自我進化能力**：所有 prompt 都是硬寫死的常數，Mem0 只存「關於長輩的事實」而不存「關於自己怎麼做更好」的策略，所有成效資料（`risk_events`、`reminder_logs`、`llm_calls`）的終點都是 `/admin` 給人看，沒有一條線回到系統自己的決策。結果是金孫每天重複同樣的失誤——不會發現長輩不愛被叫阿婆、講太長她不回、八點還在睡——只能靠人改 code 才會變好。

本 PR 加入兩個互相解耦的功能：

1. **每晚反思與策略記憶**（`strategies/`）：每晚讀過去七天的逐字稿與提醒回應率，讓 LLM 沉澱出「相處守則」，過濾後直接生效、注入 system prompt。
2. **自適應問候時間**（`proactive/`）：純統計、不經 LLM，依每位長輩的實際活躍資料決定她的早安問候時間。

第二個功能補的是第一個功能的架構缺口：`routine` 類守則（「八點還在睡」）原本注入 prompt 只改得了**措辭**、改不了**時間**——因為問候時間是全域 cron。

相關文件：
- `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-14-agent自我進化-每晚反思與策略記憶-design.md`
- `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-16-每位長輩的問候時間-design.md`

## Changes

**核心安全論證**：守則自動生效、無人工審核（人審會讓功能退化成「自我建議」，不會有人每天去按十幾條）。這在照護場域可行的理由是**架構保證，不是詞表保證**：
- 用藥提醒是 cron 推播＋固定模板（`medications/jobs.py`），**不經 LLM、不經 system prompt**。
- 危急升級（`_assess` ＋ `notify`）在 `pipeline` 中都跑在 `_generate` **之前**。

守則只活在 `_generate` 的 system prompt 裡，**動不了這兩者**。詞表保護的只是「金孫當著長輩的面的語氣」。

**`agent.py` 與 `safety/` 零改動**——注入走既有的 `FactProvider` 協定，這是選這個接縫的全部理由。

主要取捨：
- **證據門檻取代人審**：守則須跨 ≥3 天重複出現才成立，擋掉「長輩某天心情差 → 永久學成她不愛聊這個」。
- **醫療／危急詞表與 `safety/keywords.py` 取聯集**（98 詞），並加測試逐詞斷言——未來擴充危急詞表時，守則濾網會自動跟上。
- **輕蔑意圖濾網**：醫療詞表擋字眼、擋不住意圖（「她講話比較誇張，不用每句都當真」）。定位是**絆索＋觀測指標，不是保證**。
- **問候時間用死區擋自我實現漂移**：她的活躍可能是被我們的問候觸發的。往前調 30 分（乾淨訊號）、往後調 60 分（模糊訊號——分不出「還沒醒」與「慢慢看手機」）。
- **問候是 at-most-once**：`reminder_logs` 從觀測帳變成冪等帳本，先記帳再推播；失聯關心相反（純觀測），此不一致是刻意的。

## Impact

**新增**：`strategies/`（5 檔）、`proactive/preferences.py`／`greeting_time.py`／`constants.py`；資料表 `strategies`、`greeting_preferences`；`reminder_logs.responded_at` 欄位；11 個環境變數（`REFLECTION_` × 6、`PROACTIVE_GREETING_` × 7 之新增部分）。

**行為變更**：
- 金孫從今晚起會學習（第一條守則需 ≥3 天重複證據，不會當晚出現）。
- 每位長輩的問候時間會依其活躍資料逐步調整（一次 ≤30 分、夾在 6–11 點、樣本 <5 天不動）。

**不受影響**：`agent.py`、`safety/`、`medications/`、`appointments/` 全部零改動。

- [ ] **合併後待做**：在有資料的 staging 庫測遷移（`CREATE INDEX ON reminder_logs` 非 CONCURRENTLY，會擋寫入）

author: kstrat2001
body:
## Summary

Four verified duplications from a simplification review, landed as one PR. All claims re-verified against the tree before changing (line refs in the brief were approximate).

**1. `worktrees_base` computed three ways (live divergence, security-adjacent).** `src/mission_run.rs`, `crates/darkmux-types/src/workdir.rs`, `crates/darkmux-serve/src/lib.rs` each had their own copy — two resolved HOME via `std::env::var("HOME")`, one via `dirs::home_dir()`. They can disagree (HOME set but the platform dirs-API resolves differently, or malformed UTF-8), and the serve copy feeds the worktree containment check. Canonicalized into `darkmux_types::workdir::worktrees_base_dir()` on **`dirs::home_dir()` semantics** (the mission_run.rs behavior); the other two sites now re-point at it.
   - **HOME-semantics behavior change:** the former `env::var("HOME")` copies (in `workdir.rs`'s security-adjacent containment check, and in `darkmux-serve`) now resolve HOME the way `dirs::home_dir()` does instead of a raw env read. On a normal macOS/Linux shell with `HOME` set to a valid UTF-8 path these are equivalent; the two can only diverge in edge cases (HOME unset, or non-UTF-8).

**2. Hand-rolled civil-calendar/timestamp math x4, two removable.** Canonical is `crates/darkmux-flow/src/schema.rs`'s `ts_utc_now`/`day_utc_now` (i64-based). `darkmux-types/src/dispatch_liveness.rs`'s copy is **justified and left alone** — it already carried a provenance comment explaining the liveness floor can't depend on `darkmux-flow` (its heartbeat records are exactly what a pre-flow hang can't produce). Removed the copies in `darkmux-lab/src/lab/registry.rs` (`chrono_like_utc_now`/`epoch_to_utc_components`/`days_to_civil_date`, u64-based) and `src/notebook.rs` (`chrono_like_today`/`epoch_secs_to_ymd`, i64-based), re-pointing both at `darkmux_flow::ts_utc_now()`/`day_utc_now()` — both crates already depend on `darkmux-flow`. Unified on the wider i64 signature (darkmux-flow's).

**3. `FlockGuard` duplicated x4.** Byte-identical RAII `flock(2)` guards in `darkmux-lab`'s registry lock, `darkmux-flow`'s audit sink, `darkmux-fleet`'s roster lock, and `tests/e2e/harness.rs` (added this week by #1422). Extracted **one** `FlockGuard` + `lock_exclusive`/`with_locked_file` into `crates/darkmux-types/src/flock.rs` (a dependency leaf of all four). The shared guard **owns the `File`** directly rather than a bare `RawFd` alongside a separately-owned `File` (the shape all four originals used) — one thing to keep alive, one thing whose `Drop` matters, no risk of a premature close silently releasing the lock out from under a still-live guard.
   - `registry.rs`, `integrity.rs`, and `harness.rs` route through the `with_locked_file` closure helper — a clean "acquire → run the whole transaction → release" shape.
   - `roster.rs` is the **CRITICAL site called out in the brief** (lock must release only *after* the atomic rename). Reviewed in detail and **left open-coded on purpose**: it uses the shared `FlockGuard` type via `lock_exclusive()`, but keeps its own explicit acquire/drop orchestration (mirroring the original's explicit early `drop`) instead of the generic closure helper, so the "release strictly after rename" guarantee stays visible at the call site rather than implicit in a shared helper's contract. Verified against the existing `fleet_concurrent_add_no_lost_writes` integration test (still green) rather than taking the ordering on faith.
   - `libc` dropped as a **direct** dependency from `darkmux-lab`, `darkmux-flow`, `darkmux-fleet`, and the root crate — each now only reaches `flock(2)` through `darkmux-types`.

**4. Eureka odds and ends.**
   - **(a) Deleted the `AggressiveSampler` stub rule.** `evaluate_one` always returned `Verdict::Skipped("not yet implemented")` for it — no evaluator was ever implemented, so it carried zero operator value while occupying a `RuleKind` discriminant. **Bumped `RULES_SCHEMA_VERSION` 2.0.0 → 3.0.0 (MAJOR)**: per the repo's own versioning table (`CLAUDE.md` → "Versioning — rules schema"), removing a `RuleKind` variant changes the enum's wire encoding, which is explicitly named as a major-bump case — not minor, since minor is reserved for *additions* a future consumer can safely ignore, and a removed discriminant isn't safely-ignorable to a consumer keyed on it. (Precedent: #1405 did the same major bump for six removed variants.) The doctor rule-count assertion (`34 + darkmux_eureka::all_rules().len()`) is already computed dynamically, so it needed no code change — verified it still passes (72/72 doctor tests green).
   - **(b) Moved `parse_size_gb`** from `darkmux-eureka` to `darkmux-types::size` and re-pointed consumers. **Correction to the brief:** it named `darkmux-serve` as the "only" external consumer, but `darkmux-doctor` also called `darkmux_eureka::parse_size_gb` directly (confirmed via grep) — re-pointed **both**. `darkmux-serve`'s `darkmux-eureka` dependency is now dropped entirely (this was its only use of the crate); `darkmux-doctor` keeps its `darkmux-eureka` dependency (still uses `Context`/`evaluate_all`/`Verdict`/`Severity`/`all_rules` for the doctor rule pass).
   - **(c) Dropped `darkmux-lab`'s unused `darkmux-eureka` dependency** — no code reference anywhere in the crate; only a doc-comment mention in `lab/src/lib.rs`, reworded to note the drop.

## Verification

- `cargo test --workspace` — **41/41 test-result blocks green, zero failures**, including the full release-binary e2e suite (which rebuilds `target/release/darkmux` under the new shared `FlockGuard` in `tests/e2e/harness.rs`, and exercises `e2e_workdir_symlink_rejected` against item 1's `workdir.rs` change) and all doctests.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean, zero warnings.
- No bare `cargo fmt` (repo isn't rustfmt-clean; matched surrounding style by hand).
- Ran every build/test/clippy command in the foreground, blocking, in one continuous pass.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test --workspace` — all green (unit, integration, e2e, doctests)
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean
- [x] `fleet_concurrent_add_no_lost_writes` (the roster.rs lock-ordering regression test) — still passes
- [x] `e2e_workdir_symlink_rejected` — still passes against the unified `worktrees_base_dir()`
- [ ] Reviewer: confirm the HOME-resolution semantics note in item 1 is acceptable pre-1.0 (no compat shim was added, per repo convention)

author: pedropaf
body:
Roadmap item 3 from the pod gaps doc — the sync-architecture decision made concrete: **files + sidecar manifests are the sync payload; SQLite is a per-machine rebuildable cache** (same doctrine as `store/index.yaml`).

## What

- **`collect_run_export_files`** (core service): every image artifact ships with its sidecar YAML. Shared by `modl outputs export` (local copy) and the `export.zip` endpoint (ZIP entries keep matching stems so pairs survive unpacking) — so any export can be reconciled on another machine.
- **`reconcile_outputs` + `modl outputs reconcile`**: registers any outputs-tree image that has a sidecar but no artifact row (`import:<sha16>` id, metadata JSON from the sidecar). Idempotent.
- **`import_run_dir`**: lands exported files under `outputs/<date>/` (date from the sidecar's `created_at`), dedupes identical content, suffixes name collisions, then reconciles.
- **Pod `export_run` default**: artifacts now import into `~/.modl/outputs` and appear in `modl outputs` + the web UI — no more orphaned `./pod-outputs/` directory. Explicit `--dest` keeps verbatim copy semantics (now including sidecars). `modl pod pull` gets this automatically.
- **`modl outputs ls`**: falls back to the artifact's own metadata JSON when there's no job row, so reconciled artifacts show prompt/model.
- Cleanup: untracks a pod-output PNG accidentally committed in #114; `pod-outputs/` is now gitignored.

## Verified

- 182 tests pass (new: reconcile idempotency, sidecar-date routing, content dedupe, collision suffixing, sidecar↔metadata JSON round-trip); clippy clean.
- End-to-end with a fresh **z-image-turbo** generation (2 seeds, real GPU): `modl run` → `modl outputs export` produced image+sidecar pairs → copied to a pristine `$HOME` → `modl outputs reconcile` registered both (second run: no-op) → `modl outputs ls` shows prompt + `z-image-turbo`.
- Not live-tested on a pod yet: the pod-side landing (`run --pod`/`pod pull` → outputs import) — the smoke was aborted after repeated Vast host failures. The import path it exercises is the same `import_run_dir` verified above. Retry note: use rtx3090 (cheaper) when smoking.

body:
## What

`canonicalProjectDir()` in both `packages/coding-agent/src/launch/presence.ts` and `packages/coding-agent/src/launch/client.ts` now treats `EISDIR` from `fs.realpath()` as a recoverable error, just like it already does for `ENOENT`.

Also added a regression test (`packages/coding-agent/test/tools/launch-eisdir-fallback.test.ts`) that mocks `fs.realpath` to throw `EISDIR` and verifies `registerDaemonProjectPresence()` still succeeds.

## Why

On Windows, `fs.realpath()` can throw `EISDIR` when called on a drive root such as `R:\`:

```
EISDIR: illegal operation on a directory, lstat 'R:\'
```

The current code only caught `ENOENT`, so starting omp from a Windows drive root crashed during daemon presence registration.

body:
## What
Harden the Architect HITL review-posting guidance so the required attestation can't be paraphrased into a silent gate failure.

- **`.ai/context/workflow.md`** — combine the review header and the fresh-session attestation into a single **verbatim, paste-ready block**, and warn that the `architect-review` check (`hitl-review.yml`) matches **both** lines by literal `contains()` (`HEADER` + `ATTESTATION`). Call out the exact failing paraphrases. Update the "Rules" bullet from "prefix with the header" to "open with the verbatim block — paste, don't reword."
- **`.claude/skills/resume/SKILL.md`** — surface the same verbatim block + literal-match warning at the point of use (step 6), so a review session gets it right without a doc-hop.

## Why
The check matches the attestation string literally, but the docs described it as "the fresh-session attestation" in prose and split header/attestation across two blocks. A reviewer who reworded it to "Fresh-session attestation: …" — reading identically to a human — failed the gate ~4s after posting (observed on PR #107). This makes the exact string unmissable and copy-paste-able.

## Scope / review gate
Docs + skill only — no `src/` changes, so the `architect-review` gate is **exempt**. No behavior change to the engine.

author: marcosborgesphd
body:
This PR improves the `build-guidelines.yml` workflow by avoiding unnecessary tests when they are not needed. This is a first step toward addressing Issue #381.

The goal is not just to save compute time. It is also to avoid running unnecessary jobs that can slow down or block contributors because of unrelated issues elsewhere in the codebase.

## What changed

A `gatekeeper` job now determines whether the checks need to run.

When relevant files change:

- `check-rust-examples` runs
- `build` runs

Otherwise, those jobs are skipped.

> [!WARNING]
> We need to check whether the GitHub branch protection settings accept `build` reporting `success`, `failure`, and now `skipped`.

The `gatekeeper` was chosen instead of `paths` filters to keep the `build` status always reported for PRs. With `paths`, the workflow could be skipped entirely, leaving GitHub without a status to evaluate for merge/branch protection.

The `push` tag trigger was removed since tag builds are already covered by `workflow_call` from `deploy.yml`.

A `force_full_build` input (default: `true`) was added to `workflow_call` allowing `deploy.yml` and `nightly.yml` to bypass the gatekeeper and force a full build when needed.

## Files that trigger a full build

The workflow currently watches the following paths:

* `src/` (kept intentionally broad to avoid edge cases)
* `builder/`
* `exts/`
* `tests/rust-examples/`
* `scripts/extract_rust_examples.py`
* `scripts/migrate_rust_examples.py`
* `.github/workflows/build-guidelines.yml`
* `.github/workflows/check-rust-examples.yml`
* `make.py`
* `spec.lock`
* `pyproject.toml`
* `uv.lock`

There are several dependencies between the build scripts and the documentation, so I’d rather err on the side of running the build than accidentally missing a case. If we discover additional dependencies later, we can easily expand the watched paths.

I’ll keep monitoring the workflow after this lands to make sure there aren’t any unexpected side effects. 😅

author: ortunate
body:
## Summary

This PR remediates the independently audited local Qwen2.5-1.5B QLoRA track and adds a controlled three-variant rerun.

## Root cause and fixes

- Corrects the Qwen preference template so chosen and rejected are rendered as complete conversations with a verified common prompt prefix.
- Adds an independent response-only similarity mask that excludes prompt, padding, role/control tokens, EOS, and template terminators.
- Rejects empty semantic completions instead of producing a clamped pseudo-embedding.
- Preserves chosen-first/rejected-second batch alignment and applies one per-example gamma ratio without duplicate beta scaling.
- Scopes and removes the hidden-state hook safely, detaches captures, clears them per batch, and keeps the static path hook-free.
- Records true per-sample gamma and similarity distributions rather than averaged batch extrema.
- Repairs moved-script repository-root discovery and strengthens generation metadata, adapter verification, judge parsing, retry handling, and budget accounting.

## Controlled rerun

- Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct QLoRA, train 256, eval 64, 100 steps, seed 42.
- Variants:
  - `dynamic_corrected`
  - `static_mean_matched` using the pre-generation realized dynamic mean ratio `0.133509365`
  - `static_original` using ratio `0.25`
- Train/eval loss:
  - dynamic: `0.971552 / 0.975925`
  - mean-matched: `0.977387 / 0.977687`
  - original: `1.087740 / 1.109661`
- All variants had eval reward accuracy `0.4375`.

## Resource results

- PyTorch allocated peak: dynamic `5,316,828,672` bytes; each static variant `5,309,472,256` bytes.
- PyTorch reserved peak: `10,605,297,664` bytes for all three.
- 0.2-second NVML sampled peak: `11,858 MiB` for all three from a `1,439 MiB` initial reading.
- This is reported as no observed additional sampled device peak, not an exact algorithmic VRAM overhead.

## Generation and custom judge

- Independent held-out prompt hashes: 100, with zero normalized exact overlap with train 256 or eval 64.
- Deterministic responses: 300 total, no empty response.
- DeepSeek V4 Flash same-protocol AB/BA evaluation:
  - 600 requests, zero retry, zero invalid response.
  - Actual usage-derived cost: `0.33648752 CNY`.
  - Dynamic vs mean-matched: 6 wins, 3 losses, 73 ties, 18 inconsistent; tie-adjusted `51.83%`.
  - Dynamic vs original: 2 wins, 3 losses, 81 ties, 14 inconsistent; tie-adjusted `49.42%`.
  - Mean-matched vs original: 2 wins, 4 losses, 75 ties, 19 inconsistent; tie-adjusted `48.77%`.

The pre-registered primary comparison is **inconclusive** because unresolved-pair sensitivity can reverse the direction. This is not official AlpacaEval 2, an official win rate, a statistically significant result, or evidence for 8B/full fine-tuning.

## Validation

- 18 lightweight unit/tokenizer/parser tests passed.
- Full corrected 256/64 preprocessing passed.
- Real-model no-grad batch-size-two forward passed.
- Static and dynamic five-step QLoRA smoke runs passed below the 15,000 MiB hard stop.
- All three controlled training runs and deterministic generation completed.
- Audit-bundle SHA-256 manifest verified with zero mismatch.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- No `.env`, credential, model weight, adapter weight, checkpoint, or dataset/cache payload is tracked.

## Audit evidence

The lightweight public audit bundle is under:

`ASPO/artifacts/local_qwen15b/runs/remediation_2026_07/audit_bundle/`

This PR intentionally does not modify legacy L0-L20 reports or raw historical results.

body:
When preserved uint8 model IO is used, SharedQspecQuantizer can merge image-scale tensors with wider internal activation ranges.

Avoid using cat, concatenate, stack, pixel_shuffle, and slice as fallback shared-qspec bridge ops for graphs with uint8 IO. This keeps normal int8 quantisation behaviour unchanged while preserving image input qparams for uint8 IO flows.

Add a regression test covering image-like uint8 IO joined with a high-range branch.

body:
## Summary

Ports the C++11 `json11` library to an idiomatic Rust crate under `rust/` (new `Cargo.toml`, `src/lib.rs`, `src/tests.rs`). The C++ sources are left untouched. `cargo test`, `cargo fmt --check`, and `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` all pass.

The core type is an enum instead of the PIMPL `shared_ptr<JsonValue>` hierarchy:

```rust
pub enum Json {
    Null, Bool(bool), Number(f64), Str(String),
    Array(Vec<Json>), Object(BTreeMap<String, Json>),
}
```

Design notes worth calling out (the rest maps straightforwardly onto the C++):

- **Numbers unified as `f64`.** The C++ `JsonInt`/`JsonDouble` split is dropped; `Json::from(42) == Json::from(42.0)` holds. `dump()` reimplements C's `%.17g` (`format_g`) so integral doubles print as `42`, not `42.0`, and non-finite → `null`.
- **`type()` → `r#type()`** (`type` is a reserved word). `Type` variants are declared in the C++ `Json::Type` order so derived `PartialOrd` matches cross-type ordering.
- **Constructors.** Concrete `From` impls (`f64`, `i32`, `bool`, `&str`, `String`) plus generic `From<Vec<T: Into<Json>>>` and `From<BTreeMap/HashMap<K: Into<String>, V: Into<Json>>>`. A blanket `From<T> for Json` is impossible (conflicts with std's reflexive `From<T> for T`), so the `to_json()` convention is provided via a `ToJson` trait with a blanket `impl<T: Into<Json> + Clone> ToJson for T` — user types get `to_json()` for free by implementing `From<MyType> for Json`.
- **Accessors** return empty defaults on type mismatch (`0.0`, `false`, `""`, `&[]`, empty map) rather than panicking; indexing by `usize`/`&str` returns `&Json::Null` on a miss (a single `static NULL_JSON`).
- **Parser** is a direct port of `JsonParser`, returning `Result<Json, String>` instead of an out-param error. Preserves whitespace/comment strategies, no-leading-zero number rules, `\uXXXX` + UTF-16 surrogate-pair decoding, and `max_depth = 200`. `parse_multi` returns `(Vec<Json>, usize)` (values + stop position).
- **WTF-8 / lone surrogates.** To reproduce json11's byte-exact behavior for lone surrogate escapes (the `test.cpp` unicode roundtrip), parsed strings can hold non-UTF-8 bytes; this is the one spot using `String::from_utf8_unchecked` (parser + `dump`), documented on the public API and in the README.

## Tests

All assertions from `test.cpp` lines 62–253 are ported into `#[test]` functions (simple parse/accessors, comment success + failure cases, container/map conversion equality, object/nested dump strings, number unification, the unicode surrogate roundtrip compared byte-for-byte, `parse_multi` cases, user-defined `to_json`, and `has_shape`). C++ `bool` return of `has_shape` is adapted to `Result<(), String>` (asserted via `is_ok()`/`is_err()`).

README gains a "Rust port" section documenting the API and `cd rust && cargo test`.


Link to Devin session: https://outpostai.devinenterprise.com/sessions/4ac5576221ad4c98993802c83a256b72

author: remcowesterhoud
body:
## Description

<!-- Describe the goal and purpose of this PR. -->

Adds a `kind` enum (`JSON` | `SECRET_REFERENCE`) to `ClusterVariable` across the full stack. The kind determines how the variable value is interpreted at job activation — `SECRET_REFERENCE` values contain `camunda.secrets.X` references that get resolved only when a job is activated. `kind` is settable on create (defaults to `JSON`), immutable after that, stored in both ES/OS and RDBMS, filterable via the search API, and exposed in `CamundaClient`.

The implementation follows the existing `scope` pattern exactly: new `EnumProperty` in the protocol record, `@SinceVersion(8.10.0)` entity field, nullable `KIND` column with `defaultValue="JSON"` in a Liquibase changeset, `ClusterVariableKindFilterProperty` in the CamundaClient, and matching OpenAPI schema components.

One thing that turned out to be a bit more interesting than I'd expected: the ES/OS exporter handler (`ClusterVariableCreatedUpdatedHandler`) runs for both `CREATED` and `UPDATED` intents. On `UPDATED`, the engine record carries `kind=JSON` (the `EnumProperty` default), not the stored value — so naively setting `entity.setKind(...)` on every intent would silently reset any `SECRET_REFERENCE` variable to `JSON` in ES/OS after the first update. Fixed this two ways: 1. Guard `setKind()` to `CREATED` intent only, so the same-batch `CREATED+UPDATED` case doesn't overwrite the kind the `CREATED` record already set. 2. Switch the `UPDATED` path from a full document replace (`batchRequest.add`) to a partial upsert (`batchRequest.upsert`) that excludes `kind`, so cross-batch updates never touch the field in ES/OS. This mirrors what the RDBMS exporter already does by excluding `KIND` from its `UPDATE` SQL.

## Checklist

<!--- Please delete options that are not relevant. -->

[for bug fixes](https://github.com/camunda/camunda/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#backporting-changes), [for CI changes](https://camunda.github.io/camunda/ci/#when-to-backport-ci-changes), or [for documentation changes](https://camunda.github.io/camunda/ci/#documentation-specific-backporting-monorepo-docs-folders)).

author: edoatley
body:
## Summary

Implements `docs/planning/bedrock-coach-structured-output-plan.md`:

- **Structured output**: every Bedrock reply is now constrained server-side to `{aiMessage, revealHint, responseType}` via Bedrock's structured-output feature (`output_config.format` in `invoke` mode, `outputConfig.textFormat` in `converse` mode), eliminating the prose-with-no-JSON fallback class the prompt-only approach couldn't prevent.
- **Prompt-caching fix**: live Bedrock traffic confirmed the real cache-write threshold is 4,096 tokens, not the 1,024/2,048 previously documented — the system prompt was ~3,187 tokens, hence the `cacheRead=0 cacheWrite=0` regression across the whole baseline. Trimmed the now-redundant `OUTPUT FORMAT`/`FINAL REMINDER` prose and re-padded with genuinely useful few-shot examples and context clarifications (~4,274 tokens, confirmed against real Bedrock traffic).
- **`coach.bedrock.api-mode` flag** (`invoke` default, `converse`): both modes enforce the schema identically, so the flag isolates API-surface/caching-mechanism differences from the reliability change. RC workspaces default to `converse` (mirrors the existing `ai_coach_enabled`/`VITE_AI_COACH` is_rc pattern) to validate it before considering it for production.
- **`responseType` categorical field**: an enum (`nudge`/`focus-hint`/`reveal-answer`/`gentle-redirect`/`off-topic-redirect`/`celebrate-progress`/`clarify-technique`) added to the schema, logged in `COACH_RESPONSE` (null on fallback), used only for logging/testing — not part of `CoachResponse`, so no frontend changes. Replaces a flaky coach-quality harness assertion that substring-matched non-deterministic reply prose with a schema-enforced categorical check (`coachResponseType`).

All of the above was live-spiked against real Bedrock (`eu.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0`, `eu-west-2`) before implementation, and this branch has been deployed to RC (`rc-coach-structured-output`) with real production-shaped traffic confirming both structured output and cache hits work end-to-end.

LID docs updated in lockstep: `docs/llds/sudoku-coach.md`, `docs/specs/sudoku-coach-specs.md` (SC-BE-011/012/014/025/026/027/028/029), `docs/specs/coach-quality-specs.md` (CQ-AST-001), arrow tracking.

## Test plan

- [x] `./mvnw test` — 352/352 backend tests passing
- [x] `bash scripts/local/local-alltests.sh --skip-image-recognition` — all suites green
- [x] Live spike against real Bedrock confirming structured output validity, cache write/read, and `enum` schema support (both API modes)
- [x] Deployed to RC branch; real CloudWatch logs confirm `fallback: false` and `cacheReadTokens > 0` in both `invoke` and `converse` mode
- [x] Live harness run (`wrong-guess-acknowledgment` scenario) confirms `responseType: "gentle-redirect"` returned correctly and both assertions pass
- [ ] Coach-quality harness A/B run (`invoke` vs `converse`, ≥110 calls) — not required for this PR, tracked as follow-up in the arrow

author: aallan
body:
## Summary

Closes #1048: indexing directly on a **built-in call result** (`array_concat([10,20],[30,40])[2]`) was check-green but E602-dropped the enclosing function for every element type — the index-expression element-type inference (`_infer_index_element_type_expr`) had a user-function-call arm but no built-in arm. The let-bound form always worked.

## The fix

The FnCall arm gains a built-in fallback (`_builtin_call_ret_named_type`) that reconstructs the call's return `NamedType` from the same shared consultor (`_get_arg_type_info_wasm` + the `_BUILTIN_PARAMETERIZED_RETURNS` table) the sibling Vera-type inference and monomorphizer discovery use — so the three cannot disagree on a builtin's return shape — and feeds it into the same `_alias_array_element` extraction as the user-function arm. Chained indexing on nested-array results (`array_concat([[1,2],[3,4]],[[5,6]])[2][0]`) works through the same round-trip.

## Coverage — stated precisely

Covers the **12** Array-returning builtins the consultor resolves: `array_concat`, `array_append`, `array_slice`, `array_filter`, `array_range`, `string_split`, `string_chars`, `string_lines`, `string_words`, `json_keys`, `md_extract_code_blocks`, `html_query`. The **8** whose element types are type variables (`array_map`, `array_mapi`, `array_flatten`, `array_reverse`, `array_sort_by`, `map_keys`, `map_values`, `set_to_array`) are absent from the consultor tables by design (instantiation-discovery lockstep) — their direct-index form still skips loudly and is tracked separately (see the follow-up issue linked from #1048); the let-bound form works for all of them. String-returning builtins are not index targets (the checker rejects `String` indexing).

## Validation

- **RED-first**: 6 tests (`TestIndexBuiltinCallResult`, `tests/test_codegen_arrays.py`) — four value tests across `array_concat`/`array_range`/`array_slice` and an `Array<String>` element (each RED as an E602 drop before the fix, exact element values), a structural no-E602 pin, and the let-bound control.
- **Mutation-validated**: reverting only the new arm flips exactly the five new tests RED with the control and the file's other 82 tests unaffected; restored, all green.
- **Full pre-commit gate green** on the first attempt (mypy, full pytest, conformance 160/160, examples 38/38, doc gates); counts oracle-reconciled (7,554).

Closes #1048

author: lvschouwen
body:
## #313 — network hardening + cluster-wire HMAC (pre-v2.0.0 security gate)

Closes #313. Hardens the multi-display cluster wire (epic #270) before the v2.0.0 tag. Both the S3 (`Master`) and ESP-01 (`FollowerEsp01`) trees.

### Core hardening
- **CSRF (enforce, not just reflect):** a mutating `POST` with a non-LAN `Origin` is 403'd before the handler (`clusterCsrfRejectPost` / `followerCsrfRejectPost`; ESP-01 fork gates per-handler). The three flash-writing upload routes (`/firmware/master`, `/firmware/rescue`, `/cluster/follower-firmware`) gate CSRF **inline at `index==0`** because the server middleware only fires after the body has streamed.
- **Source-IP binding:** `/cluster/{render,join,ping}` bound to the leader's IP; `/cluster/leave` = leader-IP-OR-LAN-browser combined guard (keeps the local Leave button working).
- **SSRF:** member `host` restricted to LAN targets (`clusterHostIsLanTarget`) + `disable_auto_redirect` on every `esp_http_client`.
- **OTA stall watchdog** on the S3 `/firmware/master` (30 s per-chunk, aborted from `webEndpointsLoop`).
- **NVS/EEPROM flood guard:** `/cluster/join` persists only on real change.

### Cluster-wire HMAC (layer above the IP binding)
- Leader mints a random 256-bit key per member (`esp_random`), sends it at join; the follower persists it and thereafter requires `ts`+`mac` = HMAC-SHA256(key, canonical) on every leader-wire request. Portable public-domain SHA-256 in a **verbatim `ClusterHmac.h` copy** across both trees (RFC-4231 / FIPS-180-4 known-answer tested; one byte-identical host/S3/ESP-01 code path).
- Enforcement **auto-negotiates by key presence** — a pre-HMAC peer falls back to the IP binding.
- **Replay bounded two ways:** a ±30 s NTP window (skipped when unsynced) **AND** a monotonic per-member high-water mark (`ts` must strictly exceed the last accepted). The mark is **persisted coarsely (~1/h)** so a follower reboot doesn't forgive a captured `ping`/`leave`; reset durably on rekey/leave; on the S3 the mark is written **before** the key so a partial NVS write self-heals.
- The **ping mac now covers `sha256(digest)+you`** so the #294 promote-critical piggyback can't be swapped under a valid mac.

### Review
Two adversarial `cpp-reviewer` passes. FIX-2 (digest-signed ping) approved clean. The monotonic-mark reboot residual was found and closed by the coarse persistence; a follow-on review then caught a non-atomic NVS write ordering (new-key-before-reset-mark could strand a wedge) — fixed by writing the mark first. All other items (flash-flood cadence, concurrency, EEPROM layout/checksum, arity, overflow) verified clean.

### Verification
- `pio test -e native`: **Master 700**, **Follower 59**; **pytest 69 / 11 / 7**. Both firmwares build.
- **Bench E2E on hardware:** S3 leader (`.91`) + ESP-01 follower (`.121`) both OTA'd to this build; leader signs → follower enforces → cluster renders the clock with `failures=0 / degraded=false`.

### Notes
- ESP-01 membership blob magic bumped `2FFS`→`3FFS` (+8-byte `lastTs`). No in-field 2FFS blob exists (boards were pre-HMAC), so no migration hazard.
- Follow-up filed: an ESP-01 `/log` endpoint for follower visibility (it has no serial). Out of scope here.
- Also includes `flashing/cluster-ctl.py` — a stdlib CLI used to drive the bench verification (separate commit).

### Test plan
- [x] Native + pytest green
- [x] Both firmwares build
- [x] HMAC E2E on hardware (both nodes enforcing)
- [ ] Soak: confirm no spurious rejects over a longer run / a real leader reboot (key rotation) on the bench

body:
## What

Adds the tenant-creation form to `/platform/tenants`, inside `src/platform/` (its own shell, context, and bearer fetch wrapper — no coupling to the tenant-side app). Pairs with backend **`POST /platform/tenants`** (see backend PR #62).

## Behaviour

- **OWNER + SUPPORT only** — the "New tenant" button is hidden for ENGINEERING / BILLING, mirroring the backend `@PreAuthorize`. The server is the authority; this just avoids showing a button that would 403.
- **No password field, by design.** The backend sets a random password nobody reads and emails the admin a set-your-password link, so support staff never know a customer's password and the UI cannot offer to set one. (A test asserts there is nowhere to type a password.)
- **Success banner** names the tenant, plan, and where the set-up link went — or, when the email failed (`setupLinkSent=false`), tells staff to have the customer use "Forgot password" on the login screen with the workspace identifier.
- **Plan / interval** dropdown (PRO default, BUSINESS available). **Slug** auto-derives from the company name (accent-stripped: "Construcción Ríos & Peña" → `construccion-rios-pena`) until staff edit it. Client-side validation mirrors the backend slug/username rules so the two can't drift.
- Extracts the shared `PlatformModal` + `extractMessage` helpers out of `PlatformTenantDetail` so the two dialogs stay in sync.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
- **369 vitest tests green** (51 files), including a new `CreateTenantDialog` suite (9 cases: no-password guarantee, accent-stripping slug, slug-edit lock, submit payload, plan selection, validation, error surfacing) and a `platformDashboard` service test (asserts the wire contract carries no password).
- **Driven in a real browser** against the live backend (DOM-verified — screenshots are blank in this env): filled the form, submitted, and confirmed a live tenant with an `ACTIVE | MANUAL | PRO | MONTHLY` billing row in the DB, its tenant-side audit row attributed to `PLATFORM` (not the admin).

⚠️ **Do not merge / deploy** — paired with backend PR #62, which merges first (it has the V84 migration).

Implements **T1 (dice engine core)** and **T2 (roll log: table + toast + panel + useRolls)** from the M3 plan ([`docs/specs/2026-07-15-m3-gameplay-foundations-plan.md`](docs/specs/2026-07-15-m3-gameplay-foundations-plan.md)); design rationale in the [design spec](docs/specs/2026-07-15-m3-gameplay-foundations-design.md) §3.

author: galvesribeiro
body:
## What this is

The complete Gen5 (gfx10) → **Metal Shading Language** shader compiler: `SharpEmu.ShaderCompiler.Metal`, the Metal sibling of `SharpEmu.ShaderCompiler.Vulkan`, built on the backend-neutral abstractions from #200 (which is what made this possible without the IVT hacks the original spike needed). It consumes the shared `(Gen5ShaderState, Gen5ShaderEvaluation)` contract out of the neutral decoder/evaluator and emits MSL source text — per the emitter doctrine, it has **no dependency on Metal bindings**: emitters produce text, renderers own APIs (`MTLLibrary` compilation belongs to the future Metal backend).

This is the first deliverable of the macOS-native path I'm owning ([#199](https://github.com/sharpemu/sharpemu/issues/199)): with it, the remaining work to render natively on Metal is the `MetalGuestGpuBackend`/presenter, not shader translation.

## Architecture (mirrors the SPIR-V translator 1:1)

Semantics were ported from `Gen5SpirvTranslator` by reading it as the reference, not from ISA docs — the two codegens cannot disagree on instruction behavior:

- **One GPU invocation = one GCN lane, wave32** — natively the Apple simdgroup width, so the lane model maps *better* than on Vulkan.
- **PC-dispatcher control flow**: GCN basic blocks in a bounded `while/switch` loop (same `SHARPEMU_SHADER_MAX_STEPS` guard), no structured-control-flow reconstruction.
- **Typeless `uint` register file** with `as_type<float>` bitcasts; EXEC/VCC as per-lane bools whose guest-visible mask registers (s106/s107, s126/s127) materialize via `simd_ballot` on read and lane-bit extraction on write.
- **Dominating-scalar-definition dataflow** for buffer and image binding resolution — the same scheme, port for port.
- Where MSL is genuinely better, we use it: shared prelude **functions** instead of SPIR-V's per-site inlining, `device uchar*` casts for unaligned/subdword access, native `half`/`ulong` types.

**Binding contract** (documented on the translator for the backend): global buffers at `[[buffer(base+i)]]` in evaluation order; one `SharpEmuUniforms` constant buffer (dispatch limit + per-buffer byte lengths — Metal has no `OpArrayLength`); textures/samplers at `[[texture/sampler(imageBase+i)]]`; vertex attributes via `MTLVertexDescriptor` from the reflected inputs.

## Coverage (the four entry points, complete)

| Area | Contents |
|---|---|
| **Compute** | dispatch-limit bounds guard, system registers, threadgroup wiring |
| **Pixel** | MRT bindings with Float/Sint/Uint kinds (validated slots/locations), `stage_in` interpolants discovered from V_INTERP, SPI_PS_INPUT_ADDR-ordered input VGPRs from frag coord, compressed + raw exports under EXEC, `discard_fragment()` for killed lanes |
| **Vertex** | `[[attribute]]` fetch interception from evaluated vertex inputs, `[[position]]` + dense zero-filled `user(locn)` params (Metal's exact interface match), `[[vertex_id]]`/`[[instance_id]]`, compressed exports |
| **ALU** | full scalar/vector parity: carry/borrow families, `v_mad_u64_u32`, complete VCmp/VCmpx matrix incl. `class_f32`, full **SDWA** (selects, sign-extend, dst merge) and **DPP16/DPP8** (row ops, mirrors, write-enable masks) via `simd_shuffle`, lane ops (readfirstlane from first EXEC-active lane, readlane/writelane, permlane16/x16), real 64-bit SGPR-pair ops, saveexec families, Sopk/SOPC, f16/pknorm/pkrtz/cube/off_i4 conversions |
| **Memory** | scalar loads, raw + **typed format loads** (128-entry table baked from the shared `Gfx10UnifiedFormat` — decoding stays dynamic since compiled shaders are reused with new SRDs; unorm/snorm/scaled/int/float incl. 10/11-bit mini-floats), D16/D16Hi subdword merges, atomics, runtime buffer biases, range-checked robust access |
| **LDS** | threadgroup memory for compute (usage-gated for occupancy) / private scratch for graphics (the reference's own Metal-motivated trick), full ds_read/write family + ds_add_u32 |
| **Images** | `texture2d<float|int|uint>` (+`access::read_write` for storage), sample matrix (implicit/L/Lz/B/D-gradients), manual PCF compare, per-lane texel offsets folded into normalized coords (Metal requires constant offsets — same workaround the reference uses for Vulkan), gather4 ± compare/offset, clamped loads, bounds-checked stores, resinfo, A16/D16 |
| **Fixed shaders** | `MslFixedShaders`: fullscreen-triangle vertex, copy/solid/attribute fragments, output-free depth-only — the presenter surface, mirroring `SpirvFixedShaders` |

Unsupported opcodes **fail loudly with pc + mnemonic** — gaps are visible, never silently wrong. Deliberately out of scope (backend work): wave64 compute emulation (explicit error), runtime `MTLLibrary`/pipeline plumbing, the `IGuestGpuBackend` implementation.

## Maintainability: static MSL as real files

The static blocks — prelude helpers, format-conversion functions, and all five fixed shaders — are authored as **`Templates/*.msl` embedded resources** (real Metal source: highlighting, reviewable diffs), rendered with a minimal `{{placeholder}}` substituter that fails loudly on unsubstituted tokens. Only per-instruction body emission stays programmatic, where templates can't express the job. The extraction commit is provably behavior-identical: the golden files are byte-for-byte untouched.

Perf note for reviewers: translation runs **once per unique shader and is cached**; emission cost is microseconds against the 10–100 ms `MTLLibrary` compile that follows. The first-use-hitch lever is `MTLBinaryArchive` caching in the future backend, not the emitter.

## Testing (`tests/SharpEmu.ShaderCompiler.Metal.Tests`, self-contained per the per-backend model)

Three tiers, 25 tests:
1. **Golden MSL** — hand-assembled synthetic fixtures (never captured game binaries) drive the real decoder end to end; emitted source is pinned to reviewable `.msl` goldens (regenerate via `SHARPEMU_UPDATE_GOLDENS=1`). Runs on **every platform** — translation is pure text.
2. **Structural** — interface/EXEC/dispatcher assertions per stage; also cross-platform.
3. **Real device** (macOS; no-ops elsewhere so Linux/Windows CI stays green): every fixture + the pixel/vertex/fixed shaders must be **accepted by the OS Metal compiler** (fast-math off, as a real backend must compile), and executable fixtures run on the GPU with **bit-exact assertions** — including the EXEC-masked store that must *not* land, a scalar loop iterating the PC dispatcher, and an LDS write→barrier→read round trip through threadgroup memory.

The macOS CI job runs tier 3 for real on every push.

## Verified

Full Release build zero warnings; all suites green (25 Metal + 83 Libs + 33 SourceGenerators); REUSE-compliant (templates annotated — license headers inside them would leak into every emitted shader).

author: vps-manuel-blum
body:
## Problem

`SelectField` / `FinalFormSelect` has the same class of problem as the multi-select `AutocompleteField` in #5434, in a milder form: the end adornment doesn't wrap (the theme already positions it absolutely), but the select reserves a **fixed** `padding-right` (42px via the `inputAdornedEnd` theme override) while the adornment width varies at runtime. As a result, long values render underneath the icons:

- with error icon + clear button, the text paints **12px under the error icon**
- in the `SelectField` children path (`options` prop), the text paints **6px under the clear button**

## Solution

Same approach as #5434: the adornment container's position is **measured** (`ResizeObserver`) and the distance between the input's right edge and the adornment's left edge is reserved as `padding-right` on the select display, so the value text is always truncated (ellipsis) before the first adornment icon — regardless of which adornments (clear button, error icon) are currently visible.

Both render paths (`children`/`options` prop and `options` + `getOptionLabel`) now build the end adornment the same way. When no adornment is rendered, no padding is overridden and the theme default applies.

## Example

New regression story `components/form/SelectField/MultipleEndAdornment` with 10 cases (long value, many values, required, empty, disabled, error + clear, single-select, children path) and a container-width control to test any width — same setup as the story in #5434, so it can be tested on the deploy preview.

## Open TODOs/questions

- Unrelated pre-existing issue noticed while testing (not fixed here, one PR per change): the custom `renderValue` for multiple selects returns an array of labels, which React renders without separators ("ChocolateStrawberryVanilla"). Should be joined with ", " in a follow-up PR.

## Further information

- Same fix pattern as #5434 (multi-select `AutocompleteField`). Once both are merged, the measurement logic could be extracted into a shared internal hook in a follow-up.
- Verified with a Playwright geometry check at 240/320/505/700/1000px container widths: the text content box never extends under an icon, the menu still opens on click, and the clear button clears and then disappears.

body:
## 背景
前PR(#91)の「体の変化→内側の変化」ルールが「部位ごとに体感→毎回『器ができた』宣言」という機械的反復として解釈されていた。ユーザー提供の元台本（天照巫女）を分析し、実際の変化の運びに準拠して再定義。

## 元台本から抽出した構造
- **お力が体を上から下へ流れる移動＝変化の段階**。部位ごとに解決する内側の課題が異なる：頭＝「私には当たらない」という思い込み（思考）／胸＝諦め（感情）／手＝受け取る機能／腹＝軸・中心／足＝行動と導きの道
- 各部位のミニ構造: 嫌な内面の共感（適宜）→ お力の移動 → 体感確認の問いかけ → その部位のマイナスが抜ける/溶ける描写 → 新しい状態への書き換え（**途中経過の言い方**にとどめる）
- **完成宣言（「削られずに丸ごと届く体」等）は全身が繋がった最後に1回だけ**
- 完成後、流れを固定する日常アクションを1つ授ける（朝「受け取ります」）

## 反映
- create／propose: 変化の過程ルールを上記の段階設計に書き換え。骨組みには「部位×内側の課題×書き換え」の段階リスト明記を必達化
- QC（骨組みC／パートA／全体J）: 段階性の有無を検査。「部位ごとに毎回同じ結論」は段階性の欠如として warn〜fail

author: pacho20
body:
Extends `IBMCloudMachineBootVolume` beyond `encryptionKey` to let machines configure the boot volume's storage `profile`, `sizeGiB`, `iops` and `bandwidth`, and wires these into the VPC instance-create prototype. This lets an administrator configure the boot volume regardless of storage generation, choosing among the available profiles (`general-purpose`, `custom`, and the second-generation `sdp`) and tuning capacity/IOPS/bandwidth instead of always getting IBM Cloud's default `general-purpose` boot volume.

Details:
- This is a non-breaking API change; existing `encryptionKey`-only specs round-trip identically.
- `general-purpose` remains the default when `profile` is omitted, and when the boot-volume config is empty no explicit attachment is sent, so IBM Cloud's defaults apply.
- Boot volume settings are applied at instance creation only and are not reconciled on existing machines (documented in the field godoc).
- Unit tests cover the new fields.

the upstream Cluster API IBM Cloud provider already supports the gen1 storage options and gen2 storage support is being added in kubernetes-sigs/cluster-api-provider-ibmcloud#2811.

Related: https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPCLOUD-3641

author: david-rios-uipath
body: ## Problem The generated `variables.css` (raw color palette, font families like `--font-mono: inconsolata` / `--font-title` / `--font-normal`, `--radius`, …) is scoped to a bare **`:root {}`** block. `:root` only ever matches the document element (``); a shadow root is a `DocumentFragment`, not an element, so **none of these base tokens apply inside a shadow root**. **Scope:** only font tokens are affected. - Shadow-DOM canvas consumers lose `--font-mono`/`--font-title`/`--font-normal` and fall back to Tailwind's generic `ui-monospace` stack (and get no title/body font at all). - Semantic colors are unaffected because they live in class-scoped `body.light` / `.apollo-design.light` blocks that match the theme-class wrapper — only the bare-`:root` base tokens fall through the gap. ## Fix `variables.css` is emitted by Style Dictionary's built-in `css/variables` format, which hardcodes `:root {` (SD v2.8.3 has no `selector` option). Add a small `css/variables-shadow-host` format that **delegates to the built-in formatter and rewrites only the selector to `:root, :host`**, then point `variables.css` at it. `:root` still covers light-DOM consumers; **`:host` matches any shadow host that adopts or injects this sheet**, so the base tokens apply on the host and inherit through the entire shadow tree — including portaled content — with **no `.apollo-design` wrapper required**. In the light DOM `:host` simply matches nothing. ## Demo ### Before ### After ## ap-chat https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2997357e-26fe-435f-9973-f3644957e8aa ## Verification - Generated token body is **byte-identical**; only the selector changes (`:root {` → `:root, :host {`). - **Generated source:** regenerated `variables.css` diff is exactly one line — `:root {` → `:root, :host {`. - **Compiled artifact:** rebuilt `apollo-react` through the full chain — the base-token block (palette + `--font-mono:inconsolata` + `--font-title`/`--font-normal`) is now `:root, :host {…}`. - **Live shadow root:** confirmed in a real browser that `--font-mono` resolves to `inconsolata` inside the shadow root (traceview WC and ap-chat) — with no wrapper and no runtime selector rewriting — while semantic `--color-background`/`--color-foreground` resolve on both the container and the portal. Downstream, this lets shadow-DOM consumers drop client-side `:root` → `:host` rewrite workarounds. ap-chat now adopts `variables.css`/`theme-variables.css` raw (commits on this branch). _Alternative considered: `:root, .apollo-design`, scoping to the documented Pattern-B wrapper class (and working in a light-DOM subtree without touching `:root`). Chose `:root, :host` because it needs no wrapper, covers portaled/shadow content mounted outside a wrapper, and lets `:host`-based consumers (ap-chat) drop their runtime selector rewrites._

author: briananderson1222
body:
Closes #134.

## What

`flow capture <run-id> --gate <gate> --kind command [--timeout <ms>] [--cwd <path>] -- <cmd...>` — executes at capture time (argv-exact, no shell), writes a canonical receipt (`schemas/command-evidence.schema.json`: command, exit code, bounded stdout/stderr with truncation accounting, duration, sha256), and attaches it **through the existing `attachEvidence` path** so the immutable-snapshot, atomicity, and gate-visit-scoping semantics are inherited unchanged. Exit-code-derived status (`0 → passed`, else `failed`); the command's exit code propagates. `flow evaluate` remains passive — no execution at evaluate time (diff touches no gate/evaluate code; regression-tested).

Robustness (from the review's fix round): async spawn in a detached process group with SIGTERM→(5s grace)→SIGKILL group escalation, so SIGTERM-trapping commands and grandchildren cannot outlive `--timeout`; run + gate validated **before** spawning (a bad gate id never executes the command); attach failure after execution preserves the receipt and prints its path; valueless `--timeout/--cwd/--kind/--gate` rejected up front. Docs cover the 1 MiB read-back budget, unbounded on-disk spool during execution, and UTF-8-decoded hash/truncation semantics.

## Evidence

- Full suite: node 244/244 (was 237 pre-change), browser 25 pass / 7 intentional skips, typecheck + docs:check green.
- Orchestrator live probes (independent of the implementer): SIGTERM-trapping child under `--timeout 1000` returns in 6.1s wall clock with a correct SIGKILL receipt; bogus gate → command not executed; valueless `--timeout` → rejected, nothing attached; happy path pass/fail → correct status + exit propagation; receipts land in the standard manifest with sha256, indistinguishable in shape from hand-attached evidence.

## Review trail

Independent report-only review round 1: **NOT-READY** (timeout not enforced for SIGTERM-trapping commands; execute-before-validate + receipt destruction; valueless `--timeout` → false failed evidence; grandchild survival). All four fixed in a resumed implementation round; review round 2 re-probed each and verdicts **MERGE-READY-WITH-NITS**.

Disclosed non-blocking nits (follow-up material, not absorbed): paused-run lifecycle is not pre-checked (capture executes, then attach fails with the receipt preserved — known, tested behavior); `detached: true` means Ctrl+C does not reach the command's process group (no SIGINT forwarding); the spawn-error path relies on Node emitting `close` after a failed spawn (probed working; worth an explicit finish-on-error). Not verified: Windows behavior (group-kill test skipped there by design).

Provenance: field-tested gap from a live Flow-Agents production run (2026-07) — every gate's evidence was pasted by hand across 12 delivery cycles. Implemented by Codex delegate; orchestrated, gated, and published by Claude.

author: vieiralucas
body: ## Summary Behavior-only client/tool-compatibility fixes from the bug-hunt (batch 6). - **EKS OIDC issuer missing region (1.9, MED).** `DescribeCluster` returned an OIDC issuer of `https://oidc.eks.amazonaws.com/id/`, but real AWS scopes it to the cluster's region: `https://oidc.eks..amazonaws.com/id/`. Tools that parse the region from the host (eksctl IRSA, Terraform `aws_iam_openid_connect_provider { url = ...oidc[0].issuer }`) broke on non-default regions. The region is now taken from the cluster's ARN (which records the request region). - **SQS QueueUrl hardcoded localhost, ignored Host (1.10, MED, framework compat).** The returned `QueueUrl` was built from the static boot-time endpoint (`http://localhost:`), so in docker-compose/remote setups where the app reaches fakecloud as `http://fakecloud:4566`, the URL was unreachable and frameworks that treat the QueueUrl as the endpoint (Celery/kombu, Spring Cloud AWS) broke. Host resolution now honors, in priority order: (1) a new `FAKECLOUD_EXTERNAL_URL` override, (2) the request `Host` header (scheme from `X-Forwarded-Proto`, else `http`), (3) the static boot-time endpoint. Applied to CreateQueue / GetQueueUrl / ListQueues, plus ListDeadLetterSourceQueues and the `/_fakecloud/sqs/messages` introspection view so every client-facing URL stays consistent. The **stored** queue identity stays host-independent (`resolve_queue_url` still accepts any host on the way back in), and the default with no override and no Host header stays `http://localhost:`. - **SQS attribute-name loop capped at 20 (1.13, LOW).** Query-protocol `Get/SetQueueAttributes` enumerated `AttributeName.N` / `Attribute.N.Name-Value` with a hardcoded `1..=20`; SQS now exposes ~22 attributes, so a client enumerating >20 individual names lost the tail. Now enumerates contiguously, stopping at the first absent index. - **ECS RunTask group=None (1.12, LOW).** A bare `RunTask` left `group = null`; real AWS assigns `group = "family:"`. Service/daemon tasks were already correct. Now defaulted when the request omits `group`. ## New env var `FAKECLOUD_EXTERNAL_URL` — external base URL rendered into returned SQS QueueUrls (docker-compose/remote setups). Documented in `website/content/docs/reference/configuration.md`. ## Test plan - `cargo clippy -p fakecloud-eks -p fakecloud-sqs -p fakecloud-ecs -p fakecloud --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo fmt`. - Unit tests added: EKS describe-cluster issuer includes region (across 3 regions); SQS QueueUrl reflects Host header / `FAKECLOUD_EXTERNAL_URL` override and defaults to localhost without either; host-independent lookup still resolves; >20 individual attribute names all returned + contiguous-stop; `render_queue_url` pure-fn tests; ECS RunTask group defaults to `family:` and preserves an explicit group. - `cargo nextest run -p fakecloud-sqs -p fakecloud-eks -p fakecloud-ecs`: 570 passed. - `cargo nextest run -p fakecloud-e2e --test sqs`: 42 passed (includes the introspection round-trip that exercises the host-aware rendering end-to-end). - ECS e2e RunTask tests are Docker-gated and could not run in this sandbox (unreachable Docker daemon; `docker info` hangs, same on main); the RunTask group behavior is covered by the two new unit tests. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes AWS-compat gaps across EKS, SQS, and ECS: region-scoped EKS OIDC issuer, host-aware SQS `QueueUrl` rendering (including DLQ sources and introspection), contiguous SQS attribute parsing, and a default ECS `RunTask` group. Also stabilizes SQS external-URL override handling for deterministic behavior in shared-process runs. - **Bug Fixes** - EKS: `DescribeCluster` OIDC issuer now includes the region (e.g., `https://oidc.eks..amazonaws.com/id/`), matching AWS. - SQS: Returned `QueueUrl` now honors, in order: `FAKECLOUD_EXTERNAL_URL`, request Host (scheme from `X-Forwarded-Proto`), then localhost fallback. Applied to CreateQueue, GetQueueUrl, ListQueues (including paginated results), ListDeadLetterSourceQueues, and `/_fakecloud/sqs/messages`. Stored queue identity stays host-agnostic. - SQS: Query-protocol attribute enumeration no longer caps at 20; reads contiguous `AttributeName.N` and `Attribute.N.*` entries until the first gap. - SQS: Cache `FAKECLOUD_EXTERNAL_URL` once at startup and expose a pure resolver to avoid per-request env races in shared-process tests; production behavior is unchanged. - ECS: `RunTask` defaults `group` to `family:` when omitted, matching AWS. - **Migration** - Optional: set `FAKECLOUD_EXTERNAL_URL` (e.g., `http://fakecloud:4566`) so clients in docker/compose or remote environments receive routable SQS `QueueUrl`s. No change needed for localhost setups. Written for commit 309d33399a47e65fe2725e1227dd359cee00ce10. Summary will update on new commits.

author: lanegarner
body:
## Summary
Root-cause fixes for the workout-loss incident after account switching:

- **Merge**: a server tombstone (`deleted_at`) previously deleted the local copy unconditionally; now it only wins when the tombstone is newer than the local edit — the same last-write-wins rule the rest of the merge uses. A months-old stale deletion can no longer destroy newer local changes.
- **Sign-out**: now flushes the pending sync queue before wiping local data (`flushPendingSync`), and if the upload fails, warns that unsynced changes will be discarded instead of silently dropping them.

Pairs with a backend fix (already on main) where pushing a live edit to a soft-deleted server row left the stale `deleted_at` in place (`undefined` stripped from the update) — edits can now resurrect tombstoned rows.

## Test plan
- [ ] Soft-delete a row server-side with an old timestamp, edit the same activity locally → local edit survives sync and resurrects the server row
- [ ] Make an offline change → sign out → confirms flush; with airplane mode, shows the "changes haven't synced" warning with Cancel / Sign Out Anyway
- [ ] Normal sign-out with empty queue is unchanged

| Ruling | Implementation |
|---|---|
| Cap exhaustion = deterministic prefix, `truncated:true`, not a refusal | Full discovery → min-size filter → sort (label, first-seen gen, chain_id) → prefix at cap; `header.truncation={"kind":"component_cap",…}` |

| Truncation consistency | Header-level `truncated`+`truncation` = artifact state; per-finding `truncated` = record-level content, constantly `false` in S1 (both defined; validator enforces) |

author: michael-tiller
body:
## Why

The dirigible2D M5.1 phase-4 world-object event smoke detonated a wildcard content graph (`magic_amulet_events`: empty-DomainFilter GenericGameEventMessage subscription + PublishEventActionNode). Two incidents:

1. **Hard editor crash** — synchronous re-entrant routing (GameMessageBroker.Publish → GraphEventRouter.RouteAsync → GraphRunner.HandleMessageAsync → publish → …) recursed 1,139 iterations to stack overflow/OOM. No managed exception ever logged.
2. **Livelock** — with a depth guard in place, the republish re-enters frame-deferred at depth 0 every hop: main thread spins, 10 MB/min log storm, editor unusable.

`MaxExecutionSteps` cannot help: each re-trigger counts as a fresh execution.

## What

- **`GraphEventRouter.MaxRouteDepth` (16)** — synchronous depth budget; drops with an Error log at the cap, unwinds via `finally`. Catches self-loops and A→B→A ping-pong on one call chain.
- **Dispatch-rate watchdog (100/runner/1s → 5s suspension)** — catches every loop shape including fully-async ones. Per-runner; never blocks other graphs; one Error log per suspension; injectable `TimeProvider` for deterministic tests.
- **`GraphRunner` entry-node gating** — entry nodes declaring `MessageType`/`DomainFilter` in `Parameters` only start for matching dispatches. Previously every entry node fired on any subscribed message (trigger A's chain ran for trigger B's event — the loop's ignition path). Undeclared entries keep legacy fire-on-dispatch.

## Verification

- VisualGraphs runtime EditMode suite **59/59** (7 new tests: depth cap + unwind, watchdog suspend/resume/isolation, entry type/domain gating).
- Live in dirigible2D: previously-crashing door smoke now runs clean — zero loop entries, quest graph receives door events via exact domain match (see dirigible feat/m5-1-wo-event-attachment).

author: hieplam
body:
## Description

The owner's merge rule changed to **"Do not Squash merge"**, but three implementations never followed it — so the repo shipped **two mutually exclusive Definitions of Done at once**. `verify-shipped` asserted a 1-parent squash while the campaign runner's D3 point 2 requires 2 parents; they could never both pass on the same PR. This fixes all of them and adds a C3 rule so the contract is checkable instead of prose repeated in three places.

## What was broken

| Artifact | Encoded | Consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `verify-shipped` script | `if [[ "$PARENT_COUNT" != "1" ]]; then FAIL` | **Failed PR #37** — the owner's own correctly-merged PR |
| tribe agents (12 sites) | "Squash-merge into the default branch once green" | A Warchief would squash every card; the runner then rejects it → every card escalates → campaign wedges on card one |
| `c3-217` doc | "PR merged, squash strategy" | Described the stale rule |

## Verification

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `verify-shipped --pr 37` (real 2-parent merge) | **PASS** — failed before this PR |
| `verify-shipped --pr 33` (a real squash merge in this repo's history) | **FAIL**, naming the rule |
| `grep -rn -i squash plugins/tribe/agents/` | every surviving hit is a deliberate prohibition; zero instructions to squash |
| `bun test` (runner) | 116 pass / 0 fail |
| `c3x check --only c3-215` / `--only c3-217` | ok: true; both now cite `rule-no-squash-merge` |

## Design choices

- The rule's **Golden Example is the runner's real `checkTwoParents` code** — ask `git rev-list --parents` for the parent count, never infer the shape from a commit title (the old squash `(#N)` heuristic is removed).
- **Output-contract change:** `verify-shipped`'s JSON check id `merge_strategy_squash` → `merge_strategy_no_squash`. Nothing else in the repo consumes that key.
- The rule's Override offers no in-repo escape: changing the merge shape requires changing the owner's global rule, then one change-unit updating the rule **and every implementation in its Scope together** — updating one at a time is exactly what caused this drift.

**Merge with a regular merge — not squash.**

## What

The multicluster operator plane exists solely to run Stretch Clusters — the layered CR controllers registered in multicluster mode (`operator/cmd/multicluster/multicluster.go`) reconcile resources whose `clusterRef` targets a StretchCluster. But the help text only said "Redpanda multicluster deployments", which doesn't tell users what the commands are for, and collides with the docs' use of "multi-cluster deployment" for independent clusters with async replication (Shadowing).

The docs pipeline also generates the `rpk k8s` reference pages from this help output (see redpanda-data/docs#1681), so aligning the source text keeps the CLI and published docs consistent without doc-side overrides. Em dashes are banned by the docs style guide, hence the two punctuation fixes.

body:
Two code-level hardening fixes from the CapDeck security review.

## Changes

**1. `Scripts/build-release.sh` — block distributing ad-hoc builds**
Ad-hoc builds disable library validation (needed for Sparkle's nested helpers to run unsigned), which weakens code-injection protection. The script previously always packaged a distributable `.zip` + checksum, so such a build could reach users. It now refuses to archive an ad-hoc build unless explicitly opted into with `CAPDECK_ALLOW_ADHOC_ARCHIVE=1` for local testing. Developer ID release builds are unaffected.

**2. `CapDeck/Models/FilenamePattern.swift` — reject hidden filenames**
Adds a `.leadingDot` validation error so a pattern that renders to a hidden file (leading `.`) is rejected, with test coverage.

## Verification

## Summary
- **Past dates blocked**: Start/End Date inputs now have `min` set to today's local date, and `handleSaveEvent` defensively re-checks both dates server-side (native date-input `min` isn't reliably enforced across all browsers for typed/pasted values).
- **Typo-prone time entry replaced**: Start/End Time free-text inputs replaced with hour (1-12) / minute (00-59) / AM-PM dropdowns. All parsing/comparison is done on plain strings (`YYYY-MM-DD` dates, `"H:MM AM/PM"` times) — no `Date` object is ever constructed, so there's no UTC/local timezone shift risk.
- **Required fields enforced**: Title, Description, Date, Start Time, End Time, Venue Address, Venue City, Venue State, and Event Image are now all required before insert/update (both "Save as Draft" and "Submit for Review"), with a single toast listing every missing field by name.
- **End-after-start validation**: submission is blocked with a clear error if End Time is earlier than or equal to Start Time on the same effective date. A later explicit End Date is treated as a multi-day event and skips this check.
- **Moderation flow unchanged**: `handleSaveEvent`'s status assignment (`draft`/`pending`) is untouched — new validation runs strictly before it.

## Scope
- `src/pages/PartnerDashboard.tsx`, `src/lib/partnerEventValidation.ts` (new) only.
- No changes to App.tsx, Admin.tsx, AuthCallback.tsx, PartnerMember.tsx, Header.tsx, UserAccountMenu.tsx.
- No SQL/RLS/storage changes.
- No ingestion, worker, dispatcher, cron, event pipeline, legacy scrape functions, Admin Statistics, or Production changes.

## Google Maps (Scope B — diagnosed, deferred)
Confirmed no existing Google Maps/Places integration (no API key env var, no dependency, no autocomplete/map component — only a static `maps.google.com` link in `EventDetailModal.tsx`). Not implemented here per instruction to defer unless already configured. Recommended as a separate future PR: Places Autocomplete (New) + Static Maps preview, `VITE_GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY` restricted by HTTP referrer, billing enabled on the GCP project.

## Test plan
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- [x] `npm run build` — succeeded
- [x] Browser-verified: homepage loads with no console errors (shared-bundle regression check)
- [ ] Manual retest as a real logged-in partner: past date rejected, incomplete form blocked with correct missing-field list, end-time-before-start-time blocked, full valid submission reaches "Pending Review"

###  Tracing logging user input may result in poisoning logs with ANSI escape sequences
[CVE-2025-58160](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-58160) / [GHSA-xwfj-jgwm-7wp5](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-xwfj-jgwm-7wp5)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Impact

Previous versions of tracing-subscriber were vulnerable to ANSI escape sequence injection attacks. Untrusted user input containing ANSI escape sequences could be injected into terminal output when logged, potentially allowing attackers to:

- Manipulate terminal title bars
- Clear screens or modify terminal display
- Potentially mislead users through terminal manipulation

In isolation, impact is minimal, however security issues have been found in terminal emulators that enabled an attacker to use ANSI escape sequences via logs to exploit vulnerabilities in the terminal emulator.

##### Patches

`tracing-subscriber` version 0.3.20 fixes this vulnerability by escaping ANSI control characters in when writing events to destinations that may be printed to the terminal.

##### Workarounds

Avoid printing logs to terminal emulators without escaping ANSI control sequences.

##### References

https://www.packetlabs.net/posts/weaponizing-ansi-escape-sequences/

##### Acknowledgments

We would like to thank [zefr0x](http://github.com/zefr0x) who responsibly reported the issue at `security@tokio.rs`.

If you believe you have found a security vulnerability in any tokio-rs project, please email us at `security@tokio.rs`.

author: tishow
body:
## 概要

タブレットで譜面を横スクロールしづらい問題（先生要望、#85）への対応。**自前の太い常時表示スクロールバー**をグリッド下に追加しました。

## 背景・原因

- グリッドの各セルが `touch-action: none` でブラウザ標準の指スクロールを無効化 → 一本指では原理的にスクロール不可（必ず二本指が必要）
- 二本指スクロールも自前実装で慣性なし・両指をグリッド上に置く必要・音符入力と競合
- 標準バーは細く自動非表示、しかも **iPad Safari では CSS で太くできない**（`::-webkit-scrollbar` 無効）

## 実装

`GridScrollbar` コンポーネントを新規追加し、グリッド下に常時表示。標準バーは非表示化。

- **一本指でツマミをドラッグ／トラックをタップ**して移動。大きな当たり判定、音符入力ハンドラと非干渉
- `container.scrollLeft` を読み書きするだけ → 二本指スクロール・再生追従と自動同期。操作時は `measure()` を同期呼び出しして指に吸い付く
- ツマミ幅は表示範囲に比例（最小48px）。曲が収まる場合はトラック全幅＋淡色で非ドラッグ
- `role="scrollbar"` ＋ `aria-controls`/`aria-valuenow`。丸ピル、light/dark 対応
- 二本指スクロールは維持（後退なし・追加のみ）

## 検証

- `tsc --noEmit` クリーン / `pnpm lint` クリーン / vitest 57 passed
- プレビュー（tablet 768幅、grid 2616px > viewport 720px で横溢れ）実測:
  - バー描画: 高さ18px、`role=scrollbar`、`aria-controls=grid-scroll-area`、標準バー非表示（`scrollbar-width: none`）
  - ツマミドラッグ +200px → `scrollLeft` 727 / `translateX(200px)` / `aria-valuenow` 38、戻し -120px → 291 / 80px / 15（比例一致）
  - トラック90%タップ → `scrollLeft` 最大1896 / 右端 / 100
  - 音符入力の回帰なし（空セルクリックで音符追加を確認）
- スクリーンショットで丸ピルの見た目・配置を確認

Closes #85

## What changed

- `displayLines []string` → `displayBlocks []displayBlock{kind, raw}`, rendered per frame at the viewport's current width (`renderBlock` in `refreshViewport`). History semantics untouched — blocks are display-only, raw markdown stays in blocks and history alike.
- Fixed `headerView` pinned above the viewport (`● tutor · <model> · <mode>` left, dim endpoint + Ctrl-D hint right, dim rule) replaces the banner transcript entry; `recomputeLayout` accounts for its two rows; narrow panes drop the endpoint half and truncate instead of wrapping.
- `you ›` echo prefix restyled (dim "you", bold pink `›`); input prompt becomes a teal `›` and the input rule dims to `#1E5A5A`.
- New `palette.go` holds every pane color once; markdown escapes now derive from it.

## Why

The pane's styling had accumulated per feature with hardcoded escapes at each point of use and a session banner that scrolled away. One palette, one render pipeline, and a persistent header make it read as a designed surface — and the render-at-width refactor is the structural prerequisite for the editor-card code blocks (#117).

Verified: full test suite green (banner tests ported to header assertions, new header pinning/truncation tests); live OpenRouter session shows the header with exact palette escapes, styled echo, teal prompt; resizing 100→60 cols re-flows the transcript and truncates the header without wrapping.

Closes #116

author: keyaigit
body:
## What

`Ecdlp/Proved/P256TwistSecurity.lean` — the NIST P-256 companion of the secp256k1 twist certificate (#168), completing the cross-curve `x`-only / point-validation limitation picture for both curves of the repo.

The number `2p + 2 − n` for P-256 factors **exactly**:
```
2p + 2 − n = 3 · 5 · 13 · 179 · Q,     Q a 241-bit prime.
```

- **`p256_twist_order_factorization`** — the identity above (`native_decide`).
- **`p256_twist_maxprime_prime`** — `Nat.Prime Q` via a full recursive **Pratt certificate** (`lucas_primality`, witness `a = 3`, 10 nodes; `scripts/pratt_certificate.py` machinery).
- **`p256_twist_security_profile`** — factorization ∧ `Nat.Prime Q` ∧ `2²⁴⁰ < Q < 2²⁴¹` ∧ nontrivial cofactor `3·5·13·179 = 34905 ≈ 2¹⁵`.

## Honest scope (stated in the docstring and ledger row)

Interpreting `2p+2−n` as the twist order `#Ẽ = p+1+t` rests on `#E(𝔽_p) = n` — which for P-256 this repo has **not** proved (only `n ∣ #E` is in-repo, `P256Cardinality.lean`; the full count is parked on the Hasse bound, see `BARRIERS.md`). The theorems themselves are **unconditional arithmetic about the literal number**; the conditionality lives only in the interpretation, and is labeled.

## Consequences

1. **The twist is not prime-order** — cofactor `≈2¹⁵` gives genuine small-order subgroups a twist point can be confined to.
2. **Twist security is below the curve's** — generic twist-DLP `≈ √Q ≈ 2¹²⁰ < 2¹²⁸`: the machine-checked form of the publicly tabulated ~2^120.3 P-256 twist-security figure.
3. **Cross-curve comparison now certified:** secp256k1's twist (`≈2¹¹⁰`, cofactor `≈2³⁷`) is *weaker* than P-256's (`≈2¹²⁰`, cofactor `2¹⁵`) — both below `2¹²⁸`, so point validation stays mandatory for `x`-only code on either curve.

## Verification

Python pre-verification passed (Pratt `CERT_OK`, factorization product, bit bounds, completeness of the small-factor sieve); a 4-lens adversarial workflow (Pratt-tree re-derivation from the `.lean` text, arithmetic from repo constants, honesty audit, structure/collision check) is in flight — wiring (`Ecdlp.lean` import, `AxiomAudit`, `VERIFIED.md` row, canonical count bump) lands after its verdicts. The Lean kernel verdict is CI on this PR. No new axioms beyond compiler-trusted `Lean.ofReduceBool`.

**Coordination note:** independent of the in-flight torsion PRs (#172/#173/#174) — different file, different math; only the mechanical shared surfaces (count line, import list, generated artifacts) overlap, resolved by merge order.

author: nstarman
body:
Adds a scheduled **Weekly CI** workflow, modeled on the [`quax`](https://github.com/patrick-kidger/quax) reference repo, that quax-blocks currently lacks.

Every Monday (and on-demand via `workflow_dispatch`) it runs the test suite against:
- **newest stable** deps (`uv sync --group tests --upgrade`), and
- **pre-release** deps (`--upgrade --prerelease=allow`, i.e. alpha/beta/rc/nightly)

across Python 3.12 / 3.13 / 3.14, gated by an `alls-green` status check. This surfaces breakage from upstream `jax`/`quax`/`optype`/etc. releases before it lands in a tagged version — complementing the per-PR `newest-supported` job in `ci.yml`.

Actions are SHA-pinned to match the versions used elsewhere in the repo (`checkout@v7.0.0`, `setup-uv@v8.2.0`, `alls-green@v1.2.2`). Validated against the GitHub-workflows JSON schema.

> [!NOTE]
> The `3.12` floor assumes #18 (which raises the minimum Python to 3.12). If this merges first, the matrix can trivially include 3.11.
