author: gilbert09
body:
## Problem

After the direct-query migration, the DWH source/schema views still named concrete source types in five more families: xmin gating, GitHub multi-repo reconciliation, custom-source OAuth/manifest/limits, and SQL schema reconciliation. This PR migrates all of them, driving the source-agnostic guard baseline to **zero**.

## Changes

> [!NOTE]
> Stacked on #71558 (direct-query) → #71543 (guard). Review those first. Behaviour-preserving throughout. One commit per family.

Each family moves to whichever mechanism fits the concern (per `presentation/README.md`):

- **xmin** → a `supports_xmin` flag on `_BaseSource` (Postgres sets it True). The views read `SourceRegistry.get_source(...).supports_xmin`.
- **Server-managed job inputs** (Custom's `auth_oauth2_integration_id` pointer, GitHub's legacy `repository` marker) → `_BaseSource.server_managed_job_input_fields(incoming, existing)`; Custom and GitHub override it.
- **GitHub multi-repo reconciliation** → a `data_warehouse` namespaced-resource registry (`namespaced_resources.py`) keyed on source type, with a GitHub adapter wrapping the existing repo helpers. The view dispatches via `get_namespaced_resource_adapter(source_type)`.
- **Custom source** (per-team cap, manifest-host gate, row-backed OAuth2 credential-preservation gate, post-create integration-row claim) → capabilities on `_BaseSource` (`max_instances_per_team`, `job_inputs_add_connection_host`, `has_preserved_row_backed_credentials`, `on_source_created`) implemented on `CustomSource`, which owns `CustomOAuth2Integration`. The per-team cap now generalizes to any capped source type.
- **SQL schema reconciliation** → extends the direct-query engine adapter with `reconcile_schemas` (all four engines) and `refresh_name_substitutions` (Postgres only; `None` elsewhere).

The last commit regenerates the guard baseline to empty. It's now a hard regression check: any new `ExternalDataSourceType.<NAME>` / `is_direct_<engine>` in the presentation layer fails CI.

Subtlety worth a reviewer's eye: `is_multi_schema_capable_sql_source` = {Postgres, **MSSQL**, Snowflake, Redshift}, which differs from the `direct_engine` set {Postgres, **MySQL**, Snowflake, Redshift}. So the Postgres name-substitution uses a `None`-vs-`{}` sentinel: only Postgres returns a dict (handled, suppresses the generic path); the other engines return `None` and fall through to the already-source-agnostic `is_multi_schema_capable` migration, which still covers MSSQL. Traced per engine to preserve exact behaviour.

## How did you test this code?

- Extended `test/test_direct_query_engines.py` (20 cases): adds the `refresh_name_substitutions` `None`-sentinel for non-Postgres engines. All pass.
- Verified each capability resolves via the facade.
- `ruff`, `tach`, import-linter (`presentation must use facade` KEPT), and `oxfmt` all pass. The guard passes on the empty baseline and fails when a probe `ExternalDataSourceType.POSTGRES` reference is added.
- The `tests/api/` end-to-end suites can't run in my local env (pre-existing Python 3.12-vs-3.13 conftest mismatch, unrelated). CI runs them.

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?
- [ ] Alert Sales and Marketing teams?

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

I directed this with Claude Code (Opus 4.8), continuing the source-agnostic sweep to completion. Each family picked the lightest mechanism that fit: a flag where a boolean sufficed, a source method where behaviour depended on the source, an engine/registry adapter where the work was `data_warehouse`-domain (touched `DataWarehouseTable`/schema rows). The main correctness risk was the reconciliation family's MSSQL-vs-MySQL set mismatch, handled with the `None` sentinel and traced per engine. Skill invoked: `implementing-warehouse-sources`.

author: pmatos
body:
## Terminal-native dashboard redesign Rebuilds the daemon's server-rendered web dashboard (`/`, `/runs`, `/runs/:id`) from bare `system-ui` tables into a calm, **terminal-native operator console** — the "Calm Terminal" direction captured in `DESIGN.md`. It's a visual/markup refresh only: no framework, no client build, no new runtime dependency, and every existing label, link, and HTML-escape is preserved. ### Light & dark The terminal character is *structural* (mono type, density, hairlines), so it holds in both themes — system-adaptive via `prefers-color-scheme`, each tuned in OKLCH. | Light | Dark | |---|---| | ![Dashboard, light](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pmatos/symphonika/dashboard-shots/shots/dashboard-light.png) | ![Dashboard, dark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pmatos/symphonika/dashboard-shots/shots/dashboard-dark.png) | ### Run detail & mobile Run detail renders as definition-list field panels + state tables; the layout collapses cleanly at mobile widths (tables scroll inside their own container, no body overflow). | Run detail (dark) | Mobile (390px) | |---|---| | ![Run detail](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pmatos/symphonika/dashboard-shots/shots/run-detail-dark.png) | ![Mobile](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pmatos/symphonika/dashboard-shots/shots/dashboard-mobile.png) | ### What changed - **`src/http/pages.ts`** — a new inline design system in `layout()`: OKLCH token scale, light + dark themes, mono-forward type, flat surfaces (tonal layering + hairlines, no shadows), section headers with count badges, and a **run-state pill** vocabulary. State is always **text + colour** (never colour alone). The amber / red / green triad is reserved for run state; one cool accent carries links, selection, focus, and the Cancel action. Empty states now teach the domain. - **`src/http/fonts.ts`** *(new)* — **IBM Plex Mono** (SIL OFL, weights 400/500/600, Latin subset) embedded as base64 and served from an immutable `/assets/fonts/*` route. This keeps the daemon fully **self-contained and offline** (no Google Fonts / CDN fetch) and matches the project's existing convention of shipping asset content as TS constants (the build is `tsc`-only). It also removes the `favicon.ico` 404 via an inline SVG icon. - **`PRODUCT.md` / `DESIGN.md`** *(new)* — the strategic + visual design contract this PR implements, produced via the design flow. Happy to split these out if you'd rather keep them separate from the code change. - **`tests/http-app-runs.test.ts`** — the one assertion that pinned the *old* terminal-reason markup (`

…`) is updated to the new definition-list structure. Behaviour is unchanged; the cap-context assertion still passes as-is. ### Testing - `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build` — all pass. - `npm test` — 576 tests; the only red was the known-flaky `dispatch-project-disable` test, which passes on isolated re-run (this change touches only HTTP rendering). - Verified in a headless browser against a fixture-backed preview server: light, dark, run detail, and mobile (390px), plus the `/assets/fonts` route and HTML escaping. ### Notes - Screenshots are hosted on the throwaway `dashboard-shots` branch (not part of this PR's diff), so no binaries land in `main`.

Deployment automation, application security, observability, and frontend CI remain outside this issue.

author: 99yash
body:
## Problem

`x.com` (and other client-rendered SPAs) serve a 200 `text/html` shell that's almost all `<script>`. `fetch_url` extracted no text and returned `ok: true, chars: 0` — **indistinguishable from a page that genuinely has nothing**. The boss read "I couldn't read this" as "there's nothing here" and silently fell back to grounded web_search (a lagged, second-hand proxy), producing stale answers — e.g. the roast-slide thread where it got Dax Raad's bio wrong and only corrected after the user pushed back.

## Change

Two halves that reconcile: the honest signal is the trigger the live-read path escalates from.

**#509 — honest empty signal.** `runFetchUrlImpl` returns a new `empty_content` `FetchUrlError` when the page `looksHtml`, extracted text is `< 20` non-whitespace chars, but the raw HTML was `>= 500` bytes (a JS shell). Plain-text and small legitimately-empty pages are exempt. The boss now gets a distinct, greppable signal to relay or pivot on instead of treating silence as absence.

**#510 — live read via render escalation.** On `empty_content`, `runFetchUrl` re-fetches the **same URL** through a headless render+extract pass (Firecrawl `/v1/scrape`). This is **general, not per-host** — it also fixes LinkedIn and other SPAs. If no renderer is configured or it still comes back empty, the honest `empty_content` stands.

> The issue proposed a Nitter mirror list. I probed it live: only `nitter.net` still works today; public instances rot. A render/extract service is the SOTA path production LLM apps use and doesn't rot — so `fetch_url` escalates to Firecrawl instead.

### Notes
- **SSRF-safe:** escalation only fires on `empty_content`, which the direct fetch only returns *after* `safeRequest` already resolved + connect-pinned the host (and every redirect hop) to a public IP. A blocked/private host errors as `blocked_host` upstream and never reaches the renderer.
- **Config:** new optional `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY`; `FIRECRAWL_BASE_URL` (default `https://api.firecrawl.dev`) makes the OSS self-hosted Firecrawl a config swap. Already set on Railway `server`/`production` (skip-deploys → applies on next deploy).
- **No prompt-patching:** the tool *description* is the lever — it now tells the boss `fetch_url` reads X/JS pages, so it prefers it over web_search for "what's in his bio / read his tweets".
- Renderer is an injectable `deps.render` seam for hermetic tests.

## Verification

Live, with a real key:
- `fetch_url("https://x.com/thdxr")` → **current** bio via Firecrawl: *"building @opencode at @anomalyco / not the ceo"* (2046 chars markdown, latest tweets, followers).
- `fetch_url("https://x.com/thdxr")` with **no** key → `empty_content` (honest), not silent `ok:chars:0`.
- Normal page (`yashk.xyz`) unaffected.

Automated: +5 unit tests (empty_content flag, small-page exemption, escalation returns rendered text, honest fallback when renderer empty, no-escalate on readable pages). Full suite **1356 api tests pass**; `check-types` and `check:web-boundaries` clean.

Closes #509
Closes #510

author: andste82
body:
Answers the four questions about the sessile container build by closing the gaps it surfaced.

## What was missing
- `make docker` existed, but **CI never built the Dockerfile** — a broken image stayed green until someone built it by hand.
- **The container was never tested.** The `HEALTHCHECK` is runtime-only; no pipeline reads it.
- No release automation at all.

## What this adds
**`scripts/smoke-docker.sh`** — runs an image against a temp workspace, waits on its own HEALTHCHECK as the readiness signal, then checks `/api/health`, the embedded SPA, `/api/config`, creates a real pty session, lists it, deletes it, and greps the logs for panics. Runnable locally: `scripts/smoke-docker.sh sessile:dev`.

**`ci.yml`** — new `docker` job builds the image and smoke-tests it on every PR. Single-arch with gha cache; the release does the multi-arch push.

**`release.yml`** — triggered by `git push origin v0.2.0`. No workflow commits to master.
1. `version` — derives `0.2.0` from the tag; every job stamps that same value, so binary, image tag and release name cannot drift.
2. `binaries` — matrix over linux/darwin x amd64/arm64.
3. `image` — multi-arch (amd64+arm64 via QEMU) pushed to `ghcr.io/andste82/sessile:<version>` and `:latest`, authenticated with the built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN`.
4. `verify-image` — pulls the pushed image back and smoke-tests it before the release is published.
5. `release` — uploads binaries + `checksums.txt` with pull instructions.

## Verified locally

author: amagiddmxh
body:
## Why

Spool keeps one installed `better-sqlite3` binary and switches it between the Node and Electron ABIs. Two parts of that workflow were costly or fragile:

- The root `pretest` rebuilt the Node addon unconditionally, even when the installed binary already matched the current Node ABI.
- `with-electron-native.mjs` used synchronous child processes, so an interrupt could terminate the wrapper before its Node-ABI restoration completed.

## What changed

- Probe `better-sqlite3` with a real in-memory query before rebuilding for Node; rebuild only when the load/query fails.
- Run the Electron rebuild, wrapped command, and Node restoration asynchronously.
- Forward `SIGHUP`, `SIGINT`, and `SIGTERM` to the active child while keeping the wrapper alive long enough to restore the Node ABI.
- Preserve signal-style exit codes after restoration.
- Remove obsolete npm runtime/target environment overrides from the Node rebuild.
- Update contributor and development documentation to match the managed ABI workflow.

## Verification

- A matching Node ABI took 1.91 seconds through `pnpm run ensure:native:node` and skipped compilation.
- A real Electron-ABI switch followed by Ctrl-C completed the Node rebuild; `better-sqlite3` then loaded successfully under Node ABI 137 and executed an in-memory query.
- Both scripts passed `node --check` and focused Oxlint.
- Workspace typecheck, type-aware lint, core tests (417 passed, 1 skipped), and app tests (450 passed) completed successfully.
- The full local `pnpm check` reached the CLI suite, where 56/60 tests passed; four multi-process pin/unpin tests exceeded their existing 5-second timeout on this host. No timeout was changed or relaxed; PR CI remains the confirmation for those tests.

author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body:
### Why This Change is Necessary
Currently, our continuous integration validation checks do not require workspace packages to maintain standard documentation files. This has allowed several packages to be merged without local `README.md` or `CHANGELOG.md` files, and without proper references in the repository's main changelog. This lack of standardization leads to poor package discoverability, incomplete package releases, and friction during developer onboarding.

By integrating strict, automated documentation assertions directly into our existing validation suite, we prevent non-compliant packages from being merged into the main branch.

---

### Key Decisions & Rationale
1. **Lightweight Validation inside `scripts/validate_docs.py`:** Rather than introducing a complex external linter or adding a new step to our CI workflow, we integrated the new checks directly into the existing `validate_docs.py` script. This keeps CI execution fast and simplifies local verification.
2. **Simple Pattern Matching for Main Changelog:** Parsing changelog structures can be highly brittle. To assert that each package is mentioned in the central root `CHANGELOG.md`, we implemented a straightforward string-matching pattern check. This confirms package registration without introducing fragile parsing logic.
3. **Graceful Compliance Backfilling:** To avoid breaking current checks, we backfilled missing documentation for existing packages (like `plugins-sinks`, `plugins-workflows`, and `providers-airflow`) using standardized, consistent headers matching current compliant packages.

---

### What Changed
* **Validation Script (`scripts/validate_docs.py`):**
  * Added `check_package_docs()` to the main execution flow.
  * Asserts that every package directory under `packages/` contains its own local `README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`.
  * Verifies that each package (by name or directory) is explicitly referenced in the root `CHANGELOG.md`.
* **Root `CHANGELOG.md`:**
  * Updated to include explicit references to all five active workspace packages (`imednet`, `imednet-plugins-sinks`, `imednet-streamlit`, `imednet-workflows`, `apache-airflow-providers-imednet`).
* **Documentation Backfills:**
  * Created `packages/plugins-sinks/README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`.
  * Created `packages/plugins-workflows/README.md`.
  * Created `packages/providers-airflow/README.md`.

---

### Verification Results
* Running `python scripts/validate_docs.py` locally succeeds now that all placeholder documentation has been added.
* Manually deleting a required local asset (e.g., `packages/plugins-sinks/README.md`) or removing a package reference from the central changelog successfully triggers a validation failure, ensuring the CI guardrails will perform as expected.

author: kiseratimon
body:
### 1. src/com/flashcrash/agents/NoiseTrader.java
Wakes up at random intervals (technically: a Poisson process, the standard statistical model for *"random arrivals over time,"* like customers walking into a shop), and 70% of the time places a small resting order near the current price, 30% of the time crosses the spread immediately (an aggressive trade). **Depends on**: `sim` (implements Agent), `core` (submits Orders to the OrderBook). **Definition of done**: running the engine with only noise traders produces a gently wandering price with steady trading volume and no directional trend.

### 2. src/com/flashcrash/agents/MomentumTrader.java
Tracks a short-term and a longer-term moving average of price; when the short-term average pulls far enough away from the long-term one, it aggressively trades in that direction. **Depends on**: `sim`, `core`. **Definition of done**: introducing a handful of these into an otherwise-calm noise -trader-only market visibly amplifies any price move that starts to trend

## 3. src/com/flashcrash/agents/HFTMarketMaker.java
Computes a *"reservation price"* that shifts away from the market mid-price in proportion to how much inventory the agent is currently holding, quotes a buy and a sell around that reservation price, and refreshes those quotes very frequently. Also enforces a hard cap on inventory; past that cap, it stops adding to the position and instead sells (or buys) aggressively to get back under the limit. **Depends on**: `sim`, `core`. **Definition of done**: This file caused the worst bug in the whole project. Getting the inventory-skew math even slightly too aggressive causes the reservation price to run away toward zero (or below), because more inventory → bigger skew → still more selling pressure → still more inventory, with nothing to stop it

### 4. src/com/flashcrash/agents/LargeSeller.java
Holds a total quantity to sell and a target participation rate (e.g. *"never be more than 9% of recent trading volume"*); periodically checks how much volume has traded since it started, computes how many contracts it *"should"* have sold by now to hit that percentage, and sells the difference as an aggressive market order. **Depends on**: `sim`, `core`. **Definition of done**: given a fixed total quantity and participation rate, the agent sells its entire position by the end of a run, and its realized participation rate (executed quantity ÷ total market volume during its active window) stays close to the configured target

### 5. src/com/flashcrash/agents/FundamentalValueProcess.java
This file creates that *"true value"* as its own slowly -wandering random process, mathematically an `Ornstein-Uhlenbeck` process (a standard way to model a quantity that drifts randomly but is pulled back toward a long-run average), numerically simulated using a standard technique called `Euler-Maruyama` integration
On a fixed schedule, nudges a shared *"fundamental value"* number up or down using the `Euler-Maruyama` formula, and writes it into `SimulationContext.fundamentalValue` for other agents to read. **Depends on**: `sim` (writes into SimulationContext). **Definition of done**: run it alone (no other agents reading the value) and plot `fundamentalValue` over time — it should wander gently around its starting point, never explode or go negative

### 6. src/com/flashcrash/agents/ValueTrader.java.
This is the agent that actually uses the fundamental value from the previous branch. It compares the live market price to the fundamental value; if the market price has fallen well below fundamental value, it buys (more aggressively the bigger the gap); if price has risen well above, it sells. This is what gives the simulated crash somewhere to stop and bounce back from, mirroring the real event's rapid rebound
**Depends on**: `FundamentalValueProcess`, `sim`, `core`. **Definition of done**: in a full run including the large seller, the price stops falling and recovers noticeably instead of continuing toward zero

### Problem (beta.8 bug)

The smoke test surfaced a false-negative in beta.8: sub-task s1 "write docs/SMOKE.md" was always marked `failed_verification` even when the worker correctly wrote the file. ## Summary

Enables running the 64-step Metal backend generation (shader compilation + optimization) on max-2 (M5 Max 48GB) directly from Claude Code CLI, reducing execution time from ~23m (devAir) to ~12-15m expected.

**Three new files:**
- `tools/run-metal-backend-remote.sh` — 64-step Metal generation script with performance metrics capture
- `.claude/launch.json` — CLI launcher definitions for local and remote (SSH) execution  
- `CLAUDE.md` — Complete setup and execution guide with troubleshooting

## What it does

The script:
1. Verifies 30B GGUF present (`~/ds5-models/qwen3-30b-a3b-instruct-2507-gguf/`)
2. Confirms repo at latest main (PR #21 fix required)
3. Builds Zig project (`zig build`)
4. Runs 64 Metal shader compilation steps
5. Captures: duration, step success/failure rate, hardware (CPU/memory), speedup vs. devAir baseline (~1400s)

Output: metrics saved to `bench/results/metal-generation-TIMESTAMP/metal-generation-report.txt` on target node.

## Usage

From dev machine via Claude Code CLI:

```bash
# Local execution (devAir 24GB, ~23m)
claude run metal-backend-generation

# Remote execution on max-2 (48GB, ~12-15m expected)
claude run metal-backend-generation-max-2
```

### First-time setup (one-time, ~5-10m)

Copy 30B GGUF from dev machine to max-2:

body:
## Summary

Fifth PR of the perf series (#2294 #2295 #2296 #2297) — first half of the remaining `String#[](Int)` sweep, covering shared utils + miniparsers. Crystal's `String#[](Int)` re-seeks from byte 0 on every access once the content holds a multi-byte UTF-8 char, so whole-span index loops were **O(n²) on non-ASCII sources**.

- **`utils/groovy_literal_scanner.cr`** — generalized over an indexed char source: `String` (existing callers, unchanged behavior) or `Array(Char)`. All four `grails.cr` call sites and the Groovy callee extractor already materialize a chars array for their own scan loops (from an earlier fix) but still passed the `String` down — the scanner itself was the remaining quadratic hotspot. They now pass the chars array.
- **`miniparsers/groovy_callee_extractor.cr`** — `strip_non_code` + `append_blanks*` walk a materialized chars array (whole method body per call).
- **`miniparsers/js_http_route_extractor.cr`** — `split_top_level` / `normalized_arg` / `arrow_params` / `find_open_paren_backward` walk chars arrays; they scan argument spans at **absolute file offsets**, making them O(span × file) on non-ASCII `node:http` sources.

## Regression testing

- New unit specs pin the `Array(Char)` overload against the `String` overload **across every position** of a non-ASCII snippet, plus multi-byte quoted/slashy cases

author: bkearns
body:
## Problem — why PR #264 (a docs-only PR) went red

`three_node_cluster_elects_raft_leader` failed on #264's CI run with the candidate stuck at **term=1 for 30 s** while both peers stayed Learners. #264 can't have caused it — the race is in main's formation code, and the same mechanism bit the live dev cluster on 2026-07-16 (an AppendEntries retry loop erroring `unknown peer: 00000000-…` every 500 ms for hours, never healing even after its peers came back — forge t_05acdc8a item 4).

**Root cause:** openraft caches one network client per target, and `FerrosRaftNetworkFactory::new_client` resolved the `node_id → host_id` mapping **once at construction**. A client built before `register_node` landed froze `Uuid::nil()` forever — openraft's backoff retries through the same frozen client, so the unreachability is permanent. In the formation race, the seed initializes raft before its peers' registrations land; its Vote RPCs are unroutable, nobody ever hears an election, and the 30 s deadline expires. The old test `factory_unknown_node_yields_nil` was *pinning the bug*.

## Fix

The client now stores the target node_id plus the shared registration map and resolves on **every RPC** (an uncontended `RwLock` read — noise next to a network round-trip). An unregistered target maps to `openraft::Unreachable`, so openraft backs off, and the retry succeeds as soon as `register_node` lands (formation loop or membership observer). A late registration heals the existing client instead of requiring a process restart.

## Verification

- New pin `late_registration_heals_existing_client`: a client created before registration must observe the mapping afterwards — fails against the old frozen-at-construction design.
- `factory_unknown_node_yields_nil` (which asserted the buggy nil bake-in) replaced by `factory_unknown_node_is_unresolved`.
- `cluster_formation` suite green locally, including the test that failed on #264's run; full ferrosa-cluster lib suite green (1059); fmt/clippy clean.
- A 12-iteration formation-race harness under 6-way CPU pressure: green on this branch (the race is timing-dependent and reproduces on starved CI runners; the mechanism is proven by the code + CI log + live incident).

After this merges, #264 should be rebased onto main so its checks run with the fix in — its own diff is docs-only and was never the problem.

author: japerr
body:
Fixes #151.

Entities silently stop updating after a few hours while still showing "online", only reloading the integration recovers it. The access token expires mid-session causing python-socketio's built-in reconnection keeps retrying with the original (now expired) bearer token and never refreshes it, the namespace connect is rejected forever. Meanwhile the coordinator blocks in _async_disconnect() waiting on that reconnect task, so it never raises UpdateFailed and entities just keep their last value.

The fix disables python-socketio's native reconnection and lets the coordinator own reconnection, so every attempt runs _connect() (the only path that can refresh the token). The token is refreshed proactively when it's expired/near expiry, and _async_disconnect() is bounded so a stuck teardown can't hang an update. Transient connection errors (e.g. a 5xx during the websocket handshake) are treated as temporary, UpdateFailed + retry, instead of triggering a token refresh, and a genuinely invalid refresh token (4xx) now raises ConfigEntryAuthFailed to start HA's reauth flow. The emit loop is also guarded against the brief window during a reconnect where the socket client is None, which was crashing the background task.

author: mergify[bot]
body:
### What

`DefaultComparableLooseVersion` (`orca/orca-core`) mis-orders versions that have different numbers of components, and violates the comparator's antisymmetry contract.

`parse()` pads each version into a fixed `Integer[4]`, so `"1.2"` becomes `[1, 2, null, null]`. `compareTo` compares components with `>` / `<`; unboxing a `null` pad throws an NPE that is swallowed by `catch (Exception e) { return -1; }`. As a result:

- `compare("1.2.3", "1.2")` returns `-1` (should be positive)
- `compare("1.2", "1.2.3")` also returns `-1`

So a genuine library **upgrade** `1.2 → 1.2.3` is reported as a **downgrade** in the JarDiffs report (`LibraryDiffTool.calculateLibraryDiffs` maps `1` → upgraded, `-1` → downgraded), and the comparator is not antisymmetric.

### Why it's wrong

The class documents itself as a *"Groovy implementation of python LooseVersion class"* — in Python `LooseVersion("1.2.3") > LooseVersion("1.2")`. The existing `LibraryDiffSpec` never caught this because every case it covers compares equal-length versions, which never hit the `null` pad.

### Fix

Treat a missing component as `0` (Python pads absent trailing components), so a shorter version orders below its longer prefix, instead of letting a swallowed NPE force `-1`.

### Testing

Added `DefaultComparableLooseVersionTest` covering equal-length comparisons (unchanged), differing component counts, and antisymmetry. The new cases fail on `main` and pass with the fix; the existing `LibraryDiffSpec` still passes.

author: unforced
body:
## Summary

Build task S2 from the contract-drift brief (§3). `queryNotesCursor` in `packages/surface-client/src/vault-client.ts` was broken against **both** doors — pagination silently stopped after page 1 everywhere. Plus a housekeeping rider: retiring a GitHub Pages deploy workflow that's been shipping to a dead target since the `notes.parachute.computer` cutover.

## Part 1 — the cursor fix (commit 1)

Grounded against the real wire contract on both doors (not just the brief):
- bun: `parachute-vault/src/routes.ts:1383-1394` (presence-based cursor mode + bootstrap) and `:1729-1735` (`{notes, next_cursor}` envelope emission)
- cloud: `parachute-cloud/workers/vault/src/rest/notes.ts:256-268,379-383` (same presence-based gate) and `rest/parse.ts:50-53` (`X-Next-Cursor` — an ADDITIVE cloud-only mirror; bun never emits it)
- exclusivity: `parachute-vault/core/src/notes.ts:1320-1338` (`cursor` + `orderBy`/`sort:"desc"` → `INVALID_QUERY`)

Three compounding bugs, all in `queryNotesCursor` / `requestCursorWithRetry`:

1. **Bootstrap gap** (`:567` old) — `if (cursor) qs.set("cursor", cursor)` never sent `?cursor=` on the first call. Cursor mode is **presence-based** on both doors: an entirely-omitted `cursor` param never engages the envelope, so page 1 could never obtain a watermark. **Fixed**: every call now does `qs.set("cursor", cursor ?? "")`.
2. **Envelope not parsed** (`:643` old) — `const items = (await res.json()) as Note[]` cast the whole body to an array, but cursor mode answers `{notes, next_cursor}` on both doors. **Fixed**: the body is parsed as the envelope (with a defensive bare-array fallback for a server that ignores `cursor`).
3. **Wrong cursor source** (`:644` old) — read `X-Next-Cursor`, a header the self-hosted bun vault **never emits** (only cloud mirrors the same body field, additively). **Fixed**: `next_cursor` is read from the body first; the header is now only a fallback for a response whose body omits it.

Also added a client-side guard: `orderBy` or `sort: "desc"` alongside `cursor` always 400s server-side (`INVALID_QUERY` — cursor mode forces ascending `updated_at` order), so `queryNotesCursor` now throws that synchronously instead of spending a round trip on it.

**Wire-visible changes** (called out per the compatibility note): `queryNotesCursor` requests now always carry a `cursor` param (previously omitted on the bootstrap call), and its body-parsing changed from "cast to `Note[]`" to "parse the envelope." The **types** are unchanged (`{ items: Note[]; nextCursor?: string }`) — this API was demonstrably broken in practice (pagination never worked), so the runtime-behavior fix is the point. `queryNotes` (the non-cursor path) is untouched — same request shape, same bare-array response, byte-compatible; pinned by a new test.

### Tests (`src/__tests__/vault-client.test.ts`)

- Bootstrap: page 1 (no `cursor` arg) sends `?cursor=` (empty, present)
- Envelope parsing: `{notes, next_cursor}` body → correct `items`/`nextCursor`
- Header fallback only when body omits `next_cursor`; body wins over a stale header
- Final page (`next_cursor: null`) ends the loop
- **Full pagination walk**: page 1 (no cursor) → envelope w/ `next_cursor` → page 2 (`?cursor=`) → final page (`next_cursor: null`) → loop ends
- Auth-retry (401 → refresh → retry) preserves the cursor through the envelope path
- Guard tests: `orderBy` and `sort: "desc"` alongside cursor both throw client-side; `sort: "asc"` (the forced order) is allowed
- New test pinning `queryNotes` (non-cursor) never sends a `cursor` param and stays byte-compatible

Updated two pre-existing tests that encoded the old (broken) contract — mocked bare arrays + `X-Next-Cursor` header instead of the real envelope — to match ground truth; one test that combined `cursor` + `sort: "desc"` (a combination that's actually invalid per the wire contract) now uses a valid combination.

## Part 2 — housekeeping rider (commit 2)

Removed `.github/workflows/deploy-notes-ui.yml` (fired again on today's merge to main). `notes.parachute.computer` is now a 301 redirect worker on Cloudflare (`parachute-cloud/workers/notes-redirect`) — the GitHub Pages target is DNS-shadowed and unreachable, so the workflow was building+deploying to a dead target on every push touching `notes-ui`/`surface-client`. `notes-ui` package itself is untouched.

## Version

`surface-client` 0.3.5 → 0.3.6 (stable patch, no rc — repo convention). CHANGELOG updated.

## Gates (literal verdicts)

- `bun run --filter "@openparachute/surface-client" test`: **310 pass, 0 fail**
- Root `bun run test` (surface-host + surface-client + account-client + surface-server + pebble-config + doc-schema + docs-editor + meeting-ingest + meeting-mcp + notes-ui + surface-render): **1607 + 1140 + 61 = 2808 tests, 0 fail** (one notes-ui route test flaked on a prior run — `App > catch-all redirects to the root list` — confirmed pre-existing/unrelated: passes in isolation and on a clean re-run of the full suite; notes-ui package is untouched by this PR)
- `bun run typecheck`: **exit 0**
- `bun run typecheck:all`: **exit 0**
- `bun run lint`: **26 errors / 8 warnings — identical count on clean `main` before this PR** (verified via `git stash`); zero new lint errors introduced (the one formatting issue in my own new test code was fixed before commit)
- `bun run build:surface-client`: **exit 0** (prebuild regenerates `src/version.ts` → confirmed `0.3.6`)

## Which of the brief's 3 claims survived contact with the code

All three survived verification against the actual vault/cloud source (not just the brief's citations), with one clarification: the brief's own wording on bug (1) was slightly ambiguous ("never bootstraps... on the first call" vs "never sends... on subsequent calls") — ground truth is that cursor mode is **presence**-based, so the bug is specifically that `qs.set("cursor", cursor)` under `if (cursor)` skips the param entirely whenever `cursor` is falsy, which includes both the first call (undefined) and any manual re-bootstrap with `""`. The fix (`qs.set("cursor", cursor ?? "")` unconditionally) closes both readings at once.

author: andygrove
body:
# Which issue does this PR close?

Closes #2067.

 # Rationale for this change

A `UNION ALL` over file scans silently returned **inflated** results — no error,
just several times too much data:

```sql
select round(sum(p),2) from
 (select ws_ext_sales_price p from web_sales
  union all
  select cs_ext_sales_price p from catalog_sales);
-- expected 5492796521.50
-- got     49389026433.70   (--partitions 16, executor -c 8; varied run to run)
```

A task executes one partition of its stage, so `restrict_scan_to_partition` pins
each file scan beneath it to the single file group that partition reads.
Without that, DataFusion 54's shared work-queue lets a lone `execute(p)` drain
the queue and scan the whole table (#1907).

The pinning applied the stage's partition number **directly to every scan**,
which is only correct when the partition passes straight through. A `UnionExec`
concatenates its children's partitions: with N-partition children, stage
partition `N + k` is the right child's local partition `k`. So:

- for partitions inside the left child, the right child's scan was pinned to the
  wrong group (harmless — it is never polled), and
- for partitions `>= N`, `partition_id >= config.file_groups.len()` bailed out
  and returned `None`, leaving that scan **unrestricted** and free to read its
  entire table.

`restrict_scan_to_partition`'s own doc comment anticipated exactly this case:

> Returns `None` ... for a `partition_id` outside the source's file groups (e.g.
> when an operator between the scan and the stage output changed the partition
> count).

Confirmed by disabling the trigger from the other side: the query was correct
whenever the union stage's tasks fitted in a single wave of executor slots
(so nothing was left half-polled), and wrong beyond it. Moving the executor from
`-c 8` to `-c 32` moved the failure threshold from 8 to 32 tasks exactly.

# What changes are included in this PR?

- Add `restrict_scans_for_partition`, which walks the plan from the stage root
  and mirrors `UnionExec::execute`'s own partition arithmetic, so each scan is
  pinned to the group its **local** partition reads. Children a partition never
  reaches are left untouched — this task does not execute them. Every other
  operator passes the partition straight through, as before.
- Split the scan restriction out of the `ShuffleReaderExec` rewrite, which is
  partition-independent.
- Un-skip TPC-DS q2 and q5 in the correctness gate.

## Verification

The minimal case above is now correct at **every** partition count tried — 4, 5,
6, 8, 16, 20, 32 — where previously anything past one wave of task slots was
wrong.

Full SF1 TPC-DS gate: **88/88 verified** against single-process DataFusion, both
on a single executor and across 2 executors. `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo
clippy --all-targets --workspace -- -D warnings`, and `cargo fmt --all` are
clean. New unit tests pin the union mapping, including the case that previously
left a scan unrestricted.

## Note on q2 / q5

Both were skipped as "non-deterministic (ORDER BY ties; varies run-to-run)".
That diagnosis was wrong: with a total order imposed and `LIMIT` removed they
still mismatched, so they were real wrong results, not tie ambiguity — they were
hitting this bug. Both now verify in their original form across repeated runs.
q31 and q71 *are* genuinely ordering-only (both verify once a total order is
imposed) and stay skipped.

# Are there any user-facing changes?

Yes — `UNION ALL` over file scans now returns correct results instead of
silently inflated ones. No API changes.

author: opentendril
body:
## What

The scoped-ci gofmt step ran `gofmt -l .`. gofmt is **not module-aware** — handed a directory it recurses everything under it — so it walked nested checkouts of *other* modules that happen to live in the workspace and failed the step on their unformatted code.

The effect: `stem sequence scoped-ci` was unusable in a working tree hosting such a directory. `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` passed, gofmt failed, and the reported reason had nothing to do with the change:

```
❌ scoped-ci verdict: FAILED — step verifier-gofmt failed
unformatted Go files:
  <other-module>/cmd/stem/internal/rhizome/parser.go
  <other-module>/cmd/stem/internal/telemetry/resin.go
  ...
```

Build and vet were fine because `./...` already means "this module". Only gofmt, a plain filesystem walker, had no such notion.

## How

The gofmt step now derives its file set the same way build and vet do: ask `go list` which directories belong to the module, and let gofmt recurse those. Nested modules are excluded automatically, because they are not this module's packages.

Fail closed on an unusable answer: `go list` failing aborts the script via `set -e`, and an empty package list exits non-zero rather than let a gofmt that examined no files report success.

Deliberately derived, not declared. A maintained list of directories to scan (or to exclude) is fail-open the moment the tree moves on without it — the same reasoning that made scoped-ci detect skips instead of maintaining a "these need Docker" list.

## The CI step had the mirror-image defect

```yaml
unformatted=$(gofmt -l cmd/stem roots | grep -v '^cmd/stem/dist' || true)
```

A declared list that had already drifted in both directions: it **missed `cmd/sprout-agent` entirely** (not under `cmd/stem`), and it filtered `cmd/stem/dist`, **a directory that no longer exists**. So the local tier scanned too much and the remote tier scanned too little.

Both now run the same derived check, so the two tiers agree on what "formatted" means.

## Verification

Run in the working tree that reproduced the bug — a checkout hosting a nested module.

Before: `verifier-gofmt` failed, listing the other module's files.

After:

```
🔬 go build ./... — PASSED (exit 0)
🔬 go vet ./... — PASSED (exit 0)
🔬 <gofmt check> — PASSED (exit 0)
```

Committed, the change's own scoped-ci verdict is:

```
⛔ scoped-ci verdict: BLOCKED — 5 applicable test(s) skipped and were not verified
```

BLOCKED on the pre-existing environmental skips for the packages in scope (`cmd/stem`, `conductor`, `receptors`): network-or-credential tests and Docker-daemon liveness tests. None are introduced here, and the scope narrowing is working correctly — `terrarium` is untouched by this change, so the 6 firecracker/`/dev/kvm` skips are correctly absent. See #287 for the full measurement.

Coverage was checked rather than assumed: across this module the derived file set and a full walk of the tree resolve to the **same 198 `.go` files**, so nothing is lost by scoping to the module.

## Tests

The existing assertion (`gofmt -l` present, `exit 1` present) passed both before and after, so it would not have caught this. Strengthened to assert the script does not walk the workspace, derives its set from `go list`, and fails closed on an empty package list.

author: zechim-dev
body:
Follow-up to #18 (already merged). Makes `benchmark_progress_report.py` the single report and fixes GLM cost to the real Modal bill.

## What changed

**One cost method, pinned to the real bill.** GLM per-run cost was priced "sole" (own generation-seconds × rate, as if alone on the endpoint), over-counting the shared GPU-seconds by the concurrency factor (~5×). Now the real Modal bill (`billing.json`) is split across runs by per-instant concurrency (`attribute_cost`) — a run that ran mostly alone keeps more of the bill than one buried in a pack — with the rate pinned so the GLM total reconciles to the bill **to the cent**. Opus stays per-token.

**Single self-contained report file.** Inlined the engine (was `aggregate.py`) and the Modal biller (was `billing.py`, now in-process `refresh_billing()`) into `benchmark_progress_report.py`; **deleted both**. No more two tools that can drift into different numbers. Dockerfile/requirements/README updated (they were never used in-image — the image runs `run_deepswe`; reporting is local).

**Restored Eduardo's CSVs**, now built from the report's own verified numbers so they finally agree with the HTML:
- `per_run.csv` — `task,setup,run,passed,billed_usd,sole_usd,elapsed_s,steps,tokens_in/out`
- `summary.csv` — per-setup runs/passes, run + pass@k rates, total/avg/$per-pass-run/$per-task-solved, total_sole_usd, cost_basis

**Column rename** `$/pass` → `$/pass run` (denominator is passing *runs*, not tasks — keeps the top table's per-task `$/solve` unambiguous).

**Console UX** — `main()` prints a 5-step staged log; tables live in the HTML + CSVs. `sync-and-report.sh` gets a matching log and tolerates tar exit-1 (mid-run "file changed as we read it").

## Correctness

`verify_report.py` — an independent gate that recomputes from the raw files (manifest, reward.json, billing.json, output.log), not the report's internals:
- synthetic concurrency fixture (hand-computed \$15/\$5 split)
- run/pass counts vs disk; manifest `status` == `reward.json` (0 mismatches)
- GLM attributed total == real bill to the cent
- no run billed above its sole cost; Opus untouched
- `per_run.csv` GLM billed sums to the bill; `summary.total_usd` == `per_run` sum per setup

**All 15 checks pass** on the current 365-run set (bill \$561.11, GLM reconciles exactly).

## Known follow-up
`attribute_cost` is an O(points×intervals) sweep (~47s at 365 runs, minutes at full scale) — can be made O(n log n) later.

author: neilobremski
body:
## Summary

- bump the app to v1.36.0 (versionCode 42)
- replace the ambiguous nickname grammar with `/nicknames add <nickname> for <agent>`
- normalize nickname, agent, and direct `/tell` targets to lowercase
- prevent nickname mappings from claiming or overriding known canonical device/principal names
- require explicit `replace` for an existing nickname and reject multiword/reserved nicknames
- add enable/disable/status and filtered-list nickname actions
- correlate `/tell` resolution, MQTT client acceptance, broker acknowledgment/failure, retry, and broker loopback by envelope ULID
- distinguish a queued disconnected publish from a configuration with no MQTT remotes
- catch and surface exceptions from asynchronous command handlers without logging message bodies or credentials

## Root cause

Issue #54 was not an MQTT publication regression. The v1.35 nickname grammar made the argument order easy to reverse. Handset evidence showed a canonical node name saved as a nickname for a misspelled destination. `/tell` then correctly published to that misspelled destination, the broker returned the envelope to Android, and upstream a8s subscribers silently dropped the unknown recipient.

This PR makes the grammar self-describing and adds a second safety boundary: known canonical names always bypass nickname mappings, including bad mappings already present in SharedPreferences. New mappings that attempt to shadow a known canonical name are rejected.

## Follow-up scope

The broader mechanisms identified during investigation are intentionally separate:

- ingress event coalescing and dedup redesign: #57
- carrier-segment-aware SMS pacing and bounded queue: #56
- exact multiword Siri nickname matching: #58
- upstream unknown-recipient/delivery outcomes: neilobremski/bin#225

## Validation

- `./gradlew detekt test :app:compileDebugKotlin`
- `./gradlew assembleDebug -PgithubRepo=neilobremski/a8s-android`

author: mathuraditya724
body:
## Summary

Restores the ability to point the desktop app at a **self-hosted Freestyle server** (with an optional bearer token), which was removed in #342. The option lives in **Settings → Network**, after the enterprise proxy/CA section, and it applies **without an app restart**.

This is the planned follow-up to #462's deferred "remote-server auth" note.

## No-restart design

- The local embedded server **always keeps running** — startup is never gated on the configured URL, so switching back to local (or between remotes) never needs a restart.
- On save: the settings window re-points its API client (`refreshApiBase()`) + refetches everything (`queryClient.invalidateQueries()`); the main process broadcasts `server:changed` so the pill window re-points and rebuilds its streamer. The pill also already calls `refreshApiBase()` before every dictation as a backstop.

## Storage

Server URL/token are stored in Electron's `settings.json` via IPC (`serverUrl`/`serverToken`) — **not** SQLite. They're client-side config (which server to talk to), so they can't live on the server itself.

## Server-side auth

Bearer-token middleware wired directly into `createApp()` (after `pluginApiGuard`). It's a **no-op unless a token is configured**, so the loopback Electron server is unaffected. Standalone/Docker servers read `FREESTYLE_AUTH_TOKEN` (via `startServer({ token })` / `startup.ts`). `/api/health` stays exempt; WebSocket upgrades authenticate via `?token=` (browsers can't set the `Authorization` header on a socket).

## Changes

- **packages/validations**: restore `serverUrlSchema` (empty = local server; validates + normalizes URL)
- **main / preload**: `server:url`/`token` IPC + `server:changed` broadcast; auth headers on `relayEvent` / `putServerSetting`
- **renderer `api.ts`**: `serverUrl`/`token` state, `getAuthHeaders`, `checkServerAuth`, auth-carrying `getClient()`
- **`settings.tsx`**: `ServerConnection` card (endpoint, token w/ reveal, Test / Save / Reset, status chip)
- **`streamer.ts`**: bearer token via `?token=` WS query param
- **server**: `authMiddleware` in `createApp`; `startServer({ token })`; `startup.ts` reads `FREESTYLE_AUTH_TOKEN`
- **tests**: `auth.test.ts`, `server-url.test.ts`

## Known limitation

Matches #462's own deferral: plugin **UI pages** over a *token-protected remote* server won't authenticate yet (a `WebContentsView` can't send the bearer header). Local server and non-token remotes are fully covered; all primary data paths (settings, history, transcribe, plugin management) carry auth.

## Verification

- Server tests: **273 passed** (incl. new `auth.test.ts` + `server-url.test.ts`)
- Server build (tsc): clean
- Electron typecheck (node + web): clean
- Biome + knip: clean (no new issues)

body:
## El bug (Known issue #1 de la auditoría Fase 3)

`useStreamingResponse.stream()` capturaba cualquier excepción a mitad de generación, guardaba el mensaje en su estado interno `error` — que **ninguna tool lee** — y no relanzaba. El `try/catch` que las 8 tools envuelven alrededor de `await stream(...)` (el que alimenta `<ErrorBanner>` o el toast) nunca saltaba.

**Efecto neto:** un rate limit, corte de conexión o chunk malformado a mitad de respuesta dejaba un texto truncado **sin ningún feedback al usuario** — ni banner, ni toast.

## El fix

Una línea: `stream()` relanza (`throw err`) tras guardar su estado. Con eso se activan los `catch` que las 8 tools ya tenían escritos:

- `<ErrorBanner>`: AcceptanceCriteria, TestCase, TestData, EdgeCase, BugReport
- Toast: UserStory, Refiner, Converter

Verificado por grep que las 8 envuelven la llamada en `try/catch` — no hay riesgo de unhandled rejections.

**Arreglo extra de regalo:** `onComplete` se ejecuta dentro del `try` del hook, y `EdgeCaseTool` lanza `Error(t('error.noEdgeCases'))` desde ahí cuando el LLM no devuelve JSON parseable — ese error también se lo tragaba el hook. Ahora propaga.

## TDD

- **RED verificado:** `src/hooks/useStreamingResponse.test.ts` nuevo, 4 tests; el de rethrow falló contra el código original (`expected null to be an instance of Error`).
- **GREEN:** 168 → **172 tests**, `tsc` limpio, lint 0 errores.
- Los otros 3 tests fijan el comportamiento a preservar: texto parcial conservado tras el error, `isStreaming` limpio, `onComplete` no llamado en fallo.

## Stack

Apilada sobre `fix/fase3-audit-cleanup` (#3), que a su vez apila sobre `fix/fase3-audit-bugs` (#2). Orden de merge: #2 → #3 → esta.

`AGENTS.md` actualizado: Known issues renumerado (quedan 4), tabla de tests y fila de historial.

author: karishnu
body:
SpaceDO gives each app an isolated, git-backed workspace running entirely on the Workers runtime. Previously, the workspace depended on Durable Object-local filesystem state, with no durable remote source of truth for an app’s committed history.

This PR makes **Cloudflare Artifacts** the durable, git-compatible source of truth for each app while preserving SpaceDO’s existing filesystem API.

## How it works

The Artifacts-backed filesystem implements the same `FileSystem` interface used by the rest of SpaceDO. It combines:

- **Writable overlay:** An in-memory filesystem containing active edits, hydrated files, and local git objects.
- **Base snapshot:** A read-only index of the current Artifacts branch.
- **Whiteouts:** Tombstones that prevent deleted base files from reappearing.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Artifacts repository] -->|fetch branch| B[Local git object store]
  B --> C[Read-only base index]
  C -->|hydrate on demand| D[Writable in-memory overlay]
  D -->|commit and push| A
```

### Reads and hydration

Point reads first check the writable overlay. If a file exists only in the base snapshot, its blob is read from the local git object store and hydrated into the overlay.

Deleted base files remain hidden through whiteouts.

The filesystem provides two readiness levels:

- **ready()** ensures the Artifacts snapshot is loaded and indexed.
- **whenFullyMaterialized()** hydrates every visible base file into the overlay.

Full materialization happens before whole-tree operations such as commits, deploys, rollbacks, recursive listings, searches, and workspace statistics.

### Writes and deletes

- Writes and edits are applied to the overlay.
- Writing a previously deleted path clears its whiteout.
- Deleting a base file records a whiteout.
- Directory deletion and moves whiteout all affected base descendants.
- Copy and move operations hydrate base-only sources before modifying them.

## Cold-start recovery

The live filesystem and local git repository are in memory. When a SpaceDO instance starts:

1. It restores the app’s persisted Artifacts remote URL from Durable Object storage.
2. It fetches the app’s branch into the in-memory git repository.
3. It walks the fetched commit tree to rebuild the base index.
4. It hydrates files into the working tree as they are accessed.

An Artifacts repository with no commits is valid and represents an empty base. Until the first commit, the filesystem behaves as a normal writable in-memory workspace.

## Artifacts synchronization

Artifacts synchronization manages repository provisioning, authentication, fetches, and pushes.

This PR improves synchronization reliability through:

- **Durable remote discovery:** The Artifacts remote URL is persisted in Durable Object storage and reused after cold starts.
- **Serialized pushes:** Concurrent commits and deploys within one SpaceDO cannot race each other.
- **Bounded retries:** Stale-ref and concurrent-update failures are retried with backoff.
- **Token refresh:** Write tokens are cached and refreshed before expiration.
- **Best-effort failure handling:** Sync errors are logged and returned as failures instead of causing commit or deployment RPCs to throw.

`ARTIFACTS` is a required binding. There is no local-only git fallback.

> Local development and tests must provide an `ARTIFACTS` binding.

## Commit, deploy, preview, and rollback

- **Commit:** Materializes the complete tree, creates a git commit, and mirrors the branch to Artifacts.
- **Deploy:** Builds from the complete overlay-aware filesystem before pushing the commit.
- **Preview:** Uses the correct filesystem when assembling deployment files, including files restored from Artifacts.
- **Rollback:** Fetches Artifacts before resolving the target commit, allowing rollback even when the current SpaceDO has never held that commit locally.
- **Internal paths:** `/.git` and `/.afs` are excluded from user-visible listings, deployment bundles, and rollback trees.

## Editor synchronization fixes

This PR also fixes live editor updates emitted by the Think agent:

- **Generated file contents now appear when selected.** File updates use the slash-stripped paths expected by the UI, such as `src/App.tsx`.
- **Deleted files disappear immediately.** Deletes emit a dedicated `file_deleted` WebSocket message instead of an empty file write.
- **Commit and rollback updates refresh editor state.** The editor file tree remains consistent with the restored workspace.

author: kam-validmind
body:
# Pull Request Description ## What and why? **Security fix:** the external invocation status endpoint (`PATCH /api/v1/external/invocations/{id}`) allowed an agent to bypass human approval — the core control this product provides. **Background for context:** external executors (e.g. a coding-harness plugin) submit a tool call, which is parked in `pending_approval`. The executor is supposed to poll until a human approves, run the tool itself, then report the outcome back via the PATCH endpoint (`Service.RecordExecution`). **How this fix fits the three agent entry paths:** ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph paths [Three agent entry paths] P1["Path 1: Decision-only hook
Submit + RecordExecution
(this PR)"] P2["Path 2: MCP proxy / Invoke
Atryum executes upstream"] P3["Path 3: Managed Agents bridge
watcher calls Submit + RecordExecution"] end subgraph shared [Shared core] Rules[approval_rules + rule engine] Inv[(invocations + invocation_events)] end P1 --> Rules P2 --> Rules P3 --> Rules Rules --> Inv Fix["RecordExecution guards
409 invalid transition
403 wrong agent
idempotent terminal retry"] P1 --> Fix P3 --> Fix style Fix fill:#efe,stroke:#3a3 style P1 fill:#eef,stroke:#36c ``` **Before this change:** only the `running` branch of `RecordExecution` checked the invocation's current status. The `completed`, `failed`, and `cancelled` branches overwrote the status unconditionally. That meant a caller could: 1. Submit a tool call → it lands in `pending_approval`. 2. Immediately PATCH `{"execution_status": "completed", "result": {...}}`. 3. The invocation jumps straight to `succeeded` with a fabricated result and a normal-looking `invocation.succeeded` audit event — no human ever approved it. Even a **human-denied** invocation could be flipped to `succeeded`, and terminal states could be overwritten later. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Executor as External executor participant API as PATCH /external/invocations/{id} participant Svc as RecordExecution participant DB as Invocation store Executor->>API: POST submit tool call API->>DB: status = pending_approval API-->>Executor: 200 pending_approval Note over Executor,DB: Before fix — no approval required Executor->>API: PATCH execution_status=completed
result={forged} API->>Svc: RecordExecution Note over Svc: Only "running" checked status,
completed/failed/cancelled
overwrote unconditionally Svc->>DB: status = succeeded + forged result Svc->>DB: event invocation.succeeded API-->>Executor: 200 succeeded Note over Executor,DB: Audit trail looks legitimate,
human approval was never involved ``` **After this change**, `RecordExecution` is a guarded state machine: | Reported status | Allowed only from | |---|---| | `running` | `approved`, `executing` *(unchanged)* | | `completed` | `approved`, `executing` | | `failed` | `approved`, `executing` | | `cancelled` | `approved`, `executing`, `pending_approval`¹ | ¹ Cancelling a still-pending call is allowed because abandoning an unapproved call only makes the record *more* conservative — it can never fake an approval. ```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 direction LR [*] --> pending_approval: Submit pending_approval --> approved: Human approves pending_approval --> denied: Human denies pending_approval --> cancelled: PATCH cancelled¹ approved --> executing: PATCH running approved --> succeeded: PATCH completed approved --> failed: PATCH failed approved --> cancelled: PATCH cancelled executing --> succeeded: PATCH completed executing --> failed: PATCH failed executing --> cancelled: PATCH cancelled note right of pending_approval ¹ cancel from pending_approval is allowed, all other PATCH outcomes require approval first end note note right of denied Terminal — PATCH blocked (409) end note note right of succeeded Terminal — idempotent retry only, no overwrite (409 on other statuses) end note ``` **Intended happy path** (unchanged for well-behaved executors): ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Executor as External executor participant API as Atryum API participant Human as Human approver participant DB as Invocation store Executor->>API: POST submit tool call API->>DB: pending_approval API-->>Executor: invocation_id loop Poll until approved Executor->>API: GET /external/invocations/{id} API-->>Executor: pending_approval end Human->>API: Approve in UI API->>DB: approved Executor->>API: GET /external/invocations/{id} API-->>Executor: approved Executor->>Executor: Run tool locally Executor->>API: PATCH running API->>DB: executing Executor->>API: PATCH completed + result API->>DB: succeeded + invocation.succeeded event API-->>Executor: 200 succeeded ``` **`RecordExecution` decision flow** (after fix): ```mermaid flowchart TD A[PATCH execution_status] --> B{Invocation exists?} B -->|no| N404[404 Not Found] B -->|yes| C{Caller identity present
and invocation has agent_id?} C -->|mismatch| N403[403 ErrNotOwner] C -->|ok or exempt| D{Reported status} D -->|running| E{From approved or executing?} D -->|completed| F{Already succeeded?} D -->|failed| G{Already failed?} D -->|cancelled| H{Already cancelled?} F -->|yes| OK[200 idempotent no-op] G -->|yes| OK H -->|yes| OK F -->|no| I{From approved or executing?} G -->|no| I H -->|no| J{From approved, executing,
or pending_approval?} E -->|no| N409[409 ErrInvalidTransition] I -->|no| N409 J -->|no| N409 E -->|yes| W[Write executing + event] I -->|yes| W2[Write terminal outcome + event] J -->|yes| W2 W --> OK W2 --> OK ``` Plus two related hardening fixes in the same function: - **Ownership check** — if the request carries a verified OAuth agent identity, it must match the invocation's `agent_id` (new `ErrNotOwner`, HTTP **403**). Previously any authenticated agent could PATCH *any* invocation, including other agents'. Server-internal callers (the managed-agents watcher) run without an identity on the context and are exempt, and anonymously-submitted invocations are unaffected — so existing legitimate flows keep working. - **Idempotent retries** — re-reporting the same terminal status (e.g. the executor retries a `completed` PATCH after a network blip) is now a safe no-op: the first recorded outcome wins, nothing is overwritten, and no duplicate audit event is emitted. This also fixes a latent bug where replayed managed-agents tool results double-wrote the outcome and emitted a second `invocation.succeeded` event. Invalid transitions return the new sentinel `ErrInvalidTransition`, mapped to HTTP **409 Conflict** at the API layer (was 400 with no guard at all). **Files changed:** - `internal/invocation/service.go` — guards, ownership check, idempotency, sentinel errors - `internal/api/handlers.go` — `errors.Is` mapping to 409/403 - `internal/invocation/record_execution_test.go` — new service-level tests - `internal/api/handlers_test.go` — HTTP status-mapping test ## How to test Automated (all green, including `-race`): ```bash go test ./... go test -race ./internal/invocation/ ./internal/api/ ./internal/managedagents/ ``` Manual repro of the original attack (run the server locally): ```bash # 1. Submit an external tool call — response shows status "pending_approval" curl -s -X POST localhost:PORT/api/v1/external/invocations \ -d '{"source":"amp","tool":"bash","input":{"cmd":"ls"}}' # 2. Try to

author: joewiz
body:
[This PR was prompted by Joe, drafted by Claude Code, and reviewed by Joe.]

## Summary

Multipart/form-data uploads only worked for `POST`. A multipart `PUT` (or `PATCH`) was effectively unusable: `request:is-multipart-content()` returned `false`, the uploaded file part was silently dropped, and the request stream was consumed so nothing downstream could recover it. This fixes multipart parsing so it works for every HTTP method that carries a multipart body, and so uploaded files are exposed to controllers and RESTXQ resource functions (via the `request:` module) regardless of method.

Closes #6580. Substantially addresses #6578 (see *Scope* below).

## Root cause — two coupled defects

1. **`HttpRequestWrapper` gated multipart detection on `POST`.** `isMultipartContent` was only ever `true` when `getMethod()` was `POST`, so for `PUT`/`PATCH` the request was never treated as multipart: `request:is-multipart-content()` returned `false` and `getParts()` was never called.

2. **`XQueryURLRewrite` built its request wrapper with `parseMultipart=false`.** On the controller and RESTXQ path — the path a `PUT` can actually reach, since REST `PUT` *stores* rather than executes — the wrapper fell back to the servlet container's `getParameterMap()`. That exposes non-file form fields but omits file parts entirely, so an uploaded file was never visible there for *any* method, and reading the parameters consumed the body so it could not be re-parsed by hand either.

The two are coupled: fixing only (1) would have flipped `request:is-multipart-content()` to `true` without making the file available on that path — which would move consumers onto a code path that returns an empty file. Both are fixed together.

## What changed

- **`HttpRequestWrapper`** — recognize a multipart body by its `Content-Type` (`multipart/…`) regardless of the HTTP method, instead of requiring `POST`.
- **`XQueryURLRewrite`** — construct the request wrapper with `parseMultipart=true`, so multipart content (including file parts) is parsed via `getParts()` and exposed to controllers and RESTXQ resource functions through the `request:` module.

## Reproduction / test

`MultipartMethodControllerTest` stores a `controller.xql` that reports, via the `request:` module, what it sees of an identical multipart body sent as `POST` and as `PUT` — the same path a third-party router (e.g. the roaster library, eeditiones/roaster#107) takes. Before the fix, `PUT` reported `is-multipart-content()=false` and exposed neither the file field nor the uploaded file; the controller path never exposed the uploaded file for either method. After the fix, both methods see the form field, the uploaded file, and `is-multipart-content()=true`.

Behavior before vs. after, from that test (controller path):

| | `is-multipart-content()` | form field `path` | uploaded file `file` |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST — before | true | ✓ | ✗ |
| PUT — before | **false** | ✓ | ✗ |
| POST — after | true | ✓ | **✓** |
| PUT — after | **true** | ✓ | **✓** |

## Scope

- **#6580** — fully fixed.
- **#6578** — the core defect (uploaded files not parsed for non-`POST` methods / on the controller and RESTXQ path) is fixed: files are now parsed and available through the `request:` module for every method, so the "parse the raw body yourself" workaround is no longer needed. One aspect it deliberately does not add is a way to read an *individual part's own headers* (e.g. a file part's `Content-Type`) through the `request:` module — that would be a small additive API and is better discussed separately. Marked "Relates to" rather than "Closes" #6578 for that reason; happy to close it if reviewers consider the remaining item out of scope.
- Makes the client-side multipart-parsing workaround in eeditiones/roaster#107 unnecessary once released.

## Test plan

- [x] `MultipartMethodControllerTest` (new) — multipart `POST` and `PUT` through a `controller.xql`, asserting the field, the file, and `is-multipart-content()`.
- [x] `org.exist.http.urlrewrite.*` and `org.exist.xquery.functions.request.*` — full packages green (incl. `ControllerTest`, `GetParameterTest`, `PatchTest`, `GetData*Test`).
- [x] `RESTServiceTest` green.
- [x] Codacy (PMD) on the changed files — no new findings.

author: joeybukowski3
body:
## Why

PR #107 gave `useMlbPropsData` a real `status: MlbDataStatus` and `error` field, but no page reads them yet -- there's no shared way to *show* a status to a user. This PR builds that presentation layer in isolation: a `FreshnessStatus` component that turns any `MlbDataStatus` into an accessible, on-brand status row, fully tested against all 8 variants before any page wiring begins.

## Scope

Added, nothing else:

- `src/components/mlb/FreshnessStatus.tsx`
- `src/components/mlb/FreshnessStatus.test.tsx`

Confirmed via repo-wide search: only `FreshnessStatus.test.tsx` imports `FreshnessStatus`. No page, hook, or production file changed. `useMlbPropsData.ts` and `mlbDataStatus.ts` are byte-for-byte untouched. The component does not exist in the production bundle -- confirmed by grepping `dist/assets/*.js` for its copy strings after `vite build`; fully tree-shaken since nothing outside its own test imports it.

## API

```ts
import type { MlbDataStatus } from "@/lib/mlb/mlbDataStatus";

export interface FreshnessStatusProps {
  status: MlbDataStatus;
  compact?: boolean;
  className?: string;
}

export function FreshnessStatus({ status, compact = false, className }: FreshnessStatusProps) { ... }
```

Named export, no default export, no hooks internally -- it's a pure function of its `status` prop. It never calls `useMlbPropsData`, derives status, inspects dashboard rows, fetches, or compares dates to the clock.

## Design language reused, not reinvented

- `cn()` from `@/lib/utils` (existing utility).
- Border/radius/padding shape matches `src/components/ui/alert.tsx`.
- Caution-tone colors (`amber-300`/`amber-50`/`amber-900`) match the existing `src/components/nfl/StaleWarning.tsx` convention exactly.
- Positive tone uses the `--success` design token already defined in `src/index.css` / `tailwind.config.ts` (`bg-success/10 text-success`) -- registered but previously unused anywhere in the codebase.
- Error tone reuses the `destructive` token already used by `Alert`'s destructive variant.
- Neutral tone matches `MlbValuePill`'s existing neutral convention (`bg-muted/60 text-muted-foreground`).
- Icons are individually-named `lucide-react` imports (`Loader2`, `CheckCircle2`, `Users`, `Clock`, `CalendarOff`, `AlertTriangle`, `AlertCircle`), same tree-shaking pattern as every other icon import in the repo. Icon size `h-4 w-4` matches the established convention (`BracketMatchupModal.tsx`, `Bracket.tsx`, etc.).
- No new design system, no Storybook, no demo route.

## Tone mapping

| Tone | States |
|---|---|
| `neutral` | `loading`, `waiting-for-slate`, `no-games-scheduled`, `lineup-pending` |
| `positive` | `current` |
| `caution` | `stale` (both directions), `error` with `hasLastKnownData: true` |
| `error` | `unavailable`, `error` with `hasLastKnownData: false` |

Exposed as `data-tone="neutral" | "positive" | "caution" | "error"` on the root element for both styling and test assertions -- no state-specific DOM IDs.

## Accessibility mapping

| Role / live region | States |
|---|---|
| `role="status"` + `aria-live="polite"` | loading, current, lineup-pending, waiting-for-slate, no-games-scheduled, stale, error-with-retained-data |
| `role="alert"` + `aria-live="assertive"` | unavailable, error-without-retained-data |

`aria-atomic="true"` on every variant. Icons are always `aria-hidden="true"` -- text alone carries meaning, verified for every variant in the test suite. No variant is ever icon-only.

## Wording (all 8 statuses, verbatim from spec)

- **loading** -- "Loading MLB model data" / "Checking the latest available slate."
- **current** -- "Current slate data" / "Model updated {ET timestamp}." or, absent/invalid `generatedAt`, "Model data is available for today's slate."
- **lineup-pending** -- "Lineups still updating" / "{n} of {total} listed batters are confirmed." (zero: "None of the {total} listed batters are confirmed yet."; singular-total grammar handled: "batter"/"is" instead of "batters"/"are")
- **waiting-for-slate** -- "Waiting for today's slate" / "Next scheduled update: {nextRunAt.label}." (raw `nextRunAt.time` never rendered)
- **no-games-scheduled** -- "No MLB games currently listed" / "No games are available for the {formatted slate date} slate."
- **stale (past)** -- "Showing an earlier MLB slate" / "This data is for {formatted slate date}, not today's slate."
- **stale (future)** -- "Showing a future MLB slate" / same secondary template
- **unavailable** -- "MLB model data unavailable" / "The current model payload could not be used."
- **error, no retained data** -- "Unable to load MLB model data" / `status.message` when non-empty, else "Please try again after the next scheduled update."
- **error, retained data** -- "Unable to refresh MLB model data" / "Previously loaded data remains visible. It may no longer reflect the latest update." plus an optional trailing sentence with safely-formatted slate/generated metadata, only when at least one is present and valid.

No "Live," "real-time," "up to the minute," "Fresh," or "Confirmed current" anywhere -- enforced by test #9 and #49.

## Timestamp / slate-date formatting

Both formatters are internal to the file (not exported, no shared global date utility added, per instruction):

- `formatGeneratedAt`: parses `generatedAt`, returns `null` on anything unparseable (never throws, never echoes raw input), formats via `Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { timeZone: "America/New_York", month: "short", day: "numeric", year: "numeric", hour: "numeric", minute: "2-digit", hour12: true })` with a literal `" ET"` suffix appended (never relies on `timeZoneName`, which would print "EDT"/"GMT-4" instead of "ET"). Example: `Jul 16, 2026, 5:32 AM ET`.
- `formatSlateDate`: same noon-UTC-anchor + round-trip technique as `mlbDataStatus.ts`'s own `isValidSlateDateString` (parses `${value}T12:00:00Z`, requires `toISOString().slice(0,10) === value`) so a malformed date like `2026-02-30` is rejected rather than silently rolled over. Falls back to the literal string `"the selected"` so downstream copy stays grammatically valid ("...for the selected slate.").

## Compact-mode behavior

- Primary text is always visible in every mode -- never icon-only.
- Secondary text is hidden by default in compact mode for purely informational states (`loading`, `current`, `waiting-for-slate`, `no-games-scheduled`) to reduce padding/text as instructed.
- Secondary text is always retained in compact mode for `lineup-pending` (explicit test requirement -- counts must survive), `stale`, `unavailable`, and both `error` variants -- the essential caution/error reason is never dropped just because the surface is compact.
- Padding and font size scale down (`px-2.5 py-1.5` / `text-xs` vs `px-3 py-2.5` / `text-sm`).

## Tests -- 50/50 passing, mapped 1:1 to the required matrix

All 50 required scenarios implemented as separate `it()`s across 12 `describe` blocks (loading, current, lineup-pending, waiting-for-slate, no-games-scheduled, stale-past, stale-future, unavailable, error-without-data, error-with-data, general-behavior). Assertions use `getByRole`/`getByText`/`data-tone` queries, not markup snapshots. Notable ones:

- #7 -- an invalid `generatedAt` renders the same fallback copy as a missing one, without throwing and without the raw string appearing anywhere in the DOM.
- #12 -- one-total-batter lineup-pending renders "None of the 1 listed batter is confirmed yet." (singular noun + verb).
- #39 -- the retained-data error state includes formatted slate/generated metadata when present, and omits the trailing sentence entirely (falls back to the exact spec sentence) when neither is available.
- #45 -- rendering with `Object.freeze()`'d status object does not throw and the object is unchanged afterward.
- #50 -- no odds/confidence/edge/EV/betting-recommendation wording in any variant's rendered text.

## Validation

- [x] `npx vitest run src/components/mlb/FreshnessStatus.test.tsx` → **50/50**
- [x] `npx vitest run src/lib/mlb

author: danieljmarkii
body:
## What changed and why

First slice of **B-005** (smarter library deletes → **archive-not-cascade**). Removing a food from the library will *archive* (tombstone) it rather than cascade a delete, so its past meals keep their name and stay in the correlation / vet-report record — undo-capable via a later "Archived" library section + Restore. This PR is the **schema foundation only**: two additive columns on the global `food_items` catalog, the on-device cache mirror, and the sync plumbing to carry the new field down. No read/filter/UI code — those land in the follow-up read-side PRs.

Direction ratified in the 2026-07-16 B-005 planning session (STATUS.md) and grounded in `docs/nyx-food-dedup-requirements.md` (§1/§5 — repoint/tombstone, never hard-delete). Archive (owner removes a food) is a distinct lifecycle from merge/dedupe (B-018, which uses a separate `merged_into`/`merged_at` pair, §5.4) — this PR does not touch that.

## Build step

Parallel track — Food library. B-005 PR 1 (schema). File-disjoint from Step 9 / Step 10.

## Schema changes

New migration `033_food_items_archive.sql` — adds to `food_items`:
- `archived_at TIMESTAMPTZ` — tombstone stamp. `NULL` = live; non-`NULL` = archived. **Load-bearing invariant:** filter `archived_at` ONLY at picker/library reads, NEVER on history/analytics/vet-report joins (else an archived food's past meals lose their name and drop out of the protein exposure set). Restore = set back to `NULL`.
- `archived_by_user_id UUID REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL` — attribution only, mirroring the existing `created_by_user_id`. Deleting the actor's account never removes the globally-shared food.

Both **nullable, no default** — existing rows stay live with no backfill. `food_items` already carries owner-scoped INSERT/UPDATE RLS keyed on `created_by_user_id`; the new columns inherit the table's policies (this migration adds no policy, widens nothing). `food_items` stays globally scoped — the per-account re-scope (B-354) is a separate later migration and is not foreclosed.

Local mirror: `food_items_cache` gains `archived_at` only (the on-device filter field) via the existing `ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN` try/catch pattern in `lib/db.ts`; `refreshFoodCache` (`lib/sync.ts`) threads it through the select + upsert.

**Migration Safety Pre-flight**
- **Rollback plan:** `ALTER TABLE food_items DROP COLUMN archived_by_user_id; ALTER TABLE food_items DROP COLUMN archived_at;`
- **Destructive y/n:** `n` (two `ADD COLUMN`s; no drop/rename/type change on existing data)
- **Backfill:** N/A (existing rows keep `archived_at NULL` = live)

## Open questions

None resolved/raised by this PR. Note: **B-354** (de-globalize the catalog to per-account) is parked high-priority and, when built, makes B-005's per-user archive fall out for free — but these additive columns don't foreclose it, so this schema slice proceeds independently.

## Manual test steps

Backend-only (schema + cache plumbing); no user-visible surface yet. Verify:
- [ ] Migration `033` applies cleanly to the live DB; `food_items` shows `archived_at` + `archived_by_user_id` (both nullable, all existing rows `NULL`).
- [ ] `get_advisors` (security + performance) reports no new findings for `food_items`.
- [ ] On device: existing food library + picker are unchanged (all foods still live) after a `refreshFoodCache` sync — no food disappears, recents ordering intact.

## QA acceptance criteria

- [x] Additive/non-destructive migration, schema-isolated (its own PR).
- [x] `archived_at` mirrored on-device; `refreshFoodCache` INSERT/params arity + ON CONFLICT list complete and correct.
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` clean; food + sync test suites green (pre-push hook: tsc + full jest green).
- [x] No read/filter code — the "filter only at picker/library reads" invariant is documented for the read-side PR, not yet exercised.

## Summary

Adds Kimi K3 and GPT-5.6 Pro with provider-specific request behavior, using the capabilities and identifiers supplied by llm-zoo 1.18.0.

- Bumps `llm-zoo` to `^1.18.0` in the workspace, extension, and relay.
- Adds Kimi K3 to the default model list.
- Sends Kimi K3 chat requests without `temperature` or legacy `thinking`, with its fixed `reasoning_effort: max`.
- Sends Kimi K3 compaction summaries without `temperature` or `thinking`.

- Adds GPT-5.6 Pro on the shared `gpt-5.6-sol` wire identifier and selects Pro through `reasoning.mode: pro`.
- Preserves the shared GPT-5.6 Pro wire identifier when short model names are enabled.
- Preserves `reasoning.effort: max` only when llm-zoo declares a native max ceiling; older model ceilings remain clamped.

GPT-5.6 Pro is available through direct OpenAI API access. It is not advertised through ChatGPT subscription because llm-zoo does not mark it as served by the Codex backend.
