author: bjagg
body:
##### Description of Change

Captures, as an ADR, the architecture decision we worked through: **internal programmatic consumers retrieve LIF data from the Query Planner directly; GraphQL remains an external query facade and a peer consumer of the same Query Planner, not a mandatory internal waypoint.**

Today the Advisor's retrieval runs MCP (semantic-search) → GraphQL → Query Planner. GraphQL and the QP are a *facade and an engine*, not a pipeline: GraphQL is a transactional, MDR-generated ad-hoc query surface whose resolvers just POST a `LIFQuery` to the QP; the QP is the retrieval engine and already has an async job model (`/query_async`, status, orchestrator callback). Putting GraphQL in the Advisor's hot path is a consumer/contract mismatch and — critically — GraphQL's transactional response can't express "cached half now, the rest is refreshing (minutes)", which the QP's async model can. This ADR sets the target topology that unblocks the Advisor's partial/progress/streaming work (#970) and better serves LIF's microservice-independence goal (ADR 0002).

The ADR is explicit about what must be *owned* so it doesn't become debt: single query-construction path (no fork), graduating the QP async contract from "temporary", QP auth for direct consumption, field-selection parity, and that partial results are net-new QP capability.

- `docs/design/adr/general/0003-advisor-queries-query-planner-directly.md` — the ADR (Status: Proposed).
- `docs/INDEX.md` — index entry.

Note: the ADR links to ADR 0002, which is still on its own open PR (#1042) — that relative link resolves once #1042 merges.

author: scottdkey
body:
## What

Third bug in the plugin release workflow: native darwin builds now **compile** on the self-hosted arm64 mint runner (frameworks link, perl version-write works, per #16/#17) but were positioned to fail at packaging with `::error::binary not found at $path`.

## Root cause / mechanism

The staging step reads the binary from `target/${{ matrix.target }}/release/<bin>` (path derived from `matrix.target`). The build must emit there. `cargo build --target <triple>` — even when `<triple>` equals the host — always creates the `target/<triple>/release/` subdir; **drop `--target` and a host build lands in `target/release/`**, which staging never reads → *binary not found*. On the arm64 host, `x86_64-apple-darwin` is additionally a genuine cross target and needs its std installed.

## Change

- **Keep** the explicit per-triple `--target ${{ matrix.target }}` on the build (it is load-bearing for the output path).
- **Also export `CARGO_BUILD_TARGET=${{ matrix.target }}`** as belt-and-suspenders so a stray host-default on the persistent self-hosted runner cannot redirect the output dir. Flag and env agree on every leg.
- **Document** that `rustup target add` must run for both darwin triples (esp. `x86_64-apple-darwin` on the arm64 host) — the existing unconditional `Add rust target` step already does this; the comment records why it must not be gated out.
- **Self-diagnosing staging failure**: on a miss, list both the target-triple dir and the host `target/release` dir so any future divergence names itself instead of forcing another blind re-cut.

## Path trace (aarch64-apple-darwin, bin `dockge`)

- Build: `cargo build --release --target aarch64-apple-darwin --bin dockge` (method=native) → **`target/aarch64-apple-darwin/release/dockge`**
- Stage reads: `target/aarch64-apple-darwin/release/dockge` → **identical.** ✅

Same for `x86_64-apple-darwin` (rustup target added, cross build) → `target/x86_64-apple-darwin/release/<bin>`.

## Linux legs unchanged

The 4 linux legs already build with `--target`; `CARGO_BUILD_TARGET` now equals that same value (no behavior change), and the other additions are diagnostic-only (the new staging lines run only when the binary is already missing). cargo-zigbuild honors `CARGO_BUILD_TARGET` identically to `--target`.

## Validation

- `actionlint`: clean.
- YAML parse (Ruby `YAML.load_file`): OK.
- Path traced end-to-end for a darwin triple (above): build-output dir == staging-read dir.

Post-merge: re-dispatch the 8 plugin RCs (owner will do this). No RCs re-cut here.

  - `video` / `imagen` → teatro dorado dentro del hub (Drive `/preview` o MP4/Storage; solo https).
  - Respeta `activo:false` también en los docs `1..6` para ocultar tarjetas originales (solo se ocultan, nada se borra).
- **`biblioteca_bloques_parche.js` (nuevo):** inyecta la pestaña y el formulario en la Biblioteca reutilizando sus ayudantes (`db`, `esc`, `toast`, `normImg`, `normVid`, `BIB.tab`). Asigna slot libre automático (pool 11–20), convierte links de Drive solo, valida en español.
- **`index.html` + `fatima_hub.html`:** pasada ÚNICA — pool `frame11..frame20` + 1 etiqueta script. Gemelos sincronizados (verificado con diff).
- **`biblioteca.html`:** 1 etiqueta script.
- **`LEEME_HUB_DINAMICO.md`:** contrato de datos y guía de uso.

## Contrato Firestore (extensión de `hub_tarjetas`, sin cambio de reglas)

```
hub_tarjetas/din_{slot}: { nom, desc, imgUrl, icono, color,
  tipo:'html'|'video'|'imagen', src, orden, activo, slot }
hub_tarjetas/{1..6}: + activo (boolean, opcional)
```
La colección ya era lectura-alumnas / escritura-admin en `firestore.rules` — sin cambios.

## Qué NO se toca

`app.js`, `BLOQUES_DATA`, `cambiarBloque`, motores P1–P3, `biblioteca.js`, créditos, reglas, datos de alumnas. Ambos parches llevan bandera de guarda y son no-op standalone.

## Cómo probarlo

En el Deploy Preview: entrar como admin a `biblioteca.html` → pestaña "Bloques del Hub" → crear una categoría de prueba → abrir el hub y verla aparecer sin recargar. Apagarla con el toggle y verla desaparecer. Vista previa simulada del flujo: la interactiva compartida en la sesión.

author: rubentalstra
body:
The W-14 audit's structural waves, landed as one branch:

## What changed

- **Per-folder fresh rewrite of the platform crate** (13 folders re-authored from the governing spec sections, old files deleted): every `service/` chapter, `versioning`, `storage` (version_repo is now a module tree), `extensions`, `system_log`, `telemetry`, `templates`, `validation`, and `db`. Public contracts held name-for-name; each folder's module docs cite their spec sections.
- **Zero re-exports across both app crates**: every import names its defining module; `ServiceError` lives at `service::error` (the mod.rs split), and all ~25 re-export façades are dissolved.
- **Write-path redesign**: the folded audit+contribution+version commit statement is the only commit path — including with digest signing enabled (commit instant read up front with the placement, signature computed before any insert); placement is one read; contribution commits batch their target pre-reads; the persistent-duplicate check is one indexed EXISTS.
- **Committal-header merge on direct writes** (ITS-REST overview MUST): caller-supplied `openEHR-VERSION.*` / `openEHR-AUDIT_DETAILS.*` attributes now merge into direct COMPOSITION/EHR_STATUS/directory commits exactly as on the CONTRIBUTION path; the previously-failing protocol test is green.
- **Background-loop fixes**: AMQP topology declared on connect/change only; the FHIR outbound emitter parks poison rows after a bounded retry budget.
- **db bootstrap**: two-file module, migration-failure connection hygiene (a failed migration can no longer return a search_path-mutated connection to the pool).
- `docs/endpoint-map.md`: every endpoint traced to its SQL (round-trip counts, every N+1 named) — the standing navigation/optimization instrument.
- Tracker refresh: `docs/plans/w14-audit.md` (wave state + the fleet-found findings + the issue #94/#95 plans), WORKLIST, current-phase; instruction files no longer reference the deleted doc layer.

## Receipts

- `cargo nextest run --workspace`: **1656/1656 passed** (5 principled skips).
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets`: clean.
- ECC conformance: **370 executed · 335 passed · 0 failed — exact zero drift** vs the pre-rewrite baseline (CORE + STANDARD held).

The remaining W-14 fix waves (read-path/N+1/cache rows and the fleet-found defects) continue on a follow-up branch; the fresh benchmark pair lands at final W-14 close.

author: xerhab
body:
Fixes [XERK-6](https://xerktech.atlassian.net/browse/XERK-6): *"New Turma Sessions started in the root dir seem to just resume the previous session instead of starting a new session. When the session is started the whole previous chat session history is there."*

## What was wrong

Every repos-root session runs directly in `REPOS_ROOT`, so they all share **one** `~/.claude/projects` slug dir — unlike a worktree session, whose cwd (and therefore slug) is its own. The code resolved "this session's transcript" as **"the newest `*.jsonl` in that dir"**, which is exact for a worktree and wrong here: until the new claude wrote its first entry, the newest was the *previous* root session's.

So a fresh root session reported that session's tail, served its history, seeded its name from its first prompt — and on resume **relaunched it**.

The ticket's "seem to" is the precise word: the spawned claude was always genuinely fresh. I confirmed this against real Claude Code — a second root session in the same dir replies `NO CONTEXT.` when asked about the first one's conversation. Only the hub's *view* was wrong, which is why the symptom appears at session start and then heals the moment the new session speaks.

## The fix

Every launch pins claude's session id — `--session-id <uuid4>` for a fresh conversation, the `--resume` id for a rejoined one — persisted as `claudeSessionId`. Claude Code names the transcript after that id, so a session's conversation is known by name from before its first byte. `_session_transcript_path()` is the one resolver every surface goes through (heartbeat tail, `history`, subagent resolution, summary seeding, the closed record's `transcriptId`, the `--resume` target), and the hub heartbeats the id so `tunnel-agent.js`'s live tail points at the same file.

Two rules worth not undoing:

- **A pinned session with no transcript on disk resolves to nothing**, never to a neighbour's. Falling back *is* the bug; it reads as an empty conversation exactly once — before the first turn — which is the truth.
- **Sessions predating the pin keep newest-mtime**, which is all they ever had. An agent updating in place adopts live sessions without relaunching, so those keep a null id indefinitely.

Naming the transcript means the hub must also say when the name *changes*: a watch is sent once and held for its lifetime, so `rearmMovedWatches` re-sends it when a watched session's `transcriptId` moves. Only "Restart (clear context)" moves it, and without the re-arm that chat freezes on the pre-restart conversation. The newest-mtime rule rolled over by itself and needed no such signal — this is the cost of the pin, caught by review rather than by me.

## Verification

- `TestRootSessionIsolation` (11 cases) runs the real A-converses → ends → B-spawns sequence, covering tail, history, naming, resume, restart, the closed record's id, the legacy unpinned path, and that a worktree session resolves identically. The key case asserts what the *old* rule returns on the same fixture, so it can't silently stop testing the bug.
- `sessionTranscript` cases in `tunnel-agent.test.js`; live-WS watch + re-arm cases in `server.test.js` (the re-arm test was checked to fail with the fix reverted).
- Full suites green: 566 Python, 451 JS.
- Verified end-to-end against real Claude Code that `--session-id` names the transcript deterministically and `--resume` keeps writing to the same file (no `--fork-session`).

## Deliberately out of scope

Same shared-slug root cause, now fixable per transcript rather than per slug — flagged in CLAUDE.md rather than folded in here:

- `_running_slugs`: a running root session blocks archival of *every* ended root transcript (a delay, not a loss).
- `_session_meta_by_slug`: every archived/resumable root transcript inherits the newest root session's summary and date.
- `_refresh_usage` folds the whole slug, so a root session's card reports the sum of all root sessions ever run (pre-existing).

author: marcodejongh
body:
## Summary
- Settings display-name edits were saved to the DB correctly, but the NextAuth JWT session's `name` claim was baked in once at sign-in and never refreshed — so the hamburger menu, share text, and a couple of other spots kept showing the auto-generated handle (e.g. `speedywalker8392`) instead of the saved name (e.g. `jojo`).
- `session` callback in `auth-options.ts` already refreshed `avatarUrl` from `userProfiles` on every session read (there's even a comment saying so); it just never did the same for `displayName`. Extended it to do both.
- Added `updateSession()` (NextAuth's `update()`) after a successful Settings save so the header/drawer refresh immediately instead of waiting for the next window-focus session refetch.
- Mobile (2.x native) was not affected — it reads through a React Query cache (`['profile']`) that's correctly invalidated on save, not a JWT session.

## Root cause
- Write path (`PUT /api/internal/profile`) was always correct: updates both `user_profiles.display_name` and `users.name`.
- Read path bug: `packages/web/app/components/user-drawer/user-drawer.tsx` (and a few other places) reads `session.user.name` from `useSession()`. NextAuth bakes `name` into the JWT once at sign-in; nothing in the repo ever called `session.update()` or handled `trigger === 'update'` in the `jwt` callback, so that value never changed for the life of the session cookie.

## Changes
- `packages/web/app/lib/auth/auth-options.ts` — `session` callback now also selects `userProfiles.displayName` and overrides `session.user.name` with it when present, mirroring the existing `avatarUrl` → `session.user.image` refresh.
- `packages/web/app/settings/settings-page-content.tsx` — calls `updateSession()` (destructured from `useSession()`) after a successful save for an instant refresh.
- `packages/web/app/lib/auth/__tests__/auth-options.test.ts` — 5 new tests for the `session` callback: overrides name when `displayName` present, leaves it unchanged with no profile row, leaves it unchanged when `displayName` is null, regression guard on the existing `avatarUrl` override, and `session.user.id` still set from `token.sub`.

## Out of scope / follow-ups
- **Clearing the display name entirely** (saving it back to empty) doesn't currently make the header/drawer revert live to the auto-generated handle — the session only overrides `name` when `userProfiles.displayName` is non-empty, same as the pre-existing `avatarUrl` behavior. This is existing behavior, not something this PR changes; filed as a known gap, not fixed here.
- **FYI for whoever next touches `updateProfile`**: the GraphQL resolver (`packages/backend/src/graphql/resolvers/users/mutations.ts`, mobile's write path, recently refactored in #3603/#3679) updates `userProfiles.displayName` but never syncs `users.name` the way the web REST route (`/api/internal/profile`) does. It doesn't cause a visible symptom today — every read path prefers `userProfiles.displayName` over `users.name` — but it's a divergence between the two write paths worth aligning at some point. Not touched in this PR, deliberately, to avoid conflicting with #3603's just-merged changes to that same file.

## Release Notes
Fixed: your Settings display name now shows everywhere right away — no more getting stuck with your auto-generated handle in the menu after you change it.

## Test plan
- [x] `vp run typecheck:web`
- [x] `vp test run --project web --reporter=agent` (targeted: `auth-options.test.ts`)
- [x] `vp check`
- [ ] Manual: sign in, change display name in Settings, confirm hamburger menu updates immediately without reload (see `.boardsesh/qa-notes.md`)

body: ## Bug On the People Report page, the "Tasks With Completed Hours" card showed a visible boundary/seam in dark mode — the area holding the table header ("Color", "Task Name", "Hours") had a different background than the rest of the card, making it look like two separate surfaces instead of one continuous card. ## Root Cause The header background was actually being set by a completely unrelated, unscoped rule leaking in from elsewhere in the app: ```css :global(thead) { background: aliceblue; } ``` in `src/components/Projects/projects.module.css`, and an equivalent bare rule with the same effect: ```css thead { background: aliceblue; } ``` in `src/components/Teams/Team.module.css`. CSS Modules only auto-scopes class selectors, not bare element selectors — so both of these `thead` rules applied globally to every `` in the entire app once bundled, including the one inside the shared `PieChart` component used by "Tasks With Completed Hours". In light mode this pale blue tint blended in with the mostly-white card background, so it went unnoticed; in dark mode it stood out as a visible seam. ## Fix - Scoped the Projects header background to a real CSS Modules class (`.projectsTableHead`) instead of a bare `:global(thead)` selector, and applied that class directly to the `` in `Projects.jsx`. - Scoped the Teams header background the same way (`.teamsTableHead`), applied to the `` in `Teams.jsx`. - Removed the now-unnecessary hardcoded `background-color: white` / `#1f2937` on the `PieChart` component's own `th` rules, since the header now correctly inherits the card's actual background in both themes rather than being painted over. ## Testing - Checkout the `Abhishek_FixPeopleTasksPieChartDarkModeSeam` branch in the frontend repo and use `development` for the backend - Login as admin and navigate to Dashboard → Reports dropdown → Reports → People. - Verified "Tasks With Completed Hours" (People Report → select a person) shows a single, unified card background in both light and dark mode, with no visible seam

author: dream-hun
body:
## What changed

Unpublishing a challenge or course that users had progress on broke the dashboard: the "continue" card linked straight to a 404 (`challenges.show` refuses unpublished content, but the query feeding the card did not), and per-course completed counts could exceed the published totals shown beside them ("3 of 2 completed"). Attempts could also be recorded against unpublished content via direct POST, since `store()` lacked the publish gate that `show()` has.

This applies one rule everywhere: learner-facing reads and writes only touch published challenges in published courses.

- `ChallengeController::store()` now has the same publish gate as `show()`
- The dashboard continue query filters via `whereRelation` on `challenge` and `challenge.course`
- `completedCountsByCourse()` and `statsFor()` join challenges + courses and filter both publish flags, so counts share their denominators' definition of "exists"

## Why

Content admins routinely unpublish material for rework. Progress rows are intentionally kept (re-publishing restores everything), so the fix is to filter reads consistently rather than delete data.

## Reviewer notes

- Six new regression tests pin each failure mode (rejected attempts on unpublished challenge/course, continue skipping/nulling, counts excluding both unpublished variants).
- Deliberately unchanged: the server still accepts `stars` on non-completed attempts — that clamp behavior is pinned by an existing test; tightening it is a separate product decision.
- Verified: full suite 58 passed / 267 assertions, PHPStan level 7 clean, Pint clean.

body:
💡 What: Implemented an `IntersectionObserver` to pause the Three.js `requestAnimationFrame` loop when the canvas is scrolled out of the viewport.

🎯 Why: The Three.js animation frame loop runs continuously by default. If the user scrolls down to read the vision or specs sections, their CPU and GPU continue rendering a 3D scene they cannot even see. This drains battery on mobile and desktop devices unnecessarily.

📊 Impact: Reduces CPU and GPU usage to near 0% when the canvas is out of view. Battery life is preserved. Memory remains identical.

🔬 Measurement: Start the application locally. Observe task manager / Chrome DevTools performance profiler. Note CPU/GPU usage. Scroll down so the 3D brick is out of sight. Observe CPU/GPU usage drops significantly as the rendering stops. Scroll back up and see it resumes smoothly without error. Visuals verified via Playwright.

author: thepig96
body:
Closes #39. Part of #34 (the map #9 execution program). Mechanics authority: `docs/plans/2026-07-15-one-rule-enforcement-spec.md` §D, §E, §K.

## What this builds

The hard floor becomes a trustworthy signal point with a paired resume: **exactly one customer-scoped `stop.fired` per episode**, detected by the fast Redis lane at arrival AND by the durable lane independent of Redis health, deduplicated through one signal ledger — and **`stop.cleared` the moment the balance re-crosses the floor**, no hysteresis, no ack latch, carrying the episode it closes.

### The signal ledger — `StopSignalState` (new)

`apps/billing/gating/models.py` + migration `0006`: one durable row per (billing owner, signal family) holding current state (`stopped`/`cleared`), a per-family `episode_seq`, reason, and `transitioned_at`; unique on (owner, family). Families at launch: `floor_stop` (exercised here) and `soft_floor` (model support only — #40 exercises it).

`apps/billing/gating/services/stop_signal_service.py` (new) is the **single emission choke point**: `drive_stop` / `drive_clear` perform a winning-transition guard on the row, and **only the winner emits the outbox event, atomically with the row** — so the ledger and the event stream can never disagree, and a crossing observed by several lanes fires exactly once. `episode_seq` is the stop-episode id the stop-context and past-limit report (#41) will key on; `stop.fired` and `stop.cleared` both carry it.

### The lanes

- **Fast lane** (`_set_stop`, reached from `record_usage_debit` + `HoldService.acquire`): the Redis NX flag stays as the cheap per-event detector and ack read-surface, but emission now routes through the guard. A flag re-set after a Redis flush drives the ledger and simply loses — no duplicate signal.
- **Durable lane** (`handle_usage_recorded_billing`): gains the floor-crossing branch (`old >= -limit and new < -limit`) at the **configured** floor, driving the stop transition — Pin 4: a crossing during a Redis blind window signals late, never lost. The zero-crossing `balance_overage` early warning stays exactly as it was (Pin 11).
- **Reconcile** (`reconcile_prepaid` / `reconcile_postpaid`): gains **SET power** (Pin 5) — the missing `else`: when the reconciled position is past the floor/cap, it drives the stop transition; the clear-only recovery keeps working through the same guard. Both reconciles now decide on the merged live value when Redis answers and **fall back to the durable position when Redis is blind**, so the bottom line never depends on Redis health.
- **Resume** (Pin 6): `credit()` drives the clearing transition at the exact re-cross (live view when Redis answered; **durable-balance fallback when the fast INCRBY was blind or unseeded** — every durable credit site calls this hook, so a top-up during an outage still resumes now, not an hour later). Reconcile clears through the same guard. `stop.cleared` (new event type, catalog-registered) carries the closed `episode_seq` and the balance at clearance.

### Suspension folds into the stop family

The durable active→suspended flip + `CustomerSuspended` emission ride the **winning stop transition** inside the guard — floor-stop and suspension can never disagree or double-fire. Mode gates preserved: prepaid/meter_only suspension is the Tier-1 baseline (all enforcement-on modes; `off` keeps the old level-based handler branch byte-for-byte); postpaid suspends only when `enforcing` (advisory computes + emits, never suspends). The old postpaid handler branch (read-flag → suspend, D13) is deleted — its job moved into the guard.

Un-suspension deliberately stays at the clearing call sites, gated on the **durable** balance (D15 unchanged): a live-view clear never un-suspends an owner whose true balance is still past the floor.

## Interpretive calls (flagged for review)

0. **The "durable handler" clearing path is read as the credit hook's durable-balance fallback.** The issue lists three clearing paths "(credit, reconcile, durable handler)" — but the durable *drawdown* handler only debits, so it can never observe an upward re-cross. Every durable credit site (Stripe webhook, top-up apply, hold settle) already calls `LiveLedgerService.credit`; when its fast INCRBY is blind/unseeded, the durable balance decides the clear there. That IS the guaranteed lane at the moment of the top-up (pinned by `test_durable_path_clears_when_redis_is_blind`). A level-based clear inside the drawdown handler was deliberately NOT built: the live counter is conservative (durable − undebited), so it would flap stop/clear on lane skew with no real re-cross — the exact churn the ledger exists to prevent.
1. **Suspension timing moves to the crossing.** The winning transition suspends wherever it wins — so the fast lane now suspends at arrival (previously: at async handler drain). Consequence in the e2e seam test: the start-gate's refusal for a floor-crossed owner is now the suspension-shaped `insufficient_funds` (status check answers before the flag check) instead of `customer_stopped`. The gate blocks either way; `customer_stopped` remains reachable for a flag-without-suspension (stale flag, advisory postpaid).
2. **Level-based re-suspend inside an open episode is gone** (enforcement-on only). Today an admin who un-suspends a still-below-floor customer is re-suspended by the next event; now the ledger respects the operator override until the episode clears and a fresh crossing opens a new one. Reconcile's SET only wins when the ledger says cleared.
3. **`_clear_stop` (bare Redis flag delete) no longer re-arms emission** — the ledger does. The old hold-service pin asserting flag-delete → duplicate `stop.fired` was rewritten to pin the new semantics (flag-only delete = no re-emit; a real clear through the guard re-arms, episodes 1→2).
4. **`cleanup_keys` (enforcement-mode transition) silently closes open ledger episodes** (no `stop.cleared` — a config flip is not a re-cross) while preserving `episode_seq`, so a stale open episode can't swallow the first crossing after re-enable and episode ids never collide. Caveat: a consumer of the webhook stream can therefore see a `stop.fired` whose episode is never explicitly closed — the mode flip is the close. If the pairing invariant should hold even across mode flips, the alternative is emitting `stop.cleared` with a distinct reason here.
5. **StopFired.reason stays `customer_wide_stop`** on all lanes (wire contract unchanged); the suspension vocabulary (`min_balance_exceeded` / `budget_exceeded`) stays on `CustomerSuspended` / `Customer.suspension_reason`. `StopCleared.reason` is a new small vocabulary: `balance_recovered` (credit paths) / `reconciled`.
6. **Lock order extended**: `Wallet → Customer → StopSignalState` (documented in `core/locking.py`); `drive_stop` locks the owner before the ledger row so every path (fast lane, handler-under-`lock_for_billing`, reconcile) acquires in one canonical order.
7. **Open question — the customer-wide `stop_reason` string.** PR #48 flagged that the ack still answers `customer_wide_stop` and deferred the §H reason family to #39. This PR deliberately does NOT reshape it: issue #39's text doesn't ask for it, §H's `stop_context.limit` vocabulary (`customer_floor` | `suspended`) is #41's stop-context surface, and the swap touches acks/SDK docs/StopFired wire values. If the owner wants the ack's customer reason reshaped to the §H family, say so and it lands as a small follow-up (the flag value + `read_stop` + pins).

## Acceptance criteria → test pins

- Pin 4 — `test_stop_resume_pins.py::TestPin4DurableLane`: durable lane fires at the **configured** floor with Redis down (monkeypatched client raising); configured-floor-not-zero sequencing; fast + durable lanes → exactly one `stop.fired` **and one `CustomerSuspended`** (the no-double-fire criterion).
- Pin 5 — `TestPin5ReconcileSetsAMissedStop`: reconcile SETs a missed stop (flag + ledger + suspension), with and without Redis, idempotent per positio

author: c-hipple
body:
## Summary

This PR adds two complementary features: (1) extraction and display of camera settings (shutter speed, aperture, ISO, focal length) from photo EXIF data, and (2) the ability to specify custom folder names when importing photos, with a live-updating timestamp default.

## Key Changes

**Backend (Go):**
- Added `photoMetadata` struct to hold formatted camera settings (shutter speed, aperture, ISO, focal length)
- Implemented `parseExifTIFF()` to parse EXIF data from TIFF-based formats (JPEG APP1 segments, TIFF RAWs, CR3 CMT2 boxes)
- Added helper functions: `formatShutterSpeed()` for exposure time formatting, `trimFloat()` for clean decimal display, `jpegExtractExifTIFF()` to extract TIFF payload from JPEG APP1 segments
- Implemented `extractPhotoMetadata()` to read EXIF from JPEGs, TIFF-based RAWs (ORF), and CR3 files
- Added `/api/photo-metadata` endpoint to serve camera settings for a given photo
- Enhanced `importFromUSBHandler` to accept `new_directory_name` parameter; validates folder names (no leading dots, no path separators) and prevents collisions with existing directories
- Added comprehensive unit tests for EXIF parsing and shutter speed formatting

**Frontend (React):**
- Added `formatFolderTimestamp()` helper to match backend's default timestamp format (YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS)
- Added state for `photoMetadata`, `newFolderName`, and `folderNameEdited` flag
- Implemented auto-updating folder name field that ticks with the current time until user interaction
- Added `/api/photo-metadata` fetch in a `useEffect` hook that runs when the displayed photo changes
- Moved folder name input UI below the date range picker and above the Import button
- Display camera settings (shutter speed, aperture, ISO, focal length) as a metadata overlay on the photo viewer when available
- Re-arm the timestamp prefill after a successful import

**Styling:**
- Added `.folder-name-container` and `.folder-name-input` styles for the new folder name input field
- Added `.photo-metadata-overlay` style for displaying camera settings on the photo viewer

## Notable Implementation Details

- EXIF parsing handles multiple TIFF byte orders (little-endian, big-endian) and Olympus ORF variants
- Files without EXIF data (PNGs, screenshots, stripped JPEGs) gracefully return an empty metadata object rather than an error
- The folder name input is disabled when "Add to current batch" is selected, showing the current directory name instead
- Stale EXIF fetch responses are dropped when navigating quickly between photos via a `cancelled` flag
- Folder name validation prevents directory traversal and hidden folder creation

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary
Tightens error handling across the `scripts/` so genuine bugs surface instead of being masked, while keeping legitimate numerical robustness intact.

The main issue: `forward_mse_and_preds` wrapped the whole simulation in a bare `except Exception` that turned *every* error (including `KeyError`/typos/config bugs) into a `1e12` penalty. During optimization that silently hides real problems as "just a bad parameter vector".

- **`brannmark_smoke_optim.py`** — narrow the catch to expected simulation failures only; everything else propagates:
  ```python
  _SIM_FAILURE_EXC = (RuntimeError, FloatingPointError, OverflowError, np.linalg.LinAlgError)
  ...
  except _SIM_FAILURE_EXC as exc:      # was: except Exception:
      logger.debug("forward simulation failed; applying penalty: %r", exc)
      return PENALTY, np.full(len(ctx.df_m), np.nan)
  ```
  `RuntimeError` is what `simulate_opt` raises on integrator non-convergence, so infeasible vectors still get the penalty. A `KeyError`/`ValueError` from a real bug now propagates. Also introduces a named `PENALTY = 1e12` constant (previously a magic number in two spots).

- **`brannmark_full_p1.py`** — the prior-metadata read did `except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError): pass`, silently discarding a corrupt metadata file (and a bad `started_unix` would `float()`-crash unhandled). Now it also catches `ValueError` and prints a warning instead of swallowing.

- **`brannmark_nominal_r2.py`** — `load_species_ic` raised an opaque `KeyError` when the SBML model lacked an expected species. Now raises a `ValueError` naming the missing species and what was found.

- **`monitor_master_run_log_3m.sh`** — the log copy used `cp ... 2>/dev/null || true`, hiding failures. The loop still stays alive on transient errors, but now records the `cp` error in the digest.

## Notes
Branched off `cursor/brannmark-smoke-optim-6ae1` (the branch that actually contains this code — `main` has none), so this PR targets that branch. Verified: `py_compile`, `bash -n`, `flake8` error checks pass, and a spot test confirms `RuntimeError` → penalty while `KeyError` propagates.

author: jeong-sik
body:
## What changed

- add `append_private_jsonl_durable_locked_at_end_offset_result`
- compare the caller's expected byte cursor while holding the existing in-process mutex and cross-process file lock
- reject stale writers with typed `End_offset_mismatch { expected; actual }` before writing any bytes
- keep the existing rollback + fsync durability contract and return the committed end cursor
- reject negative expected cursors explicitly

## Why

The Keeper Operation Journal must replay once, then append incrementally without rereading its complete JSONL history on every event. An immutable writer state can carry its last committed cursor, but a copied/stale state must not append behind another writer. This exact-cursor CAS is the minimal storage primitive for that contract:

```text
immutable replay state + expected cursor
  -> locked cursor compare
  -> durable append
  -> new immutable state/cursor
```

It adds no timer, retry count, capacity limit, semantic classifier, or hidden fallback.

## Validation

- `scripts/dune-local.sh build test/test_fs_compat_durable_append.exe`
- `_build/default/test/test_fs_compat_durable_append.exe` — 16/16 pass
- `ocamlformat` on the three changed files
- `git diff --check`
- 3 files, 175 changed lines (<400)

Full repository CI remains authoritative. This storage leaf is independent of the published OAS v0.215.0 release and current MASC pin; it adds no OAS contract or dependency.

## Stack role

This is the first replacement slice for #24966 §3. The next PR builds one Keeper-owned generic MASC Operation Journal with immutable replay state over this primitive; the compaction-only O(n²) writer is then deleted rather than retained as a compatibility path.

## What changed

- Records the completed v3.7.0 raw-Git Round 2 exercise without modifying the source-only candidate PR.
- Preserves a UTF-8 Base64 transport form of the signed finalized bundle, plus expected source/context, derived raw-Git bindings, control record, public key, and a SHA-256 manifest.

- Updates the pilot README with the current v3.7.0 trust root and a link to the Round 2 record.

Actions artifacts are retained only temporarily. This PR preserves the exact signed result and the minimal public verification inputs so the result can be rechecked after artifact expiration.

The first reverify correctly rejected the direct binary .evb path before the seal could receive its key. This follow-up stores the exact same bytes as UTF-8 Base64 text, records the original decoded SHA-256, and documents strict Base64 validation plus the reconstruction command. It does not weaken the V1 non-UTF-8 changed-file rule.

The LF pin is a reproducibility correction: without it, a Windows checkout using core.autocrlf can alter the stored text bytes and create a false manifest mismatch even when the Git blobs are correct.

body:
## Summary

Two independent changes, one per commit:

1. **Replace devbox with flox** (`chore`) — swap `devbox.json`/`devbox.lock` for a locked `.flox/` environment with an equivalent tooling set: `go_1_25`, `golangci-lint`, `goreleaser`, `kubectl`. The activation hook and make-target aliases mirror the previous devbox `init_hook`/`scripts`.
2. **Add a Nix flake** (`feat`) — build the Go binary with `buildGoModule` and export it for NixOS/flox, including declarative installation as a kubectl/krew plugin.

### Flake outputs
- `packages.default` / `.kubectl-consolidation` — the Go binary
- `apps.default` — runnable via `nix run`
- `overlays.default` — adds the package to a nixpkgs instance
- `nixosModules.default` / `homeManagerModules.default` — `programs.kubectl-consolidation.enable = true` puts `kubectl-consolidation` on `PATH`, so `kubectl consolidation` works
- `devShells.default` — mirrors the flox tooling

### Notes
- **Go version:** both the flox env and the flake use Go 1.25. `go.mod` declares `go 1.25.0`, but the old devbox pinned `go@1.23`; a sandboxed Nix build can't auto-download a newer toolchain, so the toolchain is pinned to `go_1_25`.
- `nix/package.nix` hardcodes `version = "0.1.0"` (matches the current krew manifest / latest tag); unlike the goreleaser build it isn't derived from git, so it needs bumping per release — standard for a nixpkgs-style package.

### Verification
- `flox activate` provides Go 1.25.11 + all tools; `make build` compiles inside the env.
- `nix build`, `nix run`, and `nix flake check` all pass.
- Both modules eval-tested: enabling the option injects the package into `environment.systemPackages` / `home.packages`.

author: bramsdell-ms
body:
Fixes the DMA1 hardfault in #6525.

### Root cause
`dma::init()` only brought up DMA0 — it called `enable_and_reset::<DMA0>` and configured `DMA0.mp_csr()`. DMA1 was left unclocked and held in reset, so the first write to any `EDMA_1_TCD` register (e.g. the TCD reset in `setup_typical`) triggered a bus fault → hardfault. That's the "pointer write" fault seen when switching `dma0_ch0` → `dma1_ch0`.

### Fix
Enable + reset DMA1 and configure its `MP_CSR`, mirroring the existing DMA0 setup (`#[cfg(feature = "mcxa5xx")]`-gated). The DMA1 clock gate is already generated by the new build.rs (`impl_cc_gate!(DMA1, mrcc_glb_acc0, mrcc_glb_rst0, dma1, NoConfig)`), so `enable_and_reset::<DMA1>` works directly.

### Verification
On an **FRDM-MCXA577**, `dma_mem_to_mem` using `DMA1_CH0` now passes both mem-to-mem and memset — no hardfault:

```
[INFO ] PASS: mem_to_mem verified.
[INFO ] PASS: memset verified.
[INFO ] === All DMA tests complete ===
```

Both `mcxa5xx` and `mcxa2xx` still build.

body:
## Qué cambia (valor para el cliente)

En el dashboard (`/dashboard`), mover un proyecto a la papelera, restaurarlo o
eliminarlo definitivamente no daba ningún tipo de confirmación visual: las tres
acciones llamaban a `router.delete`/`router.post` sin `onSuccess`/`onError`. Si
la petición fallaba (sesión caducada, error de red, error 500 del servidor) el
cliente no se enteraba — la tarjeta simplemente no cambiaba de sitio y parecía
que la app no había respondido a su clic, sin ninguna pista de qué pasó ni de
si debía reintentar.

Ahora las tres acciones muestran un toast de éxito o de error, reutilizando
`react-hot-toast` (ya montado globalmente en `app.tsx` y usado con el mismo
patrón en el editor para el guardado):
- Mover a la papelera → "Proyecto movido a la papelera" / error con aviso para reintentar.
- Restaurar → "Proyecto restaurado" / error con aviso para reintentar.
- Eliminar definitivamente → "Proyecto eliminado definitivamente" / error con aviso para reintentar.

Sin cambios de comportamiento cuando todo va bien salvo el toast: no se toca
ninguna ruta ni el modal de confirmación existente.

## Cómo se verificó
- Suite completa: 244/244 tests en verde (`php artisan test`).
- `npm run build` compila sin errores.
- Probado en Chromium real: login → mover un proyecto a la papelera → toast
  "Proyecto movido a la papelera" → restaurar desde la papelera → toast
  "Proyecto restaurado".

IaC-based SNS->SQS subscription join), AWS services (SecretsManager/KMS/S3/DynamoDB; SecretsManager keyed by secret name -> shared-key edge), HTTP ingress (express/fastify/koa), crypto inventory (node:crypto + jwt), HTTP client (axios/fetch/got), Node databases, kafkajs, amqplib.

## Problem

Arcade mode had no working base-repair path. The dock heal existed but never ran: arcade configs set `reinforceGens: 0`, so `suddenDeath` was true from tick 0 and the sudden-death guard in `dockAtHomeBase` silently disabled repair for the whole mode. - **`damageBase` helper** (context.ts): all base damage (rams, munitions, rocks) routes through one clamp; the arcade player base floors at 1 HP (`ARCADE_BASE_HP_FLOOR`) — batterable to the brink, never razed. Enemy bases still raze to 0. Implements plan decision #8 (docs/arcade-mode-plan.md).

author: miried
body:
FormatMessageA is needed for error diagnostics in MSVC 4.2 (and possibly other tools from that era). E.g. RC.EXE currently errors because the function is not available. Note that the existing implementation is not feature-complete - this PR focuses only on enabling the function and giving it enough functionality to verify that the va_list works.

FormatMessageA takes a va_list pointer. On 64-bit targets, Clang canonicalizes va_list as an array of __va_list_tag, so the generated helper prototype tried to spell a pointer-to-array type as a simple parameter and produced invalid C syntax. Treat array pointees as opaque in best-effort helper prototypes: the trampoline only needs the outer pointer ABI, and void * preserves that ABI without depending on the host va_list representation.

Enable the existing shim and add a fixture that exercises reordered ANSI string inserts through a real guest va_list. Implement only the minimal FORMAT_MESSAGE_FROM_STRING insert path needed by the test; broader FormatMessageA support remains out of scope.

## Summary

Implements the Week 3 enterprise knowledge-base Agent on top of the hardened Week 2 retrieval branch.

### Core QA orchestration
- Add `KnowledgeQAAgent` to coordinate query resolution, adaptive retrieval, grounded prompt construction, LLM generation, validation, and response serialization.

### Multi-turn conversation
- Add session-isolated `ConversationMemory` keyed by `session_id`.
- Support optional JSON persistence, bounded recent history, lightweight compression of older turns, session clearing, and short follow-up resolution using the latest user question.

### Answer optimization and validation
- Block unrelated/no-result questions before calling the LLM.
- Require evidence-only answers with numbered citations.
- Detect empty answers, invalid citation numbers, and missing citations.
- Catch model-service errors and return a stable error response without corrupting conversation state.

### CLI and tests
- Add `scripts/chat_agent.py` for single-query and interactive multi-turn chat.
- Reuse the active versioned index and `AdaptiveHybridRetriever`.
- Add focused tests for grounded answer generation, no-answer interception, follow-up context, session isolation, memory compression, and citation validation.

git checkout agent/week3-core-agent

author: alf1974-lgtm
body:
This PR introduces a fully self-contained, browser-based Tic Tac Toe game playable by two people sharing the same browser. No frameworks or dependencies — just plain HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript.

## Changes
- **`index.html`** — Game markup: 3×3 button grid, status banner, scoreboard, and a win/draw overlay.
- **`style.css`** — Dark glassmorphism theme with distinct colours for each player (red for X, blue for O), winning-cell pulse animation, and a spring pop-in overlay animation.
- **`game.js`** — Game logic: turn alternation starting with X, win detection across all 8 combos, draw detection, per-session score tracking, and board reset.

## How it works
1. Player X clicks a cell; the board marks it and flips the turn to O.
2. Players physically hand the mouse back and forth until someone wins or the board fills.
3. A win/draw overlay appears at the end of each round; clicking **Play Again** resets the board while preserving scores.
4. **Reset Scores** wipes the scoreboard and starts a fresh game.

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>pnpm/pnpm (pnpm)</summary>

### [`v11.13.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/HEAD/pnpm11/pnpm/CHANGELOG.md#11130)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v11.12.0...v11.13.0)

##### Minor Changes

- Added `versioning.epics` to `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. An epic ties a group of member packages to a lead package, constraining every member's major version to a band derived from the lead's major: while the lead is on major `M`, members live in `M*100 … M*100+99`. Members move independently inside the band (patch, minor, and a `major` intent that stays in-band); a bump that would carry a member past the band ceiling is rejected until the lead advances its own major. When a release plan takes the lead to a new stable major, every member re-bases to the band floor in the same plan. Membership is matched with pnpm's package selectors — name globs, `./`-prefixed directory globs, and `!`-prefixed negations.

- Added the `team` command for managing organization teams and team memberships on the registry, with create, destroy, add, rm, and ls subcommands and support for --otp, --parseable, and --json flags.

- Added native workspace release management [#​12952](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/12952): the new `pnpm change` command records change intents as changesets-compatible `.changeset/*.md` files (`pnpm change status` shows the pending release plan), and the bare `pnpm version -r` consumes them — bumping versions across the workspace with dependent propagation through `workspace:` ranges, fixed groups, a `maxBump` cap, `--filter` narrowing, and `--dry-run` — writing changelogs, and recording consumed intents in a committed ledger that keeps cherry-picks and merge-backs between release branches safe. Packages can be moved onto per-package release lanes with the new `pnpm lane <name> --filter <pkg>` command and back with `pnpm lane main --filter <pkg>` (`pnpm lane` shows the membership), releasing `X.Y.Z-lane.N` prereleases from the same runs that release stable versions of the packages on the main lane. Configuration lives under the new `versioning` key of `pnpm-workspace.yaml` (`fixed`, `ignore`, `maxBump`, `lanes`, `changelog`). When two workspace projects publish the same name, intent files, `versioning.lanes`, and `versioning.fixed`/`ignore` may reference a project by its workspace-relative directory path (e.g. `"./pnpm/npm/pnpm"`) — the one additive extension to the changesets format, applied automatically by `pnpm change`.

  Release changelogs default to `registry` storage (`versioning.changelog.storage`): no `CHANGELOG.md` is committed. Each release's section is composed at publish time and packed into the published tarball on top of the previously published version's changelog, and the consumed change intents are garbage-collected by a later `pnpm version -r` only once the registry confirms the version is published with its section. Set `versioning.changelog.storage: repository` to keep committed `CHANGELOG.md` files instead.

- Added a new override selector form with an empty range — `"pkg@": "<version>"` — called a convergence override. It rewrites a dependency edge only when its exact version satisfies the edge's declared range, so compatible consumers converge on one version while incompatible consumers keep their own resolution — now and for any dependent added in the future [#​12794](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/12794).

  ```yaml
  overrides:
    "form-data@": 4.0.6
  ```

  The value must be an exact version. When a full resolution detects that every declared range also admits a newer version, pnpm warns that the override is stale and names the version to converge on. Previously an empty range in an override selector was undocumented and behaved like a bare (unscoped) override.

##### Patch Changes

- A `tokenHelper` set in the global pnpm `auth.ini` is no longer rejected as project-level configuration. The guard that blocks `tokenHelper` from a project `.npmrc` only treated `~/.npmrc` as a trusted source, so a helper written to `auth.ini` (for example by `pnpm config set`) failed on every command and could not even be removed with `pnpm config delete`. A `tokenHelper` in a workspace or project `.npmrc` is still rejected.

- `pnpm cache delete` now removes a package's metadata from every metadata cache directory (`metadata`, `metadata-full`, and `metadata-full-filtered`), instead of only the one the current resolution mode reads. Previously a package cached under a different mode (e.g. `metadata-full-filtered`) was left behind. Closes [#​12753](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/12753).

- Fixed an injected workspace dependency (`injectWorkspacePackages: true`) incorrectly staying as `file:` instead of deduping back to `link:` when an unrelated, ordinary shared dependency resolved to a peer-suffixed variant for the target project's own copy but not for the injected occurrence. See [#​10433](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/10433).

- `pnpm deploy` now supports workspaces that use catalogs.

- Fixed `pnpm deploy` with a shared lockfile so local `file:` tarball dependencies keep their package name in the generated deploy lockfile. This prevents warm-store deploys from failing with `ERR_PNPM_UNEXPECTED_PKG_CONTENT_IN_STORE` when the tarball filename includes the version.

- Options that follow `create`, `exec`, or `test` appearing as a subcommand of another command are now parsed instead of being silently treated as positional parameters. For example, `pnpm team create @​org:team --registry <url>` previously ignored the `--registry` option and sent the request to the default registry.

- `pnpm add -g`, `pnpm update -g`, `pnpm setup`, and the self-updater no longer fail with `ERR_PNPM_MISSING_TIME` when `trustPolicy: no-downgrade` or `resolutionMode: time-based` is set in the global config [#​12883](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/12883). The decision to fetch full registry metadata now lives in one place, and the `no-downgrade` trust policy always requests full metadata (matching the self-updater), since the trust evidence it checks is missing from abbreviated metadata even on registries that include the `time` field.

- `pnpm list` and `pnpm why` no longer crash with `EMFILE: too many open files` when a project has a large number of unsaved dependencies (packages present in `node_modules` but not in the lockfile). The reads of those packages are now concurrency-limited.

- The published `pnpm` package no longer declares `dependencies` or `devDependencies`. author: dcellison
body:
## Summary

This PR migrates fifteen inherited base verbs to the target vocabulary prose contract: `phoa`, `riola`, `shonela`, `thumela`, `kulo`, `phesua`, `thole`, `shimalo`, `thilonu`, `pheru`, `meloa`, `phelona`, `heno`, `korei`, and `kanelu`.

Each entry now has a focused definition, a physical pronunciation account, structured and validated examples, accurate usage guidance, optional embodied sound symbolism, direct pillar connections where they earn their place, and semantic-domain rationales. The Phi forms, glosses, IPA, syllabification, and base-vocabulary status are unchanged.

The generated prose report now records 564 target entries and 616 legacy entries, including 434 target-contract content entries. The generated semantic-domain reference has also been refreshed.

## Semantic decisions

- `phoa` remains the general verb of deliberate action, while `riola` retains its narrower sense of sustained purposeful labour and stays distinct from module `riporu` task and `rimawu` drudgery.
- `shonela`, `thumela`, and `kulo` now separate learning, teaching, and accompaniment along a way. Work module `thunaro` retains structured training.
- `phesua` inspiration stays distinct from `nomela` encouragement, `sharemi` persuasion, and `panoru` support.
- `thole`, `shimalo`, and `thilonu` separate repeated practice, self-discipline, and practical preparation. Planning and readiness remain neighbouring but independent claims.
- `pheru` names continuation under pressure; `meloa` adds chosen effort towards a purpose. Patience, resilience, sturdiness, and determination keep their existing boundaries.
- `phelona`, `heno`, and `korei` distinguish requirement, satisfaction, and fulfilment. Ordinary success remains fulfilment of a stated purpose, while module `thonuki` remains technical failure against a required function.
- `kanelu` reports the event of erring and stays distinct from a presently mistaken state, inaccuracy, technical fault, or functional failure.
- The coverage audit records trying or attempting as `REVIEW`. Current Phi can state intention, initiation, persistence, and result, but the active corpus already shows pressure for a neutral verb that says an action was undertaken without claiming more.

No migrated Phi form matches an ordinary English word.

## Voice pass

The Humanizer and Phi voice pass caught a batch stamp in the first draft: eight sound-symbolism fields used the same "can recall" frame, and several articulatory notes opened with identical tongue-position wording. Those repetitions were rebuilt while the phonetic facts stayed fixed. The final batch has no repeated cross-entry phrase of six or more words, no new dash construction, and no semantic meaning assigned to syllable pieces.

## Checks

- `/tmp/phi-venv/bin/python scripts/validate_examples.py`
- `/tmp/phi-venv/bin/python scripts/test_vocabulary_schema.py`
- `/tmp/phi-venv/bin/python scripts/test_name_forms.py`
- `/tmp/phi-venv/bin/python scripts/audit_phonetic_neighbors.py --output /tmp/phonetic_neighbors_learning_effort.txt`
- `diff -u documents/validation/phonetic_neighbors_baseline.txt /tmp/phonetic_neighbors_learning_effort.txt`
- `/tmp/phi-venv/bin/python scripts/vocabulary_prose_coverage.py`
- `/tmp/phi-venv/bin/python scripts/generate_reference.py`
- `/tmp/phi-venv/bin/python scripts/build_site.py`
- `git diff --cached --check`

The full lexicon validator checked 1,180 entries with zero errors and zero warnings. The phonetic-neighbour audit remained at the committed 250-pair baseline, and the complete site build succeeded.

author: domthedeveloper
body:
## Theorem being formalized

For every positive `k`,

```text
W(k + 1) - W(k) ≥ k + 1.
```

The exact AlphaProof Nexus theorem proves the slightly weaker bound `≥ k`. The April 10, 2026 Erdős Problems discussion records the more general informal refinement `W_r(k+1)-W_r(k) ≥ k+r-1`, so this PR does **not** claim novelty. Its purpose is to kernel-formalize the two-color `+1` case.

## Proof mechanism

The upstream greedy one-step lemma assumes the extension index is `i < k`. Its arithmetic argument remains valid at the endpoint `i = k`: if both colors are blocked, the two forced `(k+1)`-term progressions have differences `d₀,d₁ ≤ k`, and stepping back `d₁` terms in one progression and `d₀` terms in the other produces a common preceding point forced to have both colors. This permits `k+1` extension positions rather than `k`.

## Verification plan

- Pin AlphaProof Nexus to commit `0647711a71183c1ea492ad60860776617ce1ea88`.
- Reject placeholders, `native_decide`, and custom axioms.
- Kernel-build the strengthened theorem and print its axiom footprint.
- Keep this PR draft until CI passes.

body:
## Summary

- Adds `stellar-agent profile init`: creates and persists a new profile TOML with per-profile-derived keyring references. `--profile` defaults to `default`, `--network` to testnet, `--engine` to `v1` (with a `noop` opt-out for a zero-ceremony testnet profile). `--rpc-url` is optional for testnet; mainnet requires an explicit `https://` endpoint — the built-in mainnet default requires an API key and answers HTTP 401 unauthenticated, so persisting it silently would mint a broken configuration. Refusals are typed (`validation.mainnet_rpc_url_required`, `validation.profile_already_exists`, `validation.config_invalid`, `validation.address_invalid`) and the write is atomically no-clobber (`loader::save_new_to_dir`). Init mints no key material and emits no audit row; the loader rustdoc and MCP first-run guidance that already referenced this command now describe an implemented one.
- Completes the round trip an init-minted profile requires: `profile enroll-signer` pins the literal placeholder signer account (`"default"`) to the enrolled seed's derived G-strkey. Classification and the pin operate on the raw on-disk TOML through new loader functions (`read_signer_ref`, `pin_signer_account`) that patch only `mcp_signer_default.account` — `STELLAR_AGENT_*` environment overlays stay load-time-only and can never be persisted into the trust root. A pinned G-strkey is never rewritten (mismatch refuses, unchanged); a value that is neither the placeholder nor a valid G-strkey refuses with the new `enroll_signer.account_malformed` code; every refusal path precedes the write. The success envelope gains `account_populated`.
- One normative V1 ceremony statement (owner key, attestation key, audit key, signed policy) in the CLI reference, mirrored by init's `next_steps` and every doc surface; README and the MCP first-run comment state that a v1 profile keeps the MCP server refusing to start until the ceremony completes. Agent skill bumped to 0.3.3 and re-zipped.

## Testing

- Live testnet acceptance (registered in `run-testnet-acceptance.sh`): drives the production binary end to end — `profile init` (placeholder asserted via parsed TOML), `profile enroll-signer` through the real OS keyring (`account_populated: true`, derived G-strkey pinned on disk), then a keyring-resolved `trustline` that signs, submits, and confirms on-chain, with RAII keyring cleanup. Green on the exact committed tree.
- New offline tests: env-overlay immunity through the production loader functions, pin-before-keyring ordering, malformed-pin refusal, pinned-branch never-writes stubs, no-clobber save, patch-preserves-unknown-keys, and typed wire-code pins for every init refusal.
- Full local gate suite green: fmt, clippy (unscoped, `-D warnings`), workspace tests (CI feature set), CLI test-helpers suite, machete, deny check, release build, per-crate coverage floors.
- Three-reviewer pre-commit panel plus a cycle-2 verification pass: all findings closed (including the two blockers: the env-merged profile persist and the unregistered acceptance suite that would have failed the scheduled testnet workflow).

Closes #80

author: eilandert
body:
PR-A of the GraphQL dep-caching ladder (design: `memory/labs/nginx-cache-turbo-module/graphql-deps-design.md` §22).

Adds `cache_turbo_require_header <name>`, which inverts the store default on a location from *cacheable unless vetoed* to **uncacheable unless the origin affirms it**.

### Why

A GraphQL endpoint answers a read query and a write mutation on the same URI and method, and returns errors as `200 OK` with an `errors` member in the body. No HTTP-level inspection separates those, and the module deliberately never parses the body (it stays an opaque blob) — so the decision has to come from the application.

### Shape

- Plain header **name**, not a complex value: the value is read from the *response*, and a `$variable` would silently evaluate against the *request*. Validated as an RFC 9110 5.6.2 token at config time.
- Gate scans the **whole** `headers_out` list. A header sent twice with conflicting values is ambiguous, and any non-affirmative occurrence vetoes — a first-match-wins gate would store an uncacheable body whenever `yes` arrived first.
- Affirmative = whole-value `yes`/`1`/`on`, case-insensitive. A prefix compare would read `note` and `1x` as affirmative.
- **Stripped before store** (like `Age` / the RFC 9213 targeted directives): this cache is the intended consumer, a HIT must not replay it downstream.
- Unset ⇒ gate returns 1 ⇒ every existing config unchanged.

Fails closed by construction: any doubt = no store = a miss, never a wrong serve.

### Tests

`test_require_header` drives the gate through the `do_GET` request-echo harness landed in #33 (`X-Want-Cacheable`; a `|` in the value splits it into duplicate response headers). Covers the affirmative set, every refusal case (absent / `no` / empty / `note` / `1x` / `yes-but`), conflicting duplicates in **both** orders, the strip, and an unset control location.

Every assert is on a **positive** `X-CT-Status` — each refusal is a plain MISS, and a MISS carries no `x-cache`, so an absence assert would pass even with the gate deleted (the `[RECURRING]` weak-absence anti-pattern in `lessons.md`).

**Sabotage-canaried 4/4**, each compiling under `-Werror` (a canary that fails the build proves nothing — the `.so` isn't rebuilt): gate neutered → caught; first-match-wins → caught; prefix compare → caught; strip disabled → caught.

### Gates

`-Werror` clean · fuzz build clean (no shim drift) · `fuzz_auto_classify` 7.2M runs clean · full runtime suite green.

author: gzak
body:
## Summary

`AxonFlowLangGraphAdapter.mcpToolInterceptor()` collapsed the MCP server name and tool name into a single `connectorType` string (`` `${request.serverName}.${request.name}` ``) before sending it to `mcpCheckInput`/`mcpCheckOutput`. Policies keyed on `connectorType` could never distinguish "which server" from "which tool" was invoked.

The platform's `MCPCheckInputRequest` schema now carries a genuine two-field (server, tool) identity — `connector_type` plus a new optional `tool` field (epic #2905 / #2904, R3-approved, CI-green, schema finalized but not yet merged to `axonflow-enterprise`).

## Changes

- `src/types/connector.ts`: added optional `tool?: string` to `MCPCheckInputOptions` and `MCPCheckOutputOptions`.
- `src/client.ts`: `mcpCheckInput`/`mcpCheckOutput` now send `tool` on the wire body when non-empty (same pattern as the existing `contentType` → `content_type` optional-field handling).
- `src/adapters/langgraph.ts`:
  - `mcpToolInterceptor()` no longer concatenates; it now sends `connectorType: request.serverName` and `tool: request.name` as two distinct values.
  - Default `connectorTypeFn` now returns just `request.serverName` (was `` `${serverName}.${name}` ``).
  - Updated `MCPInterceptorOptions.connectorTypeFn` JSDoc to describe the two-field contract.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: added a `### Fixed` entry under the current unreleased section.

### Checked but not changed

- `src/adapters/governed-tool.ts` (`GovernedTool` / `governTools`) — verified it has **no server concept**: `connectorTypeFn?: (name: string) => string` maps a flat tool name straight to `connectorType`, with nothing analogous to `serverName` to split out. Not applicable to this fix.
- No generic "tool output wrapper" (analogous to the Python SDK's `tool_output_wrapper()`) exists in this SDK — `governed-tool.ts` and `langgraph.ts` are the only two adapters that call `mcpCheckInput`/`mcpCheckOutput`.
- `axonflow-docs`' `docs/orchestration/wcp/langgraph-wrapper.md` (~line 454) only name-drops `mcp_tool_interceptor()` in passing (Python SDK naming), with no code sample showing the old concatenation pattern — spot-checked, not stale, no follow-up needed there.

## Test plan

- [x] Added/updated unit tests in `tests/langgraph-adapter.test.ts` asserting `connectorType` and `tool` are sent as two separate, non-concatenated values (including a dedicated regression test with distinct server/tool names and a custom `connectorTypeFn` override).
- [x] Added unit tests in `test/client.test.ts` for `mcpCheckInput`/`mcpCheckOutput` proving `tool` is included on the wire when provided and omitted when absent.
- [x] `npx jest` (full suite, excluding integration/e2e which require a live stack): 32 suites / 972 passed, 13 skipped (unaffected).
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean.
- [x] `npm run lint` / `npm run format:check`: clean.
- [x] `node scripts/transformer-coverage/check.js --baseline .lint_baselines/transformer_coverage.json`: 2 findings, both pre-existing/baselined — no new drift from this change.

Refs #2907, epic #2905.

author: oscharko
body:
# #2386 — Govern modes, approvals, questions, pause, and revocation for Code tasks

Closes #2386.

## What this delivers

The full #2386 authority surface over the managed OpenCode runtime, proven end to end by a real-browser Playwright journey against the production `buildUiHandlerDeps`/`createUiServer` composition:

**Contracts** (`@oscharko-dev/keiko-contracts`)

- `paused` joins the runtime state machine (sticky: adapter events never auto-resume; only explicit resume/stop or a terminal runtime outcome leave it).
- `CodeTaskExecutionV1`, `GovernedActionV1`, `RuntimeGovernancePortV1`, `RunControlSnapshotV1` with branded ids, content-free reason codes, and structurally ungrantable action kinds (delivery, authority-widening, dependency-operation, external-file-apply-back can never be covered by a reusable grant).
- Grant scopes `once` / `task`: a task grant binds command template, safe-argument classes, workspace/source digests, and policy version; any drift, expiry, or inactivity lapse forces a fresh human approval. Single-use consumption fails closed for absent/unknown scopes.
- The readiness contract's invariant is now "effectiveMode never widens past the request/ceiling clamp" (the server may confirm a narrower, run-anchored posture).
- `question` joins the observation channels and the evidence token vocabulary.

**Server** (`keiko-server/coding-runtime`)

- Question / pause / resume / follow-up routes mounted behind the existing loopback + CSRF + serverPrincipal boundary.
- Pause is load-bearing: the manager refuses approval issuance while paused, so no new mutation can be admitted without terminating the run.
- The (previously unwired) mode-change gate anchors the server-confirmed effective mode to the live run: changes are confirmed only while idle or paused, widening only from idle.
- The managed OpenCode event sink publishes a content-free `observation-streamed`/`question` signal per unique reconciled `question.asked|replied|rejected`, so pull-based clients learn when to re-list.
- Question listing is a read: it no longer consumes the one-turn-per-revision slot (coordinator returns the unadvanced snapshot; the production operation guard gains a read reserve mode) — background refreshes can never race operator mutations into revision conflicts.
- The snapshot store persists the `paused` state (its own allowlist previously rejected the legal transition as an opaque 400).

**UI** (`keiko-ui`)

- "Runtime questions" section (answer/reject, single/multi-select, custom answers; question text stays transient), pause/resume/send-follow-up composer (a drafted follow-up is admitted only while paused and never queued), supervised-coding default mode, widening-rejection surface.
- The questions hook re-lists (debounced) on runtime events and run-state transitions instead of exactly once per activation.
- `paused` joins the streamable states so Pause no longer tears down the run's event stream.

**E2E** (`tests/e2e/code-task-authority.spec.ts` + dedicated config/server entry)

- bind → reconcile → supervised start → answer the required question in the browser → contained edit + vetted verification observed → sticky pause → widening rejection anchored to the live run → follow-up admitted while paused without auto-resume → resume → stop → durable `cancelled` snapshot; plus the liveness negative on the readiness surface.

## Defects the journey surfaced (each fixed at the owning layer, failure-first)

1. Question registration produced no workbench signal — UI showed "No pending runtime questions" forever, run hung (no retry path in the empty state).
2. Question listing advanced the run revision — any background refresh raced pause/answer/follow-up into `409` conflicts.
3. Snapshot-store state allowlist lacked `paused` — legal `running→paused` threw and surfaced as an opaque 400.
4. Readiness ignored the live run — a widening mode request while a supervised run was live was silently confirmed (the mode-change gate existed but was never wired).
5. UI streamable states lacked `paused` — Pause closed the EventSource; the follow-up's `task-submitted` never reached the timeline.

## Deviations from the issue text (goal-over-process)

- The adversarial-review finding proposing a paused-only follow-up restriction was **refuted and reverted**: the one-use request id plus monotonic revision reservation already enforce no-hidden-queue (five tests prove it); the UI additionally gates drafting on paused as a UX rule.
- No `paused → cancelled` direct transition: `runtime-stopped` is only emitted post-stop(), so cancellation always passes through `stopping` — the tests encode the realistic paths.

## Verification
